the data, an error is a fact about the service, and they read completely differently to an
analyst.

0900d6a8d86d060540a9c57f.source:
Nothing here needs pagination, a cursor or a streaming transport. Narrowing is what replaces
them.

4a8aa1e858d711542766dd3d.source:
**No streaming and no server cursor.** Narrowing replaces them: rather than fetching two
thousand rows, ask what is there and let the analyst choose. The contract never requires a
streaming backend, because many sources do not have one.

1748ea11809afd29a27bb7aa.source:
**No re-parenting.** A returned node never names an existing parent. Children union by id
is the only way ingest touches an existing node's children.

3ab69e978c0c7962f0a17215.source:
**No property-edit undo.** `graph.history` covers what the canvas holds and shows — what
came in, what went out, what is hidden. A node's data is backend state the library did not
author, so reverting a field locally is `onBeforeNodeEditCommit`'s job, not ours.

1066dde3256728e2eaff2413.source:
**No transport policy.** `save` writes back, but credentials, retries, rate limiting and
conflict detection are all the consumer's. The library's only retry is the analyst pressing
**Retry**.

2e13990e4d1a402a1e5ffa59.source:
**No rejection memory across a reload.** A rejection is a verdict in one session's context,
and the same candidate may be worth a different answer in another graph. Rejections are
held for the session and no further.

355fd312bd4e74c5c2a9d284.source:
**No refresh of what is already here.** An id-matched candidate leaves the existing node
untouched; reconciling a node against a fresher copy needs a conflict policy the library
does not have.

a40389aebd219c834ccc9eae.source: How the panel draws them, and where the breakdown line comes from

89aa698bc73f8c791e84167d.source: Only while the Pivot rail mode is open.

946c3421e45820b4824a4735.source: Whatever the mode, so a badge is also a way into Pivot mode.

ba4261ffa355a6459a9f4bb0.source: One badge per pivot that declared a potential, each opening that pivot. Several of them collapse into a `+n` early on a node with children.

ebef54e076a6f1dfc1e4d444.source: **One** badge, whatever the provider count. It shows the total declared with no pivot id, or — with nothing declared — how many pivots apply.

01fa3ddc193c4e0aea0dee7a.source: What a `summary` badge does when clicked, and where its count comes from

fc2a89cda41497391a2fc72c.source:
A **plugin** is a self-contained bundle of UI elements, keybindings and lifecycle hooks
that installs itself into a graph without the core needing to know it exists. Register
one declaratively or imperatively:

b571dd7f8390a05e69472ba2.source:
A plugin installed after the graph is live is caught up to the current lifecycle phase,
so there is no "too late" — and everything it registers is torn down with the UI.

1daddfedcf48862cda374c4b.source:
Installing the same `name` twice warns and skips the duplicate, so a plugin can be
listed in `plugins` and re-applied through `graph.use` without doubling up.

58243bb6384fe22533c2f714.source:
A binding's `key` is modifiers then the key, joined by `+`: `'Shift+K'`, `'Ctrl+F'`,
`'ArrowUp'`. Write modifiers as `Ctrl`, `Meta` (Cmd on macOS), `Shift`, `Alt`, in that
order, and use **`Mod`** to match either `Ctrl` or `Meta` — which is what a shortcut meant
to work on both platforms wants. The key itself is `KeyboardEvent.key` verbatim, so it is
case-sensitive and shift changes it: the two halves of an undo pair are `'Mod+z'` and
`'Mod+Shift+Z'`. Bindings never fire while a text field has focus.

2470f96f9faab170d913b1b5.source:
Which `layout` slots exist depends on the mode: `canvas` and `notification` always,
`graphnavigation` in every mode but `static`, `mainheader` / `modal` / `slidePanel` /
`moderail` / `toolpanel` / `flyout` / `legend` in `full` and `light`, and `sidebar` in
`full` only. Read the slot at the moment you need it rather than caching it.

eb45df51686613a2fdd3ba02.source:
Extend `UIComponent` and the lifecycle is driven for you — including teardown of
anything registered through `track` / `listen` / `trackInteraction`:

99f72dc97251c9db2abe0963.source:
The four phases are `mount(slot)` → `afterMount()` → `graphReady()` → `destroy()`.
`graphReady` fires once the simulation has settled, so it can be **seconds** after
mount on a big graph — anything that should be on screen immediately belongs in
`onMount` / `onAfterMount` (deferred a frame if it needs `graph.renderer`, which is
constructed after the UI).

9432ee3a09ced31b26a000c8.source:
See the [Extend with a plugin](/examples/gallery/extend-with-a-plugin/content) gallery
card for a live, complete example.

6723486b6084d8b1697ec0dd.source:
`ctx.addDockTab` puts a pane in the [bottom dock](/ui-table#dock-tabs), beside the data
table. The dock owns the region — its height, its divider, its fold and the strip that
names the panes — and your pane owns what is in it:

c24647ad05df440410591ede.source:
**A tab is a pane, not a view of one.** If your pane has several views of its own, it
stays a single dock tab and draws its own switch in `toolbar`, calling
`handle.refresh()` to change body — which re-invokes `render`. That is exactly what the
data table does for `Nodes` / `Edges`, and why the dock's strip never flattens one
pane's views out beside another pane. Switching your own DOM behind the dock's back does
not work: it keeps the element `render` gave it, and would re-attach a stale node on the
next activation. Draw an inner switch as a segmented control, not as tabs — the outer
level already looks like tabs. `pvt-dock-views` on the strip and `pvt-dock-view` on each
button (plus `active`) are public, so it looks like the table's switch and follows the
theme without you restating either.

e0e84b1078ac42c143f2e5c2.source:
**The first pane builds the region.** Plugins install *after* the UI is built, so a tab
always arrives too late for the dock's own mode gate to have said yes on its behalf.
Registering one brings the dock into being, which means your plugin works with
`UI.table: false` and needs nothing turned on but `full` mode.

53d0ce9b47b9c89e9c1f7982.source:
**`render` is called once, lazily**, the first time the pane is opened; the element is
kept and re-attached afterwards, so it holds its own scroll position. `toolbar` is
rebuilt on every activation, so its controls can read your pane's current state.

df3d28f1e0511ae0b8291fa6.source:
**`onActivate` / `onDeactivate` are the only signal that you are off screen**, and what
to do with them depends on your pane. Content that is a function of the graph's current
state can stop working while hidden and re-derive on return — that is what the table
does. Content that would *miss* something (a pane watching a live bus — an event is gone
once it has fired) has to keep working and merely stop *painting*, flushing its backlog
when it comes back. Nothing about the hooks prefers either.

0985f8dd582fc43486907e53.source:
A tab is not a `UIComponent`, so nothing drives lifecycle phases into it. When your pane
needs `graphReady`, hold a `UIComponent`, `addElement` it, and call `addDockTab` from its
`onMount` — see [Contributing a UI element](#contributing-a-ui-element) above.

be3195a85fe4d6ec13264ba9.source:
See the [Add a dock pane](/examples/gallery/dock-panes/content) gallery card for a live,
complete example — a pane with two views of its own, beside the data table.

d86e11d4a2d8278ec51773d5.source:
The left rail's four modes — Select, Create, View, Physics — are built in. Anything else
is yours: `addRailMode` puts a mode of your own **below a divider**, after them, ordered
among its peers by `order`.

49c4547aa5a44ebe9f2ff998.source:
A **pointer mode** owns the contextual tool panel. Declare its `tools` and the panel draws
them the way Select's and Create's are drawn, with the arming, the enabled/disabled states
and the collapse handled for you:

a4d7a45331ac104c2bf2c4d5.source:
A tool's `kind` decides how it behaves. An `'action'` runs once and leaves the mode as it
was. A `'toggle'` arms a modal tool: the panel collapses, and **the rail button morphs to
that tool's own icon and label**, exactly as Select's slot becomes `Lasso`. A `'default'`
is the tool the mode rests on; name it in `defaultTool` and it is what a toggle reverts to.

139fcb10ed0a2a4d021f30ef.source:
`tools` may also be a **function**, re-read every time the panel is drawn — use that when
the rows depend on what is selected, rather than only greying out. For anything a row
cannot express, `render()` returns an element appended **below** the rows:

1b96e817cd0998698438c86d.source:
A **flyout mode** opens a settings overlay instead, like View and Physics. Subclass
`Flyout` and hand `addRailMode` a factory — core mounts the panel, opens it exactly while
your mode is active, and takes it away with the mode:

3b2593a4768ef1a174e9e868.source:
Modes are mutually exclusive, so yours excludes View and Physics for free — one store, one
active mode.

2a49f59b8298f1fdd9147630.source:
**`icon` is a raw SVG string, injected as HTML and never sanitised.** It must come from
a source you trust. CSS sizes it to 20px on the rail, 18px in the panel.

dbd60128bdcb1514e416251a.source:
**`shortcut` follows the normal keybinding rules**: claiming a key something else already
owns shadows it, with a warning, until your mode is removed.

1f5a669c2cc36790657462a1.source:
**`onExit` is where you disarm.** It runs when the mode is left, and when it is removed
while active — in which case the rail falls back to Select. It does *not* run on UI
teardown; the disposers your plugin already tracks cover that.

a489da808f6434de9f3d99fe.source:
`addRailMode` returns a disposer, and works in every mode — the button is only drawn where
there is a rail, which means `full` and `light`.

0254b868d8c8411b2d0bad38.source:
Anything that navigates the graph — a minimap, an overview, a "jump to" control — uses
two renderer methods:

162733eafe1b9a2b4f9b2a0e.source:
`setViewport` leaves the scale alone unless you pass one, so it is the primitive for
panning. To read where the view currently *is*, invert the canvas corners rather than
reaching for a zoom transform — this is renderer-agnostic:

5d890390aa64e3feb61cd332.source:
`fitAndCenter()` (fit everything), `zoomIn()` / `zoomOut()` and
`focusElement(nodeOrEdge)` remain the shortcuts for the common cases.

f6c7f1b955494c2e62a4b213.source:
A first-party plugin: a cached overview of the whole graph docked in a canvas corner,
with a rectangle showing what is on screen. **Click** it to recentre the view;
**drag** the rectangle to pan. A very small toggle in the corner it faces folds it away
to just that button, and brings it back.

e09e6a57b4f60c7334bfff09.source:
**`full` mode mounts one for you** — it is part of that mode's chrome, like the header,
the sidebar and the mode rail. Every other mode leaves it to you:

14c80a4d8fb2403c799c78af.source:
`UI.minimap` takes the same {@link MinimapOptions} the plugin does, so
`{ minimap: { position: 'top-left' } }` configures the one full mode brings along.
`UI.minimap: false` suppresses it. Passing your own `minimap()` in `plugins` also wins —
full mode stands aside rather than mounting a second one — so an existing
`plugins: [minimap({ … })]` keeps working exactly as it did.

5f88a1fb747fabac92f432c2.source:
Nothing else is configurable, because nothing else needs to be: the level of detail and
the redraw cadence adapt to the graph.

682e8c6ccc2ddc3bfe16fcc9.source:
Nodes are dots in the colour the renderer gave them, edges are hairlines under them, and
notes — the only content with a size of its own — are drawn to scale as translucent
blocks in their own colour, over the nodes as they are on the canvas. Hidden and
filtered-out content is left out. Past a few thousand nodes the picture becomes a density
map instead (one stamp per node, no edges), which reads better than tens of thousands of
overlapping dots; notes are drawn either way. It is all cached and only re-rasterised when
the picture really changed — a node dropped, a note moved, the layout settling, a filter
applied — so panning and zooming stay free however big the graph is.

9c3accf4432422d16934d29b.source:
An HTML card (`html` on `shape: 'none'`) has no colour the minimap can read, so its dot
takes the colour of the smallest drawing that is a shape: the base style, or else the
first such tier in `tiers`. With none, or with a `transparent` colour, the dot is drawn in
the minimap's own ink (`--pvt-minimap-ink`). Dots are sized to what the node covers, so a
card or a `renderNode` node gets a card-sized dot rather than one sized by `size`.

0da17c4dd09dd380fd29fb28.source:
A minimap you asked for stays where you put it. The one `full` mode mounts on your behalf
was not asked for, so it opens `collapsed: 'auto'` and takes the canvas into account: it
stays open while the canvas is at least **four minimaps wide and tall**, and folds itself
away to the toggle below that. It keeps following the canvas from then on — folding away
when the sidebar opens over it or the window narrows, coming back when the room does.

45949066dc5c022f62ec6725.source:
The moment anyone folds it away or brings it back — by the toggle, or through
`setCollapsed()` — that stops: an explicit choice sticks, and no later resize overrides
it. Pass an explicit `collapsed: true` / `false` to opt out of `'auto'` from the start.

4d09b175297c99b76544320c.source:
The toggle's arrow points at the corner the minimap docks in — the direction it folds
away — and flips once it is collapsed. Folded away it draws nothing at all, not even the
rectangle, so it costs nothing while it is out of the way; opening it re-rasterises for
whatever the canvas looks like by then. `setCollapsed(boolean)` and `isCollapsed()` on the
`Minimap` instance drive the same thing from code.

30f82e8dc27bfca88159e533.source: What it draws, and what it costs

9504a465ce7a52811d1d48fc.source:
The minimap maps the **content bounds together with the current viewport**, so the
rectangle is always visible and honestly sized — zoom far out and the graph shrinks
inside the frame rather than the rectangle sliding off it.

4950a1eb4eeee674c1d31438.source:
It keeps the graph in an offscreen bitmap and only re-rasterises it when the picture
actually changed: on a data change, when a filter hides or restores nodes, when a node is
dropped after a drag, on every 10th simulation tick while a layout settles, and on resize.
**Panning and zooming redraw one image and one rectangle**, so navigating costs the same
whether the graph has 20 nodes or 50,000.

6de27a379c8cf88957069836.source: Detail degrades with size, on purpose:

5d36867b0f9e4b547e33d7e1.source:
It works in `full`, `light` and `viewer` modes, and `full` is the one that mounts it
without being asked. In `static` — which promises no interactions — it is not mounted, and
installing it there warns.

46922c02607d8e6e2f670e92.source: See the [Minimap](/examples/gallery/minimap/content) gallery card for a live one.

82e6a5e66f8f7455a32b35ab.source: the live `Graph` — nodes, edges, the data event bus, `queryEngine`

4f3d8e65d42beeb3ced1fb00.source: the `UIManager` — options, notifications, the mode store

712d4ed7d279d5c6f85ad9dd.source: the DOM scaffold, read **live** (never a snapshot). `layout.canvas` is where canvas-docked chrome goes

7d1524fc133b950e06dcab77.source: put a `UIComponent` into the lifecycle, mounted into `slot`

b49e0f869a85550146fa23b0.source: sidebar panels — the same door as `UI.extraPanels`

5af554af4c14ae2fd4ec10f9.source: a pane in the bottom dock — the same door the built-in table comes through

b14fdd2ab4e7f7b29f0dc9c0.source: a mode on the left rail, beside Select / Create / View / Physics

f3a50a49b0fe76a83daaea4e.source: a pill in the top bar — the same door as [`UI.topBar.actions`](/ui#topbar-actions)

91b18050d5a83a3ecaa7aa58.source: a shortcut that is removed when the UI is torn down

4cffb789a2e4846bbdb161b8.source: the keybinding registry, for anything more involved

5cedcb022e295f0c2c49fc21.source: Which corner it docks in. `'bottom-right'` is the only corner the built-in chrome leaves free in `full` mode.

0e08d1cdb2dca451dc5eaa16.source: Width in CSS pixels, border included.

c6e0b21b72ab0565c926f8bf.source: Height in CSS pixels. Omitted, it follows the canvas's aspect ratio (clamped to 70–400px) so the rectangle keeps the shape of the real viewport.

118b65320cda76059af91a6f.source: `false`, or `'auto'` for the one `full` mode mounts

64f3de859a42d8c75c1d8b71.source: Which state it opens in. The toggle is always there; this is only where it starts. See [Getting out of the way](#minimap-auto) for `'auto'`.

d018b121d8c26cae69140779.source: a dot per node in the colour the renderer resolved, plus hairline edges (dropped past 4000 edges)

16adf910ba3d092888e8f553.source: one stamp per node in a single ink, alpha accumulating — dense regions read as a density map, and no per-node style is resolved at all

3a187e337f08a0fcd941f14b.source: Represents an edge (connection) between two nodes in a graph.

98a2f36e8f52cefb6ff8ef2f.source: True for a stand-in: a line drawn for real edges whose ends are hidden in closed clusters.

2a61bf423ed301ff49c649f6.source: Optional data payload for the edge

5c6daa39181ea4de4cbe1f75.source: Get the edge's label style if available.

4c50c4a8ce63763369daa328.source:
The sources vouching for this edge — pivot ids, plus `'seed'` for data that was
here to begin with. Which pivot asserted a relationship is the load-bearing half
of provenance, so edges carry it exactly as nodes do.

48a0281cde5c7c6f30e8bfd7.source: Whether `source` vouches for this edge. `'seed'` is true for un-pivoted data.

b2a37d78c117a0163a805e1f.source:
Switch this edge's layer on or off, re-deriving [visible](#visible) from the other
reasons it may already be hidden for. Returns whether anything changed.

d1b7f040907396621f2823fa.source: Convert edge to a simple JSON object representation.

d314af1015a797656b172fb3.source:
Structured-cloneable payload for the simulation worker; endpoints reduced to ids, keeps
`directed`. The style is stripped of functions — see [Node.toSimulationDTO](Node.md#tosimulationdto).

0da371d18e0e7b2763de2b25.source: Merge partial data into the current edge data.

6d65176573f89b73ac7f11c1.source:
Merge partial style into the current edge style.
Useful for updating only parts of the style.

efcf1c97479d2b2d5f410f20.source:
Whether this edge's layer is switched on. A veto over [visible](#visible): every
other reason an edge is hidden (endpoints filtered out, a collapsed cluster,
a manual hide) is asserted through [show](#show) / [hide](#hide), and `show`
cannot bring an edge back while its layer is off.

620b567b705ecda4e82ffda5.source:
For a stand-in: the real edges it speaks for. Edges landing on the same pair of dots
share one line, so one stand-in can cover several relations of several kinds; it is
filtered out only once every one of them is. Undefined on a real edge.

f62adb636258df46e39f7b82.source:
What [visible](#visible) would be if every layer were on — i.e. visibility from
the endpoint, collapse and manual reasons alone. The simulation gates on this
rather than on `visible`, so switching a layer off never changes the layout.

d98514503ec02bd67267253c.source:
Shared scaffolding for the settings flyouts — the overlays opened by the
mode rail's flyout modes: ViewFlyout (grid + canvas behaviour) and
PhysicsFlyout (layout + simulation). The base owns the panel element,
the shared `pvt-flyout-*` chrome (header, section labels, switch rows) and the
binding to [ModeStore](../interfaces/ModeStore.md) — a panel is `open` exactly while its own mode is
the active one, so the flyouts exclude each other for free.

f5149a8c1f2e09f0f6f21725.source:
A subclass declares the mode it answers to, renders its controls in
template and wires them in wire. The template's words are text:
the helpers below escape what they are given, and elements marked with
`i18nText` / `i18nAttr` are filled from the graph's catalogue. A subclass overriding
`onGraphReady` must call `super.onGraphReady()`: that's where switch rows get
their initial state (`graph.simulation` only exists by then).

72f79d3a778e220121708109.source:
The rail mode this panel answers to. Public so the rail-mode registry can check a
registered flyout against the id its definition declared.

9d050663fe9873c263c27fac.source: Represents a single node (vertex) in a graph.

ebf48aed64f3cfe21714f73e.source:
True for a group drawn by `graph.simplify`: a stand-in for its members, never part
of the data.

31f3c4ef8ecec96f108a9280.source: Optional data payload associated with the node

8fc8a0587f72db78da9276ed.source: The node's clusters, outermost first — empty for a node of the root graph.

baa1d2f05d3e0e9e509af686.source:
The node the canvas actually draws for this one: itself when every cluster above it
is expanded, otherwise the outermost collapsed cluster — the box hiding it — and in
either case the closed group that dot is folded into, if any.

91361342b645fc17e41f5c99.source:
This answers "which dot on screen stands for this node", not "is it visible": an
expanded cluster renders a *separate* subgraph built from `toDict()` data, so a
nested node is never drawn by this graph even when its cluster is open.

01e05981905f544b3c2deec0.source: Every node below this one, depth first.

fbb0b0c832ccf3140b686d70.source:
The node's rectangular border grown by `outset`, or `undefined` when the
node is anchored as a circle.

a35a8c96b331adb136ec29c0.source:
Distance from the node's centre to its border along the unit direction
`(dirX, dirY)`, grown by `outset` — where an edge leaving in that direction
should start. Rectangular for a measured node, the circle radius otherwise.
Deliberately free of style resolution: this runs for both ends of every
edge on every tick.

bbd2a958df078a3651928f4b.source:
The radius the layout spaces this node by: its declared footprint where it has one,
and otherwise whatever the drawing measured. Every force reads this; the drawers read
[getCircleRadius](#getcircleradius), which is the drawn size.

57afcab32ab1181bc1adc089.source: The declared footprint half-width, or `undefined` when the drawing owns the spacing.

5f63e295ac9845b4b31aa4cc.source:
The potential declared for one pivot, or — with no argument — the total declared
for no particular pivot. `undefined` when none was.

806529649440366470def04b.source: Every declared potential on this node, keyed by pivot id.

5c80425e4d7ef8f5203fcd00.source:
The sources vouching for this node — pivot ids, plus `'seed'` for data that
was here to begin with. A node can be vouched for by several pivots at once,
and `graph.removeBySource` deletes it only when the last one goes.

0cd5960aaab01c8cbb91eff4.source: Whether `source` vouches for this node. `'seed'` is true for un-pivoted data.

ef2a9c81ef23260b4bd02152.source:
Drop one child, and its own subtree with it. Returns the removed child so the
caller can clean up after its descendants.

11f14a2b66a6cdb293800af6.source:
Declare that the node's border is the centred `width`×`height` rectangle it
actually renders as, so edges stop on it instead of on the bounding circle.
Call it *after* [setCircleRadius](#setcircleradius), which clears it.

423ed0f0f94b910c49894c4b.source:
Set the node's circle radius. Also drops any measured rectangular border:
the radius is the coarser fact, so every caller that resizes a node keeps
anchoring correct by default, and only the drawers that know the rendered
shape opt back in through [setBorderBox](#setborderbox).

96792328a8b3428d4568ec8b.source:
Declare the box this node reserves in the layout, as a half-width in graph units.
Unlike [setCircleRadius](#setcircleradius) this is constant: the drawing can change inside it
without anything moving.

463c2d3f00d697dfd336ead4.source:
Declare how much more there is for this node, without asking for any of it —
what the rim badge shows. `0` clears the declaration.

878c9c1a02c1968f60de8c10.source:
With a pivot id it is that pivot's number, and its badge opens that pivot. With
a count alone it is the total across everything, which is the number the
`'summary'` rim badge prefers — the one to declare when there are more providers
than a rim could ever name.

3d6bc3e22dbf14286eda2d1c.source:
Marks the node dirty like every other setter here, so the badge appears on the
next render — call `graph.renderer.update()` if nothing else is about to.

bb04446a94be9f6e171cab8f.source: Convert node to a simple JSON object representation.

9bb218e73909b86544b00066.source:
Structured-cloneable payload for the simulation worker (no live parent/children/_subgraph
refs, unlike `clone()`). The style is stripped of functions: every resolvable channel may
hold one, and no force reads them, so sending them only risks a `DataCloneError`.

2531913c2fdd67dfccbf1a3f.source:
Merge `children` in by id: new ones are added, matching ones are left
untouched — their own children merged in turn — and none are ever removed. The
union is how a pivot re-discovering a container adds what it found without
disturbing what is already there.

34fe2bdc390cbfca1e78edeb.source:
every node newly added, at any depth, so the caller can register and
tag them.

639d5164b376683043cd3bbe.source:
Merge partial data into the current node data.
Useful for updating only parts of the data.

32d05019c3b90e93121e0038.source: True if this node is a child within a collapsed cluster

bd2e0c7b82468c58819aa70c.source: True if this node has child nodes

5d7c4afdab073623dcc25a76.source: Reference to the parent cluster node (if this node is a child)

fda5423dafc729547da10b60.source:
The plain options that rebuild this note: `new Note(note.toJSON())` or
`graph.addNote(note.toJSON())` on another graph. Visibility is left out, as
hiding notes is a view state rather than part of the note.

b61d1eb711c1a9df06880005.source: Initializes a graph inside the specified container using the provided data and options.

fbc70dbaf3a640da24ac0717.source: The HTMLElement that will serve as the main container for the graph.

ec98fd97f1616357a11b214f.source: The graph data, including nodes and edges, to render.

0aa0732ba5e96b5286625d08.source: Optional configuration for the graph's behavior, UI, styling, simulation, etc.

6a0be1b7ec735a8662e251e3.source: Adds an edge to the graph.

bc6b365698ee1674fbfa26a9.source:
Both the source (`from`) and target (`to`) nodes must already exist in the graph.
Throws an error if an edge with the same ID already exists.

20f1cfd8ae034d1457c780b6.source:
Error if the edge ID already exists or if either node does not exist.
Triggers `onChange` after the edge is successfully added.

eeebddbcc76317335b296556.source: Adds a node to the graph.

f34a5f5f206d9498db289ab9.source:
Error if a node with the same `id` already exists.
Triggers `onChange` after the node is successfully added.

8dbb7d028519900abcf72182.source:
Adds a note to the graph and draws it. Takes the same options as `data.notes`
(what [Note.toJSON](Note.md#tojson) returns), or a `Note`. Emits `noteAdd`.

716d718ad7115de0ca5650b1.source: Error if a note with the same `id` already exists.

2230529843836c46e098ece5.source:
Adds nodes to the current selection, leaving what is already selected in place.
Already-selected nodes are ignored.

441c132d3f9d54d32ab169da.source:
Nodes only: the interaction layer has no additive setter for edges, which can only
be selected as a whole set via [selectElements](#selectelements).

09a6f178a3dfe0481af7eb57.source: End the emphasis [emphasiseElements](#emphasiseelements) started: the canvas reads normally again.

4c7ca8cac10e0e1224ba40d0.source: Remove any highligh class from any nodes or edges

42fef46a6ea49c51012591a9.source:
Repaint after an edge-layer change. Deliberately not onChange: layers
don't touch the link force (see `Simulation.getActiveEdges`), so restarting the
simulation would move the graph for no reason.

e2dbec4f4e27cd043884da5a.source:
Pick a **set** of elements out of the graph: they keep the look they already have
while everything else on the canvas dims, until [clearEmphasis](#clearemphasis). This is
how hovering a legend entry reads its category off the canvas.

fe0a0c898159da7d061f1b20.source:
Where [highlightElement](#highlightelement) points at one element, this describes a group.
Elements that aren't drawn right now are skipped, and an empty set dims nothing.

a0e53422456b8125d6625fa8.source:
Brings the specified node or edge into focus within the graph view. A node hidden in
a closed cluster or group brings that cluster or group into focus.

72cb9a4376b78ba0a500f449.source: Retrieves all nodes directly connected from the given node.

4f33a5bb7b283840a3c0f370.source: Returns cloned nodes to prevent external modifications.

72dee460fe8a4f32accd1d88.source: The node or node ID to find connections from.

fed5e4fd3046ceefd2966d2c.source: An array of `Node` objects directly connected from the given node.

94ad3babd70a76fc8b0976e1.source: Retrieves an edge from the graph by its ID.

f0896102d9d5d588db702679.source: Returns a deep clone of the edge to prevent external mutations.

a7e6cf79c46d20e9741e7f9b.source: Returns the number of edges currently in the graph.

e7e4be248873866828912523.source: Retrieves all edges in the graph.

74ae020a98f456ecdc6832ef.source: Returns clones of the edges to prevent external modifications.

455886a1ed756ac95f889f4e.source: Finds all edges originating from a given node.

9b4bdb839711e5032697a7e8.source: Returns cloned edges to prevent external modifications.

88d5098b6c240ff6af66ea22.source: The node or node ID to find outgoing edges from.

7760a5bd63737365c95cd139.source: An array of `Edge` objects whose `from` node matches the query.

7f360643680770c719d48a7e.source: Finds all edges pointing to a given node.

301479a8de720bf013c3a8b8.source: The node or node ID to find incoming edges to.

df93dcdf4c1df2e1bafcc920.source: An array of `Edge` objects whose `to` node matches the query.

efac9b02742c0f83e2361679.source: Returns the actual edge instance, allowing direct modifications.

5a6fd930a158fb19f640f78a.source:
**Warning:** Directly modifying edges using this method may lead to unexpected behavior.
It is generally safer to use `getEdge` which returns a cloned instance.

0cfa790c1d3043694063eeaa.source: Returns the actual edge instances, allowing direct modifications.

df74417491967daf476200a1.source:
⚠️ **Warning:** Modifying edges directly may lead to unexpected behavior.
Use [getEdges](#getedges) instead to work with safe clones.

ed8683ce1c7ec67bca2baa15.source: Retrieves a node from the graph by its ID.

f9727c23feaa25eeed134c98.source: Returns the actual node instance, allowing direct modifications.

c9ae0b214fc05bedbb378f3a.source:
**Warning:** Directly modifying nodes using this method may lead to unexpected behavior.
It is generally safer to use `getNode` which returns a cloned instance.

6b8bce030dbfa49f9063d68d.source: The ID of the node or a Node object.

fd2644235b4299f4bb4e6aec.source: Retrieves all nodes in the graph.

12010607edd193ba96a7d5e8.source: Returns the actual node instances, allowing direct modifications.

f3902915ab70821c61e7015a.source:
⚠️ **Warning:** Modifying nodes directly may lead to unexpected behavior.
It is generally safer to use `getNodes`, which returns cloned instances.

bed322de8689e09376549ae6.source: Retrieves all visible edges in the graph.

2686e29175e04e03dc641f34.source: Retrieves all visible nodes in the graph. Recursively adding visible children

70c2e52a4d0fd92ab8bfe053.source: Returns a deep clone of the node to prevent external mutations.

ac289678f4df0040d85af362.source: Returns the number of nodes currently in the graph.

af172f0559f2d732340117f6.source: Returns clones of the nodes to prevent external modifications.

6e44d22d14b6b972eeaa37e2.source: Returns the current configuration options of the graph.

b36bb579e6431e2db2119d8c.source: Add a highligh class to the given node or edge

52869102c6ba562334cde9a8.source: Trigger the next render update of the graph.

8fb8f677df669d0d3ee3b5c5.source: Trigger the next render update of the graph for the passed subjects.

99d7997c99d920c2edffe60d.source:
The dock can hold panes other than the table now, so this also brings the table's
pane to the front: the call is named for the table and should show you one. Reach
for `UIManager.dock` or `activateDockTab()` to drive the region without that.

f49d299070a24563c711151a.source:
Remove everything a source vouches for. An element several sources vouch for
survives, one claim lighter — the same uniform rule pivot undo follows, and the
only way anything a pivot brought is removed.

e75e7ce3235bf1035db51bf3.source:
It is a forward operation, and one entry in [history](#history): undoing it puts back
what left and hands the source's claim back to what stayed.

2ec6ddc4336019cd01b6a5e3.source: A pivot id, or `'seed'` for data that was never pivoted.

54a1211181362da54d6d3181.source: Removes an edge from the graph by its ID.

2c4a2a7fa0687de92419a2f0.source:
The ID of the edge to remove.
Triggers `onChange` after the edge is removed.

4537a3c6d61ce86b20d86aae.source:
Removes nodes from the current selection, leaving the rest of it in place.
Nodes only, on the same terms as [addToSelection](#addtoselection).

0c67367c9977040c348f0bdb.source: Removes a node from the graph by its ID.

a91e853df70cbba9ed899dd0.source: Also removes any edges connected to the node.

aeed171d96723413fd28afe9.source:
The ID of the node to remove.
Triggers `onChange` after the node and its edges are removed.

d8f7a77b67a7cd0e9d2e1df3.source:
Selects a given node or edge in the graph. A node hidden in a closed cluster or group
is still the one selected; the canvas lights the cluster or group drawn for it.

0c4bf6ff70d7dd69653987be.source:
Selects several nodes, or several edges, replacing the current selection — the
plural [selectElement](#selectelement), resolving each element's rendered handle for you.

69a88994715ec99ccaa1ef08.source:
Nodes and edges cannot be selected together (the interaction layer clears one kind
when the other is set), so a mixed array selects the **nodes** and warns.

1f9703fe86bd505b20824497.source: The `Node`s or `Edge`s to select. An empty array clears the selection.

a56d41cb5de574c411a01d72.source:
Replaces all current nodes and edges in the graph with the provided data.
Clears existing nodes and edges before setting the new ones.
Triggers the `onChange` callback after the update.

804dd8125f175613a4e5f7d8.source: Array of nodes to set. Defaults to an empty array.

4a9bad0d37842a328e4acf2b.source: Array of edges to set. Defaults to an empty array.

1750d28e0f3334ae62cbcb95.source:
Replace the canvas legend at runtime — the imperative twin of `UI.legend`.
A graph that started without one gets it built on the spot; `false` empties
the legend and drops its filter, and `true` / `undefined` fall back to
deriving one from `render.nodeTypeAccessor`. Pass a
[LegendGroupOptions](../pivotick/namespaces/GraphUI/interfaces/LegendGroupOptions.md) to key the graph on several dimensions at once.

03e8428f82691938523267df.source: The legend to show, or `false` to remove it.

e944e8cad14c5551ea5c338b.source:
Replaces the graph's notes, leaving nodes and edges alone. Notes are matched by
id: one already on the canvas is updated in place, so its drawing stays bound
to it, one not in `notes` is removed, and a new one is added.

680ea7dcdfbdfb82dec2e395.source: the notes now on the graph, in the order given.

8327a23d7900c1e0bc747d19.source: Error if two entries share an id. Nothing is changed then.

d4a3d0de5323d72bcc121751.source:
Returns whether anything moved, so an edge-only filter change can repaint itself.
`notify` is off for the query engine's first pass, which runs before anything is
drawn — the constructor's own `simulation.update()` / `renderer.init()` follow it.

c3fa455a64ff29c48b10623a.source:
Paint what an action *would* do, and change nothing else: the elements it would
take away drain in place, the ones it would hide with them, and whatever it
would bring back is outlined where it would land.

5a4b8be82be45e765a1ee0d6.source:
Where [emphasiseElements](#emphasiseelements) reads a set out of the canvas by receding the
rest, a forecast answers "what happens if I click" — so the graph has to keep
reading normally around the few elements that would change.
`graph.history.preview(...)` returns one ready-made.

5da16ca842550ada4a2ef67a.source: Opens the data dock if it is closed, closes it if it is open.

aa3229ae1e6df60232fc32a2.source: Remove a highligh class to the given node or edge

c57409a53db6d1f1f8a52e23.source: Updates the graph with new nodes and/or edges.

1cc7a0cdfa803bb1b7dda892.source:
An id the graph already holds is updated **in place**: what the element *is* —
its data, style and weight — becomes what you handed over, while the object
itself keeps its identity. It has to work that way. Its edges, the simulation
and the DOM binding all hold that object, and so does everything it has learned
since it was built: which sources vouch for it, where it sits, whether it is
pinned. A position on the incoming element still wins, so `updateData` can move
something as well as refresh it. Unknown ids are added.

74b3267a37e7256436abaf4c.source:
A container's `children` are not restructured here — pass the container through
[removeNode](#removenode) and [addNode](#addnode) to change what it holds.

598130583807ccd867fb78cf.source:
The whole call is one batch: one `dataBatchChanged` listing every add and change in
the order given, then one re-render, however many elements it carries.

b7f5b4bb75690bff67eabda7.source: Optional array of nodes to update or add.

5d1b3ebff50d7dac222fd012.source: Optional array of edges to update or add.

72edce8f42a4313cf163e07d.source: Announce the in-place changes. Adds are announced either way.

90cc0ca5d13e4b2fe6630399.source:
Install a [PivotickPlugin](../interfaces/PivotickPlugin.md). Can be called at any time — the plugin's
UI elements are caught up to the current lifecycle phase. Returns `this`
for chaining.

60c81f3fe95bc777ffc84026.source:
What the canvas holds and shows, and how it came to: every ingest, deletion,
durable hide and hand-drawn element, contiguously reversible. Bounded and
session-scoped — it does not survive a reload.

248a67163a263bec6a7f3de8.source:
The language this graph writes its own text in, from `GraphOptions.i18n`: message
lookup, plurals, and number, list and sort formats. A nested graph shares its
parent's.

ed39f87944cce1b615dbef2c.source:
The pivot runtime: register enrichments, run them, triage what they return,
and undo a whole run. Lives on `Graph` rather than the UI because pivots
produce *data* — and because it has to exist before the UI is built.

6b25c5df479c772cc35fbeef.source:
Folds nodes that play the same role into one group drawn in their place. The groups
are view state: `getNodes()`, `getEdges()`, the table and the history see the members.

075d04aaed529c016c4c687b.source: Base class for every UI element. It provides:

dee00c71eec9cf4fb7a92f69.source:
**A composite tree.** A component owns `children`; three of the four
lifecycle phases (`afterMount` / `graphReady` / `destroy`) recurse into
them automatically. `mount` is the exception — it needs a per-child slot,
so `addChild` mounts each child explicitly instead. A parent declares its
children via `addChild` and their lifecycle is driven for it.

e4487f1612bd671bd9076d7d.source:
**A disposable registry.** Anything registered via `track` / `listen`
(event unsubscribes, DOM listeners, timers) is torn down on
[destroy](#destroy).

228bc501934e81ea3f27b636.source:
Subclasses override the `on*` hooks rather than the lifecycle methods
themselves, so the recursion and teardown always run.

ec794b87931df294328a7f80.source:
The minimap plugin: a cached overview of the whole graph docked in a canvas corner,
with a rectangle showing what is on screen. Click it to recentre the view; drag it to
pan.

e94ee45b83f5cb0cd608eada.source:
Built entirely on public API (`renderer.getContentBounds` / `setViewport` /
`screenToGraphCoordinates`), so it is exactly as privileged as a plugin you write
yourself — and it is renderer-agnostic.

4a3b5831c7cfcaffa85c651d.source: An edge a forecast outlines, as the two points it would run between.

f6f2e9ead0cd303543c1c569.source:
One element a forecast has to *outline* because it is not on the canvas: where it
would land, and how big it would be.

6d6d0226de4c3f43a17ea9bf.source: The radius it was last drawn at, so the outline is the size of what returns.

7d4db0101b2334ffba2e390d.source: What an action would do to the canvas, ready to paint.

84e0c69a5066318bbd27564d.source:
A forecast leaves the graph exactly as it is — nothing dims, nothing moves — and
marks only what the action would change: what would go, what would be hidden, and
an outline of what would come back. That is the difference between a forecast and
[GraphRenderer.emphasiseElements](GraphRenderer.md#emphasiseelements), which reads a set *out* of the canvas by
receding everything else.

5db66d27c5c81ec41aa3c631.source:
GraphHistoryLike.preview hands one over ready-made, which is how hovering
a history row shows what the click would do.

3f1e1d0808725019b075cc8b.source: Not on the canvas at all — drawn as an outline where it would land.

3c178905bdede9e352dd481a.source: Staying in the graph, but about to be hidden.

b51f99785703fd6e3921e13f.source: On their way out: still in place, drained.

a0cc136a7b32d9c15453fd73.source: Touched by the action and staying: ringed, otherwise left alone.

d324266229178fe02ebdbb5a.source: A bounded, session-scoped history of what the canvas holds and shows.

f80752f1846f31798a84f248.source:
It is one timeline with a line drawn through it: everything above the line has
happened, everything below has been undone and can be redone. Undo walks the line
down through a contiguous span, redo walks it back up, and any new action strands
whatever was below it. Nothing here reverses a single old entry on its own — that
is `graph.removeBySource`, which is a forward operation and says so.

af0495b10b08326c04924e8d.source: Forget everything. The canvas is left exactly as it is.

ab09ed961039eb7ba9401433.source: What has been done and can be undone, newest first — the order the menu renders.

f0d3f73e48d78636e6adac9d.source: Subscribe to every change to the history — a new entry, a span travelled, a clear.

5b61e6f28f6c97be784f1da2.source:
What that span would do, played against a copy of the graph rather than summed
from the entries — so a hide cancelled by a later unhide nets to zero, and a
node a second run also vouches for is not counted as leaving.

83270c37f6e2b5429f4656a2.source:
Re-land the span from the line back through `throughEntryId` — the nearest
undone entry by default. Exactly as it was: no provider call, no re-gating, no
second trip through a hook.

17435783db075cb2b9e2dd72.source: what was actually re-applied, newest first.

515affc1eba7b204206279e0.source: What has been undone and can be redone, newest first. Emptied by any new action.

8f388f10f2d427b7835fde4c.source:
Undo the span from the newest entry through `throughEntryId` — the newest entry
alone by default. A sealed entry inside the span is passed over rather than
walled off: the entries around it are named element by element, so skipping one
cannot put the rest out of order.

6f6227a66b3ec39b0896ddd4.source: The whole span lands as one `dataBatchChanged`, and one re-render.

18abcad83e92f9dfda5acd4c.source: what was actually reversed, newest first.

b5a330431d5fc627906cc035.source:
Release renderer-owned resources (observers, listeners) on teardown.
No-op by default; renderers that hold such resources override this.

27ed562a17adede3b589e3b3.source:
Fit-and-centre once the content has stopped resizing. Renderers that lay
out over several frames after the sim stops (e.g. expanded clusters)
override this to wait for a stable bbox; the default fits immediately.
Resolves once the fit is applied.

e8a8528420f0effbca16162f.source:
The style `node` draws with. With `tier`, the style of that one drawing instead of the
one the zoom picks: `-1` for the floor style, or an index into the node's `tiers`.

adbf7868a5aca6a91eb09ed3.source:
The graph's root container — everything, chrome included. Deliberately distinct
from [getCanvas](#getcanvas): the canvas shrinks whenever chrome opens (a sidebar, the
data dock), the container only changes when the page around it does. Anything
that must not react to chrome measures this instead.

4bd9f7f76187fa7e63b5086a.source: Graph-space point where the preview edge ends, or `null` while none is drawn.

93959572be3bee676926ea90.source:
The language one graph writes its own text in: message lookup and plurals, and the
number, list and sort formats that go with them. Each graph has its own, read from
`GraphOptions.i18n`; a nested graph shares its parent's.

d0a9528bf9a2ed644324f36d.source: A collator for the locale, so "Émile" sorts beside "Emma" and "item 10" after "item 9".

faf8ccf286ddb4468abfb6fe.source: Compares two strings for a sort in the locale's order; safe to pass to `sort` as is.

15eb3fff2b7b4e21626f1aa2.source: Items joined as a sentence: "a, b and c" in English, "a, b et c" in French.

f513a2c1a0844f1fbecab3e5.source: A number written the way the locale writes it: `1,234` in English, `1.234` in German.

7017a57db25cd597149c2785.source:
The text of `key` with its `{placeholders}` filled from `params`. A plural message
picks its form from `params.count`.

cf31c8787b2548a8c9c32648.source: The BCP 47 tag in use: the host's, or `'en'`.

8d93160336926833f52bd272.source:
`minimap(options)` — how the minimap is placed and sized. Everything else about it
(level of detail, when it redraws) adapts to the graph and needs no configuration.

2f81f06b28f7a1e9f0100994.source:
Which state the minimap opens in. The toggle is always there — this only decides
where it starts.

945c9e2ee62e8a34d762fcff.source:
`'auto'` keeps it open unless the canvas is too small to give a 200px overlay away,
and follows the canvas from then on: collapsing when the room goes (the sidebar
opening, the window shrinking) and coming back when it returns. The first manual
toggle — or any `setCollapsed` call — ends that and the choice sticks.

aa70eda53e0d4366eee09bb4.source: false — but `'auto'` for the minimap `full` mode mounts for you

7ecffd58497de97030530941.source:
Height in CSS pixels. Left out, it follows the canvas's aspect ratio (clamped to
70–400px) so the viewport rectangle keeps the shape of the real viewport.

bf0fb5033e4047aa109ba23b.source:
The corner it docks in. `'bottom-right'` is the only corner the built-in chrome
leaves free in `full` mode.

afb490ff412f7f4acda48364.source: Observable state of the mode rail.

f4a08ce38d024f1cae4ccb18.source:
The armed tool per pointer-mode (`'pointer'`/`null` = the mode default), keyed by
mode id. The rail slot reflects this: a non-default modal tool morphs the slot's
icon + label. Reset to the mode default when its mode is left.

ebf93e6b33b9cb8bbb83d886.source: The active rail mode. Defaults to `'select'`.

7351302a15a7b85cb3aed81d.source:
Whether each pointer-mode's contextual tool panel is expanded, keyed by mode id.
Remembered per mode (persists across mode switches); the armed tool does not.

e8272c90c224ebc425c94ca7.source:
A tiny observable holding the mode-rail state. The rail, contextual tool panel
and the settings flyouts subscribe to it; clicks / keybindings dispatch to it.
Setters are idempotent — they only notify when the value actually changes — and
every notification carries a fresh snapshot so a listener can't mutate the
store's internal state.

6841a550a32fa4ec218c66d9.source:
The four built-in modes are always present. Modes registered through `addRailMode`
are added with [registerMode](#registermode) and hold state exactly like a built-in does.

f0e4d71959e3594809c8ab72.source:
`subscribe` fires on *changes only*; render initial state from
[getState](#getstate) first, then subscribe for updates.

6e1fc6b36e0637b169938dbf.source: Arm a tool in a pointer-mode (the rail slot reflects it). Idempotent.

73ab018bc254e266859409b2.source: Drop every subscriber (called on UI teardown).

59fbe3bd498fa49f99a6dffc.source: The armed tool for a pointer-mode (`'pointer'`/`null` = default).

b95975be0001afae064a02f8.source: The tool a mode rests on when nothing special is armed.

e5cb9f8927617a627a4793b9.source: A copy of the current state (safe to read; mutations don't leak back).

622af277625a8c4f23ff817c.source: Whether a mode is currently registered (the four built-ins always are).

41a7368dedc11d270d384fac.source: Whether a flyout is open (i.e. its mode is the active one).

9142ef8b67b2f0e713ab0476.source: Whether a pointer-mode's tool panel is currently expanded.

f02073f33e728ae56a3283ee.source: Whether a mode owns the tool panel. Unknown modes are not pointer-modes.

b138f0c494be516f6ae9dec9.source: use `isFlyoutActive('view')` — the rail has more than one flyout now.

4bea5505173bb218b533e7d3.source:
Add a mode's state to the store. Called by the rail-mode registry; the four
built-ins are already present. Re-registering an id overwrites its record but keeps
whatever tool/panel state it already had.

806d2bc4a736c58ae862fcf2.source: Expand / collapse a pointer-mode's tool panel. Idempotent.

ca81bf3b53a7b8b810b44289.source: Subscribe to state changes. Returns an unsubscribe fn (pass to `UIComponent.track`).

78eeba4ae2eb62f257693a05.source: Open a flyout mode, or close it back to the last pointer-mode.

1a67e55e8b67086dd4f0ae07.source: Toggle a pointer-mode's tool panel open/closed.

211c2cf5720a65d13dac605a.source: use `toggleFlyout('view')` — the rail has more than one flyout now.

d717bd3a0fc50d5e9c6e40a6.source:
Drop a mode's state. The caller is responsible for moving off it first — the store
will not decide what to activate instead.

c73b0172699018eb2620aad5.source: Half-extents of a node's rectangular border, measured from its centre.

12ffe6c1532feb8b922cdb5e.source: Manages and displays notification messages in the graph UI.

442b45b458b538f24ac35558.source:
Use this component to show success, warning, error, or info messages
to the user.

b0a47f287deec9da9be8b17b.source:
A notification can also carry one action and outlive the default four seconds,
which is how an outcome offers to undo itself:

5e5632cd81f7efbae42e6620.source: Dispatch a notification to the UIManager.

5804774eb3a7f87509f20e1c.source: The severity level of the notification.

c1ede18333a5f3e19998ceab.source: The title to display in the notification.

ee3d163c7a16fc69bf6b2d95.source: Optional detailed message for the notification.

3e879eaf6fda1027afef87bd.source: An action to offer, and how long to stay.

16574db5cb85a59177135a4c.source:
A handle onto the toast, or `undefined` where there is nowhere to
show one (a UI mode with no notification slot).

4b59841595a70ae6a54264fa.source:
The abstract physics knobs surfaced by the Physics flyout. Each is a plain number in
its own [range](../variables/PHYSICS_KNOB_RANGES.md); the [Simulation](Simulation.md) setters map them
onto the underlying d3-force domains. Also the complete vocabulary the `Auto` preset
speaks — auto only ever moves a knob the user can see.

b4354111441e3ea789b52292.source:
Pull toward the canvas centre. Higher keeps separate components — which
otherwise only ever repel — inside the frame.

2510f3e1beb60ef128c2b900.source: Node spacing (collision radius). Higher keeps nodes further apart.

bc055a50e2bcbe3ea12b33b6.source: Motion damping. Higher settles the layout faster (calmer).

622efc7f8d74fbcb04af3262.source: Push-apart force. Higher spreads the graph out.

20b196075fcc3250abf400e0.source: How long the layout is given to settle, in seconds.

84b913c6ec2b0c6eecc69ca0.source:
A Pivotick plugin: a self-contained bundle of UI elements, keybindings and
lifecycle hooks that installs itself into a graph without the core needing
to know it exists.

8da9f3d030b784561712ba04.source:
Register one either declaratively via `GraphOptions.plugins`, or imperatively
via [Graph.use](../classes/Pivotick.md#use):

49e5cda3bc9a73fac5c89ebe.source: Called once when the plugin is installed.

4043678b760fb4e436ed5f4a.source: Stable identifier, used for logging and de-duplication.

07a9356175d35181fac8900e.source:
The pivot runtime: the registry, the two provider calls with their cancellation
and cache, the narrowing gate, the candidate sets awaiting triage, and ingest
with its provenance. Taking a run back is `graph.history`'s job, alongside every
other thing the analyst can reverse.

4cd4f032df24d7b9198b9098.source:
It holds no UI. Everything here is drivable from the console — a pivot with
`autoIngest: true` is end to end without a single pane — and the triage pane and
the Pivot rail mode are readers of this state, not owners of it.

c127f4a8a693e96563829427.source:
What the library draws on a node's rim for its pivots: one badge per pivot that
declared a potential, one badge for all of them, or nothing. Set it through
`pivotRimBadge` in the graph options, or here to change it later.

e9fe8a8a5e0d8cfe2990b7cc.source:
Assigning marks every node dirty, the way `setPotential` does for one — the rim
redraws on the next render, so call `graph.renderer.update()` if nothing else is
about to.

e606815c56eb30aa440358f5.source: What the library draws on a node's rim for its pivots.

e8be9c9284ef7ffd2de36d9e.source: Whether the rim badges are drawn right now.

98a710312fc9d17ecf0f4709.source:
When the rim badges of [rimBadge](#rimbadge) are drawn: only while Pivot mode is open,
always, or never. Set it through `pivotRimBadgeVisible` in the graph options, or
here to change it later.

c025d56f27b5d8a8646f9ac8.source: Like [rimBadge](#rimbadge), assigning marks every node dirty.

9434180c8d58c826fb61196a.source: When those rim badges are drawn.

17f83c7ad389ba75a93b4d41.source:
Whether the Pivot panel and the triage pane offer their own *N unsaved · Save*.
Off, a consumer writes back only through [save](#save), which, like the ledger and
[unsavedCount](#unsavedcount), works either way. Set it through `pivotSaveControls` in the
graph options, or here to change it later.

57255bdf554120a67995e2bd.source: Whether the Pivot panel and the triage pane offer their own Save.

5549f5fe7c1dfd0b50c8d318.source: How many pivots are registered — what the Pivot rail mode's gating reads.

ad560e28b64a3a0ed77c05f6.source: Every registered pivot, in registration order.

97f9cd8d5e121960f997daa8.source:
How many pivots apply to one node — what the `'summary'` rim badge counts when
nothing was declared for it.

fe929f8ff5d81b256e483626.source:
Memoised, because the rim asks this for every node on every render and the
answer is one `appliesTo` call per registered pivot: at a hundred providers and
a thousand nodes, asking each time is a hundred thousand calls a frame. The memo
is dropped whenever the registry or the graph's nodes change, so a predicate
reading anything *else* can go stale — acceptable for a hint on the rim, and the
panel is always the exact answer.

d4ee230ecdfc2cd2fbb46485.source:
The cached summary for exactly this question, if there is one. Lets a surface
paint a number it already knows without asking again.

010d2c7abd02085f77f9d055.source:
Abort in-flight provider calls: one pivot's or every pivot's, and optionally only
one kind.

10eea23412bbcfd18730346f.source:
The `kind` is what lets leaving a surface stop the questions it was asking without
cancelling the work it commissioned — a `fetch` already has a candidate set of its
own and a pane showing it, so abandoning that silently would throw away results
nobody asked to lose.

34e4f10bbaf857a6aaa349c3.source: Cancel a fetch in flight. The candidate set goes with it; nothing is staged.

6ad7711a2d5db3f3140a94de.source: The candidates staged for one pivot, if any.

4fd3909538837c57399a2b79.source: The id the source system assigned this element, when it assigned one.

5d2e9ddcc5c6a0466f897395.source:
Drop a staged set without rejecting anything. Closing a pane is not a verdict:
whatever was never rejected is offered again on the next run.

70b10e6d992095e234653be4.source:
Drop a waiting re-run and carry on with what is on show. Nothing is rejected:
the next run offers those candidates again.

009c6231184b6a485c2a6d77.source:
What applies to this origin. An empty origin yields the origin-less pivots —
search, import, staging — and nothing else, because a selection-driven pivot
with no selection has nothing to run on.

96e2e08448d1ac0e081e507d.source:
A pivot that applies to only *part* of the origin is in: a selection mixing a
domain and an IP offers the domain-only providers too, and each is run against
the nodes it kept.

c5bdc58546189711ef48c74e.source: Commit the marked candidates of one staged set.

b534f32290421753737b6d0f.source:
Purely additive: an id already on canvas is skipped, never overwritten, and
removal only ever happens through `graph.history` or `graph.removeBySource`.
The whole batch goes through `onBeforeIngest` once, and lands as one
`dataBatchChanged`.

c61da85e0546e49331c964f5.source:
`group` folds the landing into groups, one per type (`graph.simplify.groupLanding`),
and defaults to [ingestGrouped](#ingestgrouped).

708dbdd9b70b441b22509001.source:
Drop cached summaries: all of them, one pivot's, or only those asked about
particular nodes. The library caches because a multi-selection summary is an
aggregate nothing can decompose, but only the consumer knows when their backend
changed.

22b2a1d655d1d20a94951871.source: Whether this element came from a run whose pivot declares a `save`.

97996f3a0dd60df7160b5767.source:
Written to the source system. `false` both for an element still waiting and for
one whose pivot can never write it anywhere — [isSavable](#issavable) is the question
that tells those two apart.

2a76b4d1e1b5c3f1913cc828.source:
Mark or unmark a candidate for ingest. Deliberately silent: with hundreds of
rows, re-rendering the pane on every tick loses the analyst's place, so the
caller updates the row it just changed.

7c70b9d713f5cc5ac20d7b9b.source: Mark every landable candidate — what "select all" resolves to.

a2bc8bed9b1ae2a7ee06b6ec.source:
Subscribe to pivot state changes — the registry, a summary, the staged
candidates, the run stack. Returns a disposer.

2f6a825eb44814fcd9833ce1.source:
How much of `nodes` one pivot applies to. Empty when it does not apply, and
empty for an origin-less pivot, which is asked about nothing by definition.

38458ec4be39c85e424e93cf.source:
Register a pivot. Returns a disposer; calling it twice is a no-op. A duplicate
id is skipped with a warning, as everywhere else in the library.

82c308b96c170ed981824e92.source:
Reject candidates explicitly. Remembered for the session, keyed per pivot: a
candidate rejected under one pivot is still offered by another, which asks about
it in a different analytic context.

93b40b04bd8ab7f8c7002963.source: How many candidates have been rejected for this pivot this session.

e94db36f0b48ef44856be9a8.source: The rejected candidate ids for this pivot — what the pane reveals on demand.

81182a8b706f50cc8ad0ae71.source:
The rejections themselves, rows and all, newest last. What a surface listing them
shows: an id names nothing once the run that carried it is gone.

9173097456adae6c6d4da8c3.source:
Reject everything still untriaged in this set — how triaging 1,800 down to 12
and dismissing the rest stays one gesture.

2f4a80c9bebfa17e61d852eb.source:
Run a pivot: gate the advertised count against its cap, fetch, then either land
the results (`autoIngest`) or stage them for triage.

cfb90365a6cef8ab3ca6f5c9.source:
Resolves at the hand-off — a staged run does not wait on the analyst. The
outcome's `runId` is the id the resulting ingest is recorded under, so it is
the handle for `graph.history.undo`.

df8b096ec3547ad84a8ee3f0.source:
Write ingested runs back out to the systems their pivots speak to: one run, or
every savable run with something still unsaved.

91d968223a0d41133d914765.source:
The library contributes the bookkeeping, not the transport — which elements a
run created, which of them have been written, and what a retry should carry.
The write itself is [PivotDefinition.save](../pivotick/namespaces/Pivot/interfaces/PivotDefinition.md#save)'s, and a pivot that declares
none is skipped entirely rather than counted as failing.

86954909a3fd297ef42d00d4.source:
Runs go one at a time: a backend being written to is not helped by six parallel
batches, and a sequential pass makes the report exact.

42e2eba967c3b835371cd6e2.source:
A run id for one run, a pivot id for every unsaved run of that
pivot, `{ elements }` for just those, or nothing for all of them.

046b5a2f640d4a4e85493b52.source: `interactive: true` when an analyst asked for it, so a save can prompt.

65015597a8e8b28329cb10d5.source:
Promote a waiting re-run: its candidates become the set on show, and the marks
on the one it replaces go with it. A no-op while the re-run is still fetching —
swapping in a set with nothing in it yet would be the silent discard this whole
mechanism exists to avoid.

de8636658092674e758e7bb5.source: Every staged candidate set — one per pivot that has been run and not yet cleared.

994b582a964b6a8951074eda.source:
Ask a pivot what is out there. Serves a cached answer without touching the
provider, and supersedes any summarize already in flight for the same pivot.

53e9618843b2926af8ba2b00.source:
Resolves `undefined` when the call was superseded or cancelled — nothing to
render, and never an error. A provider that throws rejects, so a surface can
show the failure and offer a retry.

93a9cdd687245b072336174c.source: Unregister a pivot, dropping its cached summaries and its staged candidates.

59451350c3d6395c13bab897.source:
Take a rejection back. Reaches the session memory whether or not the candidate is
still staged — a rejection from an earlier run suppresses the row rather than
showing it, and taking it back is the only way that row is ever offered again.

a49385c1dd65400f18937015.source:
Take every rejection this pivot holds back. The way out of a `Reject all
remaining` that went too far, which one-by-one restoring is not.

ad8f9da38df0c5253259823d.source: Savable runs with elements still on canvas and not yet written.

e16a9c4cda5d4e25c2207c61.source: What a Save would send — across every savable run, or one pivot's.

e14e2406d888c38c8da72bfa.source:
Absolute ceiling on what one `fetch` may stage. A provider that returns more is
**refused** — nothing is staged, nothing is truncated, and the analyst is told
the number. It is about memory for candidate objects, not the table, which
virtualises. Override it through `pivotCandidateCeiling` in the graph options.

080bb0d7d5ad84f8578e70c6.source:
Whether an ingest lands folded into groups, one per type, when its caller does not
say. Set it through `pivotIngestGrouped` in the graph options, or here to change it
later. Does nothing while the graph does not simplify.

efb7e0804e34f146fe610cfb.source:
Whether a node a run created and has not written back carries a
`pvt-node-unsaved` class. Set it through `pivotMarkUnsaved` in the graph
options, or here to change it later.

5270ed6f91a145a6d5cde3e7.source:
How many new candidates a one-click pivot lands without triage. The number is
about the canvas rather than the clicking: undo takes an ingest back but not the
layout the simulation made around it, so the limit is roughly what a graph can
absorb and still be the graph the analyst was reading. Override it through
`pivotQuickIngestLimit` in the graph options.

5f399ab8fa97500e9337adb8.source:
The capabilities handed to a plugin's [PivotickPlugin.install](PivotickPlugin.md#install). Anything
registered here is driven by the same lifecycle as the built-in UI and torn
down with it.

515abe147cb84c9419c95a3a.source:
Register a pane in the bottom dock — the same door as `UIManager.addDockTab`,
and the one the built-in table comes through. Returns a disposer.

055baaf63076b07dc04a222c.source:
The first tab **builds the region**, so a plugin does not have to ask the
consumer to turn the dock on: `full` mode is the only requirement.

457bc7bcf9193124fe9a9fa1.source:
Add a UI element into the lifecycle. When `slot` is given the element is
mounted into it immediately; it then participates in every subsequent
phase (afterMount / graphReady / destroy). Safe to call after the graph
is already live — the element is caught up to the current phase.

8d05e4f778d98de463731d40.source: Register a keybinding that is automatically removed when the UI is torn down.

5a891e19ced27c1203359951.source:
Register a sidebar panel — the same door as `UI.extraPanels` and
`UIManager.addPanel`. Returns a disposer; the panel is re-rendered on every
selection change and torn down with the UI.

181de1fd6037e86db31f31c6.source:
Register a pivot — the same door as `graph.pivots.register` and the `pivots`
option, and the way a plugin ships an enrichment. Returns a disposer.

0bea54d5b28fcb6918ce01fe.source:
The Pivot rail mode appears as soon as the first pivot is registered and goes
when the last one leaves, so a plugin does not have to ask the consumer to turn
anything on.

0ca6fc9541ceb144d1e316b8.source:
Register a mode on the mode rail — the same door as `UIManager.addRailMode`, and
the way a plugin ships its own Explore or Enrich mode. Returns a disposer.

27924d493bb9916444a08a36.source:
Registered modes render below a divider, after the four built-in modes. Registration
succeeds in every mode; the button is only drawn where there is a rail
(`full` and `light`).

480a328402e0825de718d50c.source:
Add a pill to the top bar — the same door as `UIManager.addTopBarAction` and
`UI.topBar.actions`. Returns a disposer. `ui.refreshTopBar()` re-reads its fields.

e46fbd2e97c641b9b304f281.source: Hook a lifecycle phase. Returns an unsubscribe function.

72a71e16792338de7125edab.source:
Rebuild a dock tab from its `render` and `toolbar` — for when the pane's own data
or chosen view changed. The same thing a `DockTabHandle`'s `refresh()` does, for
code that holds the id rather than the handle.

8c106531112fe98b238a6ecc.source: Re-render one sidebar panel, or all of them when `id` is omitted.

c167f75cbcf04b0c3d3d4dcc.source: Remove a dock tab by id (equivalent to calling its disposer).

691f901c6e7e2109687ca48f.source: Remove a sidebar panel by id (equivalent to calling its disposer).

4a36ffaf385cde1ee7e243fb.source: Remove a rail mode by id (equivalent to calling its disposer).

a996d0a78b87555c88e7a4be.source: Remove a top-bar action by id (equivalent to calling its disposer).

127de51d5cac470257eba2e2.source:
Rename a dock tab in the strip, leaving its body and its scroll position alone —
a live count, without re-registering the tab.

cec7e8540c00cd725402dfed.source:
The graph's language: its locale, the number, list and sort formats, and `t` over
the library's own messages. Text the plugin writes itself is the plugin's to
translate, keyed on `i18n.locale`.

d9df00e51fc0dc5cd3927c06.source:
The root DOM scaffold, read live from the UI (never a stale snapshot). It
exists in every mode while the UI is alive and is `undefined` only after
the UI is destroyed. Its *slots* are what vary by mode: `canvas` and
`notification` always; `graphnavigation` in every mode except `static`;
`mainheader` / `modal` / `slidePanel` / `moderail` / `toolpanel` / `flyout` /
`legend` in `full` and `light`; `sidebar` in `full` only.

f10404b165bf2996b8ee6f92.source: `canvas` is the slot a canvas-docked element wants — see the minimap plugin.

dd82830892e314b8acd3792c.source: What the matches set were matched on.

db62a49170decd3e23d82f57.source: The members above which Open asks first (`UI.simplify.openConfirmAbove`).

6ee00f88b5b22505af3004ef.source: Fold an open group's members back into it.

7d2c0b819e122ebcf0fa2603.source: The colour a dot is drawn in: `UI.simplify.colorOf`, else a node's style, or a group's own.

804a73d376f20ced7c717115.source: The label these nodes would get from their types, what the title prompt starts from.

6b06a6c0c97fda0d157b79ce.source:
Every group from the last run, open ones included, and those a later rule folded
again: the group holding one lists its members too. `summary().groups` counts the
closed groups the canvas draws.

9fc41134280a3539cdf9f589.source: The hand-made groups, for a host to save.

c3b68daeedaa955291eb46b4.source: Every rule, in run order, with what it did on the last run.

f299e3e20a96461a26b3d9fa.source: The real nodes a selection stands for that a hand-made group may hold.

1bc99c53eb4b019893cbd236.source:
Land what this pivot run adds in groups, one per type. Call it with
`graph.pivots.candidates(pivotId).runId` before `pivots.ingest`, so the nodes are
never drawn loose; calling it after folds them on the next redraw. Adds the Pivot
landings rule at the top when it is not declared, and switches it on.

8627a6e0f93e1e5a1513a26e.source:
Fold these nodes into one group of their own, titled `title` (unset or the default
label: labelled by its types). A group among them gives its members. A node already
in a hand-made group leaves it; annotated nodes and expanded clusters stay out.
Returns the new group's id, or nothing when fewer than two nodes can be grouped.

3844ac2649d07d51930f95e2.source: The group the first rule to fold this node put it in.

48b0cae0bd00e6982bb2e9f7.source: Whether the feature is on at all (`UI.simplify.enabled`).

b139d8cdc1b9f629220af95b.source: Whether this pivot run was asked to land in a group.

dc05d7a32c06c81719a26a27.source: Whether this group was made by hand.

298abd9de69be36b32cab75d.source: Whether a node was pulled out of its group.

ad5ad79b2d888e8da82a721f.source: A group's label: its title, else its parts joined, largest first.

47e9786dd32b5d3f1b142789.source: How many of a group's members are among the matches set.

8425d031cad9912eb2311577.source: Subscribe to changes of the grouping. Returns its own unsubscribe.

686024302f6bb13e8af9c994.source: Put a group's members back on the canvas. It stays open until closed or dissolved.

509f6e92eadba226a6c144d7.source:
Take nodes out of their groups for the session; each stays a plain node until put
back. Several at once regroup once.

babd87588bd76bfe8fff059a.source: Let pulled-out nodes be grouped again.

34e27b2ec7891c5ec2bddc81.source: Retitle a hand-made group; an empty title labels it by its types again.

7d9acfc1ebd960b394ab85e4.source: The name a rule goes by on its card, for a group's subtitle.

7a7640fb2c78967b19d0912d.source: Replace the hand-made groups, as a host restoring them does. Not an undo step.

b5d6eeaebac0bb30654086f3.source:
Mark a search's matches: a closed group holding some draws their share over its ring,
and its tooltip counts them. An empty list clears them.

dfde0220a86929f172afbc41.source: Switch one rule on or off. Switching a failed rule back on tries it again.

96b3d80c67ece06c91b4c509.source: Set a rule's smallest group, clamped to 2–50. A rule with another setting has none.

3a2db1dc8a6df76ebe17bfee.source: Replace the rules. Their order is the order they run in.

9363599e79fd7a6c783cdff3.source:
Set a rule's one setting, what its stepper or slider does: the smallest group (2–50),
the fewest links or core strength (1–10), or the Communities level (1–7).

d2457bc6b110fbb769974d05.source:
What the canvas holds: `total` top-level nodes pass the filters, `folded` of them sit
in closed groups, and `shown` dots are drawn for them, `groups` of which are groups.

086a8abd4b3421b581c93a66.source: The colour a member of this type is drawn in; `''` is no type.

c2f66b8dbad32735478237eb.source: The name of one part of a group, `12 × ip` unless `UI.simplify.typeLabel` says otherwise.

da8e87daa788310dd261f9a0.source: A group's parts joined, largest first, whatever its title.

f25ea420c7c12cb4cbc0a354.source: Remove hand-made groups, as one step; their members are drawn as they would be without them.

49e4dc8b3a96e28d86f83c27.source: Let what this run added be drawn as plain nodes again.

5d583f4866a8495789039b3b.source:
Apply a named preset ([PHYSICS\_PRESETS](../variables/PHYSICS_PRESETS.md)): sets every knob and reheats once, at
CLICK\_REHEAT\_ALPHA rather than the slider default — a preset describes a whole
layout, and reaching it from a settled graph takes a fresh layout's worth of travel.

92d64bc1d777803a0c00aab1.source: Allows to change the layout of the graph

6dbecd0d7f37b30455f82d02.source: Stop the engine and release the container observer.

868cdd88f9882fbb8a5ca6eb.source: Turn `Auto` off, leaving the knobs wherever they currently sit.

0c8b29ebdb75c1327692763f.source:
Turn `Auto` on and tune immediately. `force` because this is the Auto *button*: an
answer inside the deadband would otherwise make the click do nothing visible.

1140199020159fc0c3606605.source:
Hand the tree spacing back to the tuner, which re-derives both multipliers from the
node sizes and tree shape and keeps doing so as the graph changes. The counterpart of
[setTreeSpacing](#settreespacing). No-op under the force layout, where `Auto` is
[enableAutoPhysics](#enableautophysics).

b642f3e78159838215317b31.source:
Which side of its node a node's floated label goes on, when the layout chose one —
only the `structured` layout does.

536e1c807a588687377793f5.source: The active layout type — the Physics flyout greys out physics under non-`force` layouts.

5906a1d826c9e8405e188a14.source: Current knob values, for seeding the Physics-flyout sliders.

2cdc2261709706227c31a7fe.source:
Where the active tree hangs from. Under the force layout there is no tree, so this
reports the finder a tree would start with and no pin.

ce8f1e42ba1319e4cf11cd12.source: The active tree layout's spacing multipliers; `1×` under the force layout.

94fa73ea573bb696a063e2a6.source: Is the `Auto` preset currently driving the knobs?

dde29c9784de26989f5153cf.source: Is the tree spacing tuning itself? `false` under the force layout.

4ad30743328c798eee754433.source:
Re-read the node-dependent force accessors and reheat. d3-force caches per-node
radius/strength when a force is initialised, not per tick, so a radius mutated mid-run
has no effect until the nodes are re-set. For a custom node that measures itself after
the opening layout has cooled. No-op when disabled.

5f2d519643aef06a8424f262.source: Restart the simulation with a bit of heat

4d61457f3e09b18c35ebceb9.source: Restart the simulation with rendering on each animation frame.

f3fe9aec2a07da64de65d7ad.source:
Pull toward the canvas centre. Knob 0–100 → d3GravityStrengthConnected, with
d3GravityStrength (isolated nodes) following as a fixed multiple. Separate components
only repel each other, so this is the only thing keeping them in frame.

2775e90eff214cd107ac40aa.source: Node spacing. Knob 4–60 → d3CollideRadiusMultiplier (scales each node's collision radius).

bf3aa71ec55e1470761da95e.source: Motion damping. Knob 0–100 → d3VelocityDecay (÷100). Applied live each tick — no reheat.

9e65a48626c5518d8f696c9e.source:
How long the layout is given to settle, in seconds. Knob 0.5–8 → d3AlphaDecay
*and* cooldownTime together: alpha decay sets how fast the sim cools, cooldown
is the wall-clock wall that stops it. Moving either alone does nothing — raise
the cooldown and the sim is already cold; slow the decay and the wall truncates it.

2b1d02b2c5b4e08619694e59.source:
Re-hang the tree from another root: `{ rootId }` pins it to that node, `{ algorithm }`
drops the pin and lets the finder choose. No-op under the force layout, which has no
hierarchy to root.

7c668f7eb6a7dfd8fee9602e.source:
A pinned root is walked ignoring edge direction, so any node — a leaf included — gives
a whole tree rather than a stump beside the old one. See TreeLayout.setRoot.

68fc87d0771b1f1d36b9b1fd.source:
Re-lay-out the tree at new spacing multipliers ([TREE\_SPACING\_RANGE](../variables/TREE_SPACING_RANGE.md)). No-op
under the force layout, where spacing is the physics knobs' job.

c9508248e03ec937cfc7235d.source:
A redraw *and* a reheat: the pinned axis moves immediately, so the change shows even
with physics paused, while the free axis still settles into its new sibling slots.

4c871f6db04df8b51777648f.source:
Snap a graph-space coordinate to the grid when grid-snapping is enabled
(a no-op otherwise). Public so non-simulation draggables (e.g. notes) can
snap on the same grid as nodes.

4f881a237500dabbc38368fe.source: Start the simulation with rendering on each animation frame.

90f50203473c129a5a365488.source: Manually stop the simulation and cancel animation frame.

8291835da8ac439e7a42ab7f.source:
Returns a promise that resolves when the simulation stops naturally.
Useful for performing actions (like fitAndCenter) after stabilization.

4bbdfbd92c02595f839875de.source:
Where a tree layout hangs from, as the Physics flyout's Root card offers it: a node
the tree is pinned to, or — with nothing pinned — the finder that picks one.

5ce8d218f761c4e8fc3c35c7.source: The two are exclusive: pinning a node retires the finder until the pin is dropped.

405a76b5513792d5afd4d8d1.source: The finder that chooses the root while nothing is pinned.

04e3f3d43844c5befb4689e7.source: The node the tree is pinned to; `undefined` while the finder decides.

339173eed6a43448597e459f.source:
The tree-spacing multipliers surfaced by the Physics flyout — the one thing left to
turn once the physics knobs grey out under a `tree` / `egoTree` layout.

95ff4025ad650eaee68c1fac.source:
Multipliers rather than pixel gaps because a tree is laid out to *fit* the canvas:
"half again as far apart as the fitted layout" survives a resize; a pixel gap does not.

b34e739385a3dd7667c95c58.source: Distance between levels — rings, in `radial` mode.

e6440c870f88276f9d4d39a0.source: Distance between nodes within a level. Ignored in `radial` mode, where a level always spans the full circle.

c56fea177bd791d278c24943.source:
Where to point the view. `x` / `y` is the graph-space point to put in the middle
of the canvas.

9887c3354c882a4488e8e10f.source: Animate the move rather than jumping.

2ed8b53c93e5d322db56b23d.source:
What the library shows while a content hook's promise is in flight, and what
it shows if that promise rejects. Both are optional — the built-in skeleton
and error affordance follow the active theme.

9b35c9f7a404faecc22cfa2d.source:
Synchronous hooks never see either of these: they commit in the same frame,
exactly as they always did.

9c637a496ed4c2158d15f0bc.source:
Shown in the slot when an async hook rejects. An aborted render is not a
failure and never reaches this.

63fab933588c0387eaca72cd.source: Shown in the slot while an async hook is pending.

cfe86d0863db5885a6d15707.source:
Passed as the **last** argument to every async-capable content hook, so a
consumer can abandon work the UI no longer needs.

3e776b69a290af7fac351e6b.source:
Existing synchronous hooks simply ignore it — a one-argument callback stays
assignable, and nothing about its timing changes.

6d96c74e21cabf20fc8dba10.source:
`true` once this render has been superseded. A cheap guard for consumers
doing non-abortable work, so they can bail out between steps without
touching [RenderContext.signal](#signal).

742db1d6ea8b8f692f89b1b4.source:
Aborted when this render is superseded — the tooltip hid or reopened for
another element, the selection changed, the panel was refreshed or
removed, the graph was destroyed. Forward it to `fetch` and in-flight
requests are cancelled instead of leaked.

f414da23951f517f8fd30471.source:
