The UI surfaces that can render consumer-supplied content asynchronously.
Handed to [AsyncContentOptions.placeholder](../interfaces/AsyncContentOptions.md#placeholder) / `.error` so one factory
can serve every surface and still tell them apart.

71948df6cfbff2949aaf6bfa.source:
A [RenderResult](RenderResult.md) for a hook that replaces a default drawing (the properties
panel, the main header): `undefined`, or a promise of it, draws that default instead.

15cb7fa8cb2ae770ea7d2949.source:
Content a consumer hook may return. A `string` renders as plain **text**;
return an `HTMLElement` to render your own markup.

3e59e829ad579e563cf4e8b3.source: What a content hook may return: the content itself, or a promise of it.

8587e0372860e04984b84655.source:
When a hook returns a promise the library mounts a placeholder in its slot,
swaps in the resolved content, and drops the result if the slot has since
gone away (the tooltip moved to another node, the selection changed, the
panel was torn down). See [RenderContext](../interfaces/RenderContext.md) for cancelling the work that
produced it.

a92b84197624e8490fe3e831.source: `null` renders nothing: the slot stays empty.

3654bdcc5f92866ae0744869.source:
A rim badge was clicked. Specific before general: the badge's own `onClick` runs first,
then the graph-wide `onBadgeClick`. Neither can suppress the other — a bus listener
calling `cancel()` is the one way to stop both.

676798660af954141d00c447.source: Expand or collapse the selected clusters, and open or close the selected groups.

a5979de70da466e74e434b00.source:
A rim badge was clicked. Fires before the badge's own `onClick` and before
InterractionCallbacks.onBadgeClick; `context.cancel()` suppresses both.
`element` is the node's group, as for every other node event.

de926720abeb03f4d78576b9.source: This interface should be used as the entry point when configuring the graph.

1a549cbbcfc0d431b84f5826.source: Callbacks to handle various graph events and render hooks.

ce1f896969992f0b0c83dd47.source:
The language of the text the library writes itself: menus, panels, toasts,
tooltips. See [I18nOptions](../../I18nOptions/interfaces/I18nOptions.md).

535170cbdaa6c945c69a62f8.source: Enable whether the graph is directed or not

b712e00eb0859f75f0fe1ad5.source:
Absolute ceiling on how many candidates one pivot `fetch` may stage. A provider
that returns more is refused, not truncated.

ac86ccc9c9f51fd92417b359.source:
Every pivot landing arrives folded into landing groups, one per type
(`graph.simplify.groupLanding`): a one-click run, an `autoIngest` pivot, and
Review's main buttons. Review then offers *Ingest loose* for a landing drawn as
separate nodes. Ignored while `UI.simplify` is off.

bdb4e230b9c399eec6b7cbf7.source:
Put a `pvt-node-unsaved` class on every node a pivot run created and has not
written back yet, so a stylesheet can mark them.

95a678ddc76e13ff70a945ba.source:
A class rather than a badge: the rim rations four corners and only two on the
container nodes an enrichment produces, and a marker that pushes a declared
potential off the rim costs more than it says. Off by default — the count in
the Pivot panel is the surface that always tells the truth about this.

aae654d1902c713b898cef7b.source:
How many candidates a one-click pivot may land on the canvas without offering
triage first — a context-menu pivot row, or a rim badge with a single pivot to
offer. Only candidates that are *new* count: what dedup will skip does not, and
an edge between two nodes already on screen does.

5a8873bb7561c340710a944c.source:
It decides nothing for a pivot that declared [PivotDefinition.autoIngest](../../Pivot/interfaces/PivotDefinition.md#autoingest)
either way, and nothing at all for a run started from the Pivot panel — going
there to read the counts is never answered by having the results land instead.

e0e4896d3a04866b0da3864e.source: `0` sends every one-click run with something new in it to triage.

d1b298b60211b544dca82048.source: What the library puts on a node's rim for its pivots.

6b1d7bccad406509f2b86282.source:
`'per-pivot'` — one badge per pivot that declared a potential for this node,
each opening that pivot. What a handful of providers wants.

a416ae9c7fcce43c0b6d2549.source:
`'summary'` — **one** badge for all of them, whatever the provider count. It
shows the total declared through [Node.setPotential](../../../../classes/Node.md#setpotential) with no pivot id,
or, failing that, how many pivots apply to the node. Clicking it opens the
Pivot panel on that node — unless exactly one pivot applies and it has nothing
to narrow, which runs straight away.

134d5edd335a5338f20ad8a6.source:
A node has four rim corners and only two once it has children, so `'per-pivot'`
stops being readable somewhere around a dozen providers. `'summary'` is the
answer at a hundred.

469e86f71c45e9c38b1f2c47.source:
`'pivot-mode'` — only while the Pivot rail mode is open, where they help pick
an origin. Clicking one there scopes the panel to that node and pivot.

70b56c25493696e3980342b6.source: `'always'` — whatever the mode, so a badge is also a way into Pivot mode.

c697a5884b50c4c0e8cea8a3.source: `'never'` — not at all. The same as `pivotRimBadge: 'off'`.

e66416b84ffd151cd38a181d.source:
Pivots to register before anything is built, so the UI's first paint already
knows whether there are any. See [Graph.pivots](../../../../classes/Pivotick.md#pivots) for the imperative door
and [PluginContext.addPivot](../../../../interfaces/PluginContext.md#addpivot) for the plugin one.

2e3eb1791c11b292eabca844.source:
Whether the Pivot panel and the triage pane show what is unsaved with a Save that
writes all of it. Off, the consumer offers saving where it wants, through
`graph.pivots.save(...)`; the ledger and the save itself are unchanged.

263d1b539d92e9809735e726.source:
Plugins to install after the UI is built. Each is handed a
[PluginContext](../../../../interfaces/PluginContext.md) and can add UI elements, keybindings and lifecycle
hooks. See [Graph.use](../../../../classes/Pivotick.md#use) for imperative registration.

38fa5b84f092a0c0773440b2.source: A legend entry was toggled: which categories are now hidden / shown.

7a8c923f66a5038ab4d68ebe.source: A note changed: its content, colour, visibility — or, on drop / resize, its geometry.

887760c4c1a18000a4fe364e.source: The first layout has settled and the opening fit is under way; a view set now stays.

f8a404ba87f56ca777e8830b.source:
A node as plain data — what a consumer hands the graph and what a pivot returns.
`expanded` defaults to `false`, so a flat result carries no boilerplate.

84fcab41ad39f094b26ab46b.source: `UI.busyIndicator`: the cue shown while an async hook is in flight.

d9527447615cafaefc0652c5.source:
It sits at the end of the preview edge for `onBeforeEdgeCreate`, at the drop point
for `onBeforeNodeCreate`, and at the bottom-centre of the canvas otherwise. While it
shows, the graph's root carries `data-pvt-busy`.

500375a6bbcd2eb0196b9e5f.source:
Milliseconds to wait before showing anything, so a fast hook never flickers.
Applies again each time a prompt the hook opened closes.

920b8e39df751c9553d509f5.source:
Announced to assistive technology, and shown beside the spinner at the
bottom-centre.

075123c6d6cc270d4e292af2.source:
The menu over a node that is part of a multi-selection. Its entries receive the
selected nodes, as a `Node[]`, in both `visible` and `onclick`.

3a85f102ffb272481d4687a6.source: `UI.dock` — the bottom dock's own settings: the region, not its occupants.

b27f90f42ef4c1c61efc1e5b.source:
Everything about *what is in* the dock is declared elsewhere — the table under
`UI.table`, anything else through `addDockTab()`. What is left here is the region
the occupants share, which is why there is exactly one of each setting however
many tabs are registered.

0fbe9075df55fd2fe4094f1c.source:
Folded away to just its header bar. `'auto'` follows the room available, until
the first explicit collapse or expand hands control to the user for good.

f13a8936388065e389fa31eb.source: Expanded height: a pixel count, or a fraction of the canvas between 0 and 1.

4be9329acce6bd15515b89f1.source:
Whether the region is present, and expanded when it is. Three states, because
the collapsed bar is the control that opens it:

c059bec5dc0b042bf9ad06bc.source: `false` — not present at all. `Shift+T` still brings it in.

52f087f65f57c4c0dada028f.source: **unset (default)** — present, folded to its header bar.

acc0180f56217c763be17ab4.source: A pane in the bottom dock — one entry in its tab strip.

e0f5ef76e41db1e8b5f870bf.source:
The dock owns the **region**: the grid row, its height, the resize divider and the
fold. A tab owns what is *in* it — a body, and optionally its own header controls,
which the dock swaps in and out as the active tab changes. With only one tab
registered no strip is drawn at all; there is nothing to switch.

056697e6cff45e3afc354ad2.source:
Register one at any point in the graph's life with `graph.UIManager.addDockTab()`,
or from a plugin's `install` via `ctx.addDockTab()`. Either returns a disposer.

f62a3fa67dd10cb22035bcdf.source:
**One tab is one pane, not one view of one.** A pane with several views of its own —
the data table's `Nodes` and `Edges` — is a *single* dock tab that draws its own
switch in its `toolbar` and calls [DockTabHandle.refresh](DockTabHandle.md#refresh) to change body. So
the dock's strip lists panes (`Table`, `Events`) and never flattens one pane's views
out alongside another pane; the two levels are drawn differently for the same reason.

eaa82bca17bc3870e6356681.source:
The data table is itself just such a tab, so a registered tab is exactly as
privileged as the built-in one.

f90fced9e0481052e5cfd926.source: A glyph drawn before the label in the strip, marking where the pane came from.

64a494fd4cdfca97eaed6ab8.source:
An SVG string, injected with `innerHTML` and **not sanitised** — it must be
trusted, exactly like PivotDefinition.icon. Useful when several tabs are
the same *kind* of pane: four candidate reviews and a data table read as one list
of five otherwise.

6dca297e218bd3e0ea5ae846.source:
Stable identity: what `removeDockTab` / `activateDockTab` take, and the
`data-tab` written onto the strip's button.

ee8adc3515618e547ea1401c.source: The strip's label, used verbatim (so it can be translated).

3ba836cc24e9ab0b4faaf84d.source:
Called when this tab comes to the front, and when it leaves. A tab that watches
live data should stop working in `onDeactivate` and catch up in `onActivate`:
nothing else tells it that it is off screen.

71203f3e6cc9d32b162908eb.source:
Display order in the strip, ascending. Equal orders keep registration order —
and since plugins install after the UI is built, a plugin's tabs land after the
built-in ones without having to say so.

7b5a7f74b9dc9e4d0fc4aafc.source:
Build the pane's body. Called **once**, lazily, the first time the tab comes to
the front — a tab nobody opens costs nothing. The element is kept and re-attached
on later activations, so it holds its own state (scroll position included).

5bc266ade2f3c5d436945bc9.source:
Build this tab's header controls, laid out as part of the dock's header row.
Re-invoked on **every** activation, so the controls can reflect the tab's
current state.

2e3593f61c002c32e5e07f8c.source:
A pane with several views of its own draws the switch here. Two public classes
give it the same look the built-in table has — `pvt-dock-views` on the strip,
`pvt-dock-view` on each button, `active` on the current one — so it stays a pill
group beside the dock's own tabs and follows the theme.

bf31f62619d962312ed98e96.source:
What a live dock tab gets to drive itself with — passed to its own `render`,
`toolbar` and activation hooks. It lets a tab bring itself to the front or
unregister without capturing the graph, the dock, or the disposer
`addDockTab` returned.

290bd96a7988150f47267aa6.source: Bring this tab to the front, unfolding the dock if it is folded.

994c9121684b673ecbbc12d9.source:
Rebuild this tab's body: `render` is called again and what it returns replaces
what is there.

ff68a59865d47fc5219537cc.source:
This is how a pane with **its own** internal views switches between them — the
data table does exactly this for `Nodes` / `Edges`. Doing it by hand is not an
option: the dock keeps the element `render` gave it, so an occupant that swapped
its own DOM would leave the dock holding a stale reference to re-attach later.

677e20009a4bc980fcf76334.source: Unregister the tab and take its DOM with it.

e0b9acdaceddbbee910fa8bb.source:
Rename the tab in the strip. Nothing else moves — the body, its scroll position
and whether the tab is on show all survive, which re-registering the tab to
change a word would not. This is how a pane carries a live count.

c2512141a69fec9811041755.source: Whether this is the tab currently on show.

11bec5c9b3f577e51abf9af0.source: The tab's id — the declared one, or the auto-generated one.

72a5f8fd51e87a841a11d04d.source:
Deleting graph elements from the UI — the sidebar bulk-action Delete button and
the node / edge / note context-menu delete entries. Every one of them is gated
by InterractionCallbacks.onBeforeDelete; this switch decides whether
they are shown in the first place.

7c06a97926b6f1999f7d35b0.source:
Offer the delete affordances at all. `false` removes them, which is what a
read-only integration wants — cleaner than vetoing every click.

169e46f043ef264eb1ba5a29.source:
Interactive edge creation — the Create ▸ Add edge tool (drag-to-connect and
click-click alike) and the node context-menu's "Connect to…". What the new edge
carries, and whether it is allowed, is decided by
InterractionCallbacks.onBeforeEdgeCreate.

806b920469680f6741911aac.source:
Offer the connect affordances at all. `false` removes them, so a graph whose
relations come only from the backend never arms a connect session.

f1096c5a553badf1892ab4a3.source:
Offer the edge editor at all. `false` hides the "Edit Edge" context-menu
entry.

73f33c5dace8ab0fb40ee6ed.source:
Optional field list for the edge edit modal. Inferred from the edge's data
when undefined.

6eae95be40f07076ef8264c2.source:
When set, every interactive edge create prompts the end-user for a label
(stored on the new edge's `data.label`) using the chosen UI — no callback
needed. An `onBeforeEdgeCreate` hook, if present, takes over and this is
ignored (the hook can prompt itself via `ctx.promptLabel`).

5a2c0b22c3ad4c6b797e8f3b.source:
Optional custom body renderer for the edge edit modal — the static twin of
InterractionCallbacks.onEdgeEdit. A custom body owns the draft:
mutate `session.draft` as the user types.

ea2934c6cc16c7ec5bfa2480.source:
Interactive node creation — the Create ▸ Add node tool and the canvas
context-menu's "Add Node Here". What the new node carries is decided by
InterractionCallbacks.onBeforeNodeCreate.

c44b663fe4698360e34435f5.source: Offer the create-node affordances at all.

ea353de2c8050628867382dd.source:
Offer the node editor at all. `false` hides the Create ▸ Edit node tool —
a consumer whose backend forbids edits removes the affordance rather than
vetoing every commit.

a116891f94df8b11a7a35332.source: Optional custom field generator. Inferred if undefined

a9ca496d7908e3b8833d542f.source: Optional custom modal renderer. Leave undefined for default edition modal

9efd1bb5a735085f4a06b531.source:
`true` once this render has been superseded. A cheap guard for consumers
doing non-abortable work, so they can bail out between steps without
touching [RenderContext.signal](../../AsyncContent/interfaces/RenderContext.md#signal).

cdb6a81ed7a67a43a49b5a9d.source:
`true` while the graph has never held a node since it was built; `false` once it
has, so an analyst emptying a full canvas can be told something other than what
an empty source is told.

8658d89afce4287a00074f6d.source: `UI.emptyState`: the card an empty canvas shows.

d82d70d2a537e123f2306bc1.source:
The card is click-through, so panning and the canvas menu work over it, except for
interactive content inside it (a button, a link, a form control, anything with a
`tabindex`), which receives its own clicks.

fc430a522be9c5874c63ac65.source:
The card's content. Run each time the card appears, not on every change while it
is up, so it can say something different once the graph has held a node. A
returned `string` renders as plain text; return an `HTMLElement` to render your
own markup. May be `async`.

64afe9c903cef3e272d10020.source: Additional panel in the graph UI's sidebar.

77135159c00155671c1863cc.source: A string or `HTMLElement` for static content, or

1caf4d02c2562a398e5ef471.source:
A function of the current selection (a `Node`, an `Edge`, an array of either
for a multi-selection, or `null` when nothing is selected) — re-invoked on
every selection change unless [ExtraPanel.reactive](#reactive) is `false`.

cfe5c768567e458a637e4b31.source:
Declare panels up front via `UI.extraPanels`, or register them at any point in
the graph's life with `graph.UIManager.addPanel()` (which returns a disposer).

9d2196e27d7fc59fb41a0c1b.source: should the panel be always visible

d3b3545292a6f7402bf25e36.source:
Stable identifier, used to address the panel in `removePanel` /
`refreshPanel`. Auto-generated when omitted.

3ccdbe9bf07eeddbfe6d5752.source:
Display order in the sidebar, ascending. Panels sharing an `order` keep
their registration order, so `UI.extraPanels` reads top-to-bottom and
runtime panels append after them.

f69d85e5cb4b61fe7290f94c.source:
Re-resolve `title` and `render` whenever the selection changes. Set
`false` for a panel that is expensive to build and doesn't describe the
selection: it then renders once, and only an explicit `refreshPanel()`
rebuilds it.

71446c94bd232e94ff08f47e.source: A `string` renders as plain text; pass an `HTMLElement` to render HTML.

510784b85c90b7658391ff0f.source:
The panel's header row. A `string` renders as plain text; pass an
`HTMLElement` to render HTML. Omit it (or resolve to blank) for a panel
with no header at all.

ea1a2bb90321afae21281250.source:
A handle on a live panel, passed as the second argument to its own `title` /
`render`. It lets a panel drive itself — re-render when its own data changed,
or unregister — without capturing the graph or the disposer `addPanel`
returned.

c885e331f7743773acd9cb5b.source: Re-resolve this panel's `title` and `render` against the current selection.

fb120802f2d9454a6ba69dad.source: Unregister the panel and remove its DOM.

a937db68b41b625eb68d238a.source: The panel's id — the declared one, or the auto-generated one.

f8dc4b25c0495be610162850.source: A UI feature that is either offered or not.

4b2de80d52e3ad6af3cbe3b6.source:
Every one of these is **on unless it is switched off**, and switching one off
removes its affordances rather than leaving them to refuse: no button, no menu
entry, no keyboard shortcut, no panel. See UIManager.isFeatureEnabled.

26bbf807b3f7a1fa04661e90.source: What to show while a content hook's promise is in flight, and if it

e2a89b9b5746db4e9a405dfe.source: rejects. Only async hooks ever reach it — see [AsyncContentOptions](../../AsyncContent/interfaces/AsyncContentOptions.md).

d6d43c0c164ff664ce5e0318.source:
What the canvas shows while it waits on one of your async hooks
(`onBeforeEdgeCreate`, `onBeforeDelete`, `onBeforeNodeCreate`, the edit-commit
hooks, `onBeforeIngest`): a progress cursor and a small spinner, never while a
prompt the hook opened through its context is on screen. `false` shows nothing,
for a consumer that draws its own. See [BusyIndicatorOptions](BusyIndicatorOptions.md).

01546329d0214f2881ada257.source:
The bottom dock itself — the region the table and any registered
[DockTab](DockTab.md) share, rather than what is in it.

d1ab975caaead4b606308925.source:
`UI.table` carries the same three settings; those are honoured, and anything
set here wins. Declare them here when the table is switched off, since that is
the only way to reach the dock a plugin's tab brings with it.

940b9095bb1b8b1f49250f5d.source:
What the canvas says while the graph holds no node and no note: a card centred in
the canvas, shown and hidden as data comes and goes, so an ingest takes it away and
undoing that ingest brings it back.

13d71b2562441561503c427e.source:
Left out, or `true`, it reads "Nothing on the canvas yet". `false` shows nothing.
Declare `render` to say something of your own. See [EmptyStateOptions](EmptyStateOptions.md).

c3dd34e62911e1f542dc7db3.source:
The filter panel's facets. Omit to derive them by scanning node data
(the zero-config default); declare `facets` to generate the form from
your own declaration instead. See FilterOptions.

3c6d68d8407d49a298a19730.source: The undo / redo split buttons, their history dropdown and `Mod+Z` / `Mod+Shift+Z`.

db874d6d5c017fae1125861d.source:
Only the controls: `graph.history` goes on recording either way, so a consumer
driving undo from its own chrome switches this off and keeps the engine.

0d05b8adc5bd91e25d1e815c.source:
The inspect-properties modal — the node menu's **Inspect Properties** entry and
the `I` shortcut.

56956454d140f62da47587f8.source: The canvas legend: a key for the graph's colours that doubles as a filter.

dc68ef0029434fd011b944cb.source:
Left out, a legend appears **by itself** when the graph's colours are
explained by a declared `render.nodeTypeAccessor` — see
[LegendOptions](LegendOptions.md). `false` suppresses it, `true` asks for it without the
check, and an object configures it. A graph that encodes several things at
once passes [LegendGroupOptions](LegendGroupOptions.md) instead: one docked card, one section
per encoding.

860d0ae661a26ecd26552efb.source:
The canvas minimap: an overview of the whole graph with a rectangle showing what is
on screen. Click it to recentre the view, drag it to pan.

178522ff1083a02022c27704.source:
`full` mode mounts one for you, opening in `collapsed: 'auto'` so it folds itself
away on a canvas with no corner to spare. `false` suppresses it; `true` or an object
asks for it in any mode — see [MinimapOptions](../../../../interfaces/MinimapOptions.md). Passing your own
`minimap()` plugin in `plugins` also wins over this.

bdabf2e4baf0c26a8401dace.source:
Free-floating notes on the canvas: the strip's **Notes** button and its panel,
the Create ▸ Add note tool, the canvas menu's **Add Note**, and the `N` /
`Shift+N` shortcuts.

6b800e70af8b7118140f4cdd.source:
`enabled: false` takes every one of them away *and* closes the door behind them:
`graph.noteManager.addNote` refuses, so nothing — not a plugin, not the initial
data — puts a note on a canvas that offers no way to read or remove one.

8d42aebc839e88f2f0c7c811.source:
Toast notifications. `enabled: false` silences the corner: every
`graph.notifier.*` call becomes a no-op returning `undefined`, which is already
what a mode with no notification slot returns.

69b23f0bcb49289fb592beaa.source:
The **Physics** rail mode — the flyout holding the simulation sliders and
presets. `enabled: false` takes its rail button and its panel away; whether the
simulation runs at all is `simulation.enabled`'s business.

e7a35fc7c5d154e9cb3a49fd.source:
The Pivot rail mode — where an analyst picks an origin, reads what each
registered pivot advertises, narrows it and runs it.

3481c34eccf5f4de16e5aa2c.source:
`'auto'` (the default) ties the rail button to the registry: it appears when the
first pivot registers and goes when the last one leaves, so a consumer with no
pivots sees no trace of the feature. `true` keeps it there regardless, for pivots
that arrive asynchronously; `false` never shows it. Never mounted in `viewer` or
`static` mode.

c9d4e551d8cb3cf7a212fea1.source:
Node search: the header's **Search** button, its picker modal and `Shift+J`.
`graph.selectElement` and the pickers other features open are untouched.

e72e21ea0bf69ddc20827ebb.source:
Fold nodes that play the same role into one group node, and the **Simplify** rail
mode that switches the rules. Left out, `full` mode offers the neighbour rule
switched off; the other modes show and run nothing unless rules are declared.
`enabled: false` removes the feature.

ee22d6f4caf362d8fbf82529.source:
The data dock: the graph's nodes and edges as a sortable, selectable grid
split off the bottom of the canvas.

cb85a9a4dc1742e0bc2d33e7.source:
`full` mode offers one by default; `false` suppresses it entirely, an object
configures it. Other modes never mount it. See [TableOptions](TableOptions.md).

59638d8ca5a3ac009ba85041.source:
The classname of the theme to force the UI to ignore user's prefered color scheme.
Available by default: `light` and `dark`.
Keep it `undefined` to use user's prefered color scheme.

588a4d09b11fb2d51446bfb5.source:
The strip along the top of the canvas: the Search / Filter / Notes pills, the
host's own [TopBar.actions](TopBar.md#actions) and the undo-redo group. `enabled: false` removes
the strip, the 48px it reserved and the shortcuts its controls own.

66c3f9f146320add13f49aad.source:
Not to be confused with [GraphUI.mainHeader](#mainheader), which is how elements are
*named* wherever they are shown. Each pill also has its own switch
([GraphUI.search](#search), `UI.filter.enabled`, [GraphUI.notes](#notes),
[GraphUI.history](#history)) for taking one away rather than all of them.

6cad40ee01e6fef713b8b9aa.source:
The **View** rail mode — the flyout holding the layout, grid and visibility
switches. `enabled: false` takes its rail button and its panel away.

3bd60d2a854bf3209fe322b8.source: Mapping functions to extract a node/edge's title and subtitle.

90b48b41f582a10ad78f420b.source: Example for node. Replace with edge for edge mapping.

630a9cf4df5cc458796ff027.source:
**Synchronous only.** These feed the header's auto-fitting title slot
and `resolveNodeByName` (node search, `[[node]]` note autocomplete), all of
which need the text now. To show fetched detail, use an async
[MainHeader.render](MainHeader.md#render) or [PropertiesPanel.nodePropertiesMap](PropertiesPanel.md#nodepropertiesmap) instead.

36a8069a1466f1e96d226940.source: Takes the key over from an earlier binding on purpose, until disposed: no warning.

4a22fdb2799f8e7bf829043e.source:
One row in the legend: a swatch, a label, and how to tell which elements it
stands for — nodes, or edges in an `edge`-scoped section.

3cca46ca77f14c7d46c319e8.source:
Draw this badge as the swatch instead of a dot, for elements told apart by a
`NodeStyle.badges` mark rather than by their fill. It is drawn the way the canvas
draws it, so the legend shows the same mark. A badge naming no `color` takes the
entry's. Ignored in an `edge`-scoped section, whose swatch is a line.

b8b311d6194d37858b9b4d65.source:
The swatch colour — any CSS colour. Sampled from the renderer in derived mode:
the node's fill, or an edge's stroke in an `edge`-scoped section.

5bbdbdc74f7dcee0e1bd2f49.source: Stable identity: the toggle key, and the value written to the filter.

c27cfded4461af1217d8abee.source: Human label, used verbatim (so it can be translated).

2030198644cf61c223d4ffdd.source:
Which elements this entry stands for. Defaults to matching `id` against
`LegendOptions.key` on the element's data, when a `key` is declared.

676ffe9c5070e84b07cafd8c.source: Receives a `Node`, or an `Edge` when the section declares `scope: 'edge'`.

e5458ac72217517473e9bbef.source:
`UI.legend` in its **multi-section** form: one docked card keying the graph on
several encodings at once. Sections stack top to bottom in declaration order,
each with its own title, entries and collapse toggle.

eb1ad4fdf851f2530fdbdb88.source:
Every filterable section owns its own filter, and filters **and** together: with
`attribute` switched off in one section and `self` in another, what stays on the
canvas is the nodes that are neither.

14473d32384b1720f63af9e0.source:
A section declaring neither `key` nor `entries` is the dimension already declared
as `render.nodeTypeAccessor` — the one spelling for a styling dimension that
isn't a plain data key. Only one section may do that.

024d3a602f9939fb488caf26.source: Which corner the whole card docks in.

a5730ccd576da9e7bb49d564.source: The sections, rendered top to bottom in declaration order.

80c936233c27f652c2ddbebd.source:
`UI.legend` — the canvas legend. It is **descriptive**: it reports the colours
the renderer already resolved and never assigns one, so the consumer stays the
sole owner of node colouring.

345590b3c9a22d5f0810f676.source:
Entries come from `key` (derived from the data, swatches sampled from the
renderer), from `entries` (declared), or from both — `key` then supplies the
default predicate for entries that don't carry one.

90ae5ad5e50fc78ede027609.source:
With **neither**, the legend keys itself on `render.nodeTypeAccessor` (the
dimension you already declared for `nodeStyleMap`) — but only after checking
that this dimension really is the colour dimension: every category must resolve
to exactly one colour, there must be at least two of them, and few enough of
them to be categories. That check is what makes a legend nobody asked for safe;
`UI.legend: true` skips it, `false` suppresses the legend entirely.

f2537b90a840f0f502370448.source:
To key a graph on more than one dimension at a time, pass
[LegendGroupOptions](LegendGroupOptions.md) instead.

726f234182687e82761093db.source:
Declared entries, or a function re-resolved against the live graph every
time the legend rebuilds (so the list can follow the data).

b189dd1cd28a81bed86c1b32.source: Clicking an entry filters the graph. `false` renders a pure key.

65b35f5fb0183a66249dc77f.source:
Hovering an entry reads its category off the canvas: the elements it stands for
keep their look, everything else dims until the pointer leaves. Works on a
`filterable: false` key too — pointing at a category asks nothing of the graph.

c17081ab8d541bfd82a1d1da.source:
Stable identity: the section's own filter key (`__legend:<id>`) and the
`section` field of the `legendToggle` event.

5265fe76a60d433c7c416b6f.source:
Derived mode: the data key whose distinct values become the entries, each
swatch sampled from the renderer's resolved style. Read off nodes, or off edges
when [scope](LegendSection.md#scope) is `'edge'`. Also supplies the default predicate when
`entries` are declared without one.

1850d9618ace9b3790078b1d.source: Entries shown before the list scrolls.

f048414a0eac2c66ee6dccf9.source:
Which corner it docks in. In `full` mode the default is the right column,
stacked above the minimap — the left one belongs to the mode rail and its
panels. Other modes keep the bottom-left corner.

9c025e3e337ee925cf77a4c1.source:
Which collection this section keys on. `'edge'` lists the graph's relation
kinds with a **line** swatch — stroke colour, dash and marker as the renderer
resolved them — and its toggles hide edge *layers*: the nodes stay put, and so
do the layout, the selection and the camera.

4a5895b31edddb2f141432dd.source:
An `edge` section filters whether or not `UI.filter.edgeFacets` declares its
key: given one it drives that facet, so the panel and the legend are two views
of one filter; without one it reserves a facet of its own.

ec9821fe0bb2d7751d665a45.source: Header text, used verbatim (so it can be translated).

ac41349fc1f791898d2d9e13.source:
One section of the legend: a key for one dimension of the data. These are
[LegendOptions](LegendOptions.md) minus `position` — a section never claims a corner of the
canvas, the card it is stacked in does (see [LegendGroupOptions](LegendGroupOptions.md)).

54b587805f0e817f24a869fb.source:
Derived mode: the data key whose distinct values become the entries, each
swatch sampled from the renderer's resolved style. Read off nodes, or off edges
when [scope](#scope) is `'edge'`. Also supplies the default predicate when
`entries` are declared without one.

cd5c743476a36df41eef7c9a.source: The payload of the `legendToggle` event: which legend entries are on and off.

ebb29e923340473e71760c4b.source: Ids of the entries whose nodes are hidden.

c52e93f8550406790d753a9f.source: Ids of the entries whose nodes are shown.

72893a5046952bdb383d863f.source: Define what should be displayed in the sidebar's main header slot for node or edges.

d467abceddec9507ecccd6a6.source:
These maps also name elements elsewhere — the tooltip's header, the table's `Name`
column, `[[node]]` note references — so they are about *naming*, not about one
panel. The strip along the top of the canvas is a different thing entirely: switch
that off with [GraphUI.topBar](GraphUI.md#topbar).

3d304954cfdd869e34a3795c.source: Custom renderer for the main header. This content will override the default sidebar main header.

12a207e059828d796a2dcdb8.source:
A returned `string` renders as plain text; return an `HTMLElement` to render HTML.
May be `async`: the slot shows a placeholder until it resolves, and a result
arriving after the selection moved on is dropped.

66bf281530d9ca442128958b.source:
Return (or resolve to) `undefined` to hand the selection back to the default
header: the [nodeHeaderMap](#nodeheadermap) / [edgeHeaderMap](#edgeheadermap) title for one element,
the selection count for several, the canvas total for none. Return `null` to
draw nothing.

4456f28e2d51eba559cd5fe4.source: Overrides for the neighbours panel's graph. See [NeighborsPanel.graph](NeighborsPanel.md#graph).

13495f21da8034580f0f318b.source:
Merged over the panel's radial `egoTree` layout. The root is always the
selected node.

069613ddc8ace1d8edb3b322.source:
Shallow-merged over the main graph's render options. The panel's own settings
(no drag, no zoom, no node expansion, no focus mode) still win.

13b5d574f932cebcda03ad2c.source: Represents the configuration for the neighbors panel in the graph UI's sidebar

be1f9fbe3fbd83a71bfdeddf.source: Defines how to compute and display neighbors for nodes and edges.

572e5300cbdddcf8a67ae268.source:
Whether the sidebar shows a neighbours panel at all. `false` removes it and its
separator — right for a graph whose edges say nothing worth listing.

74ab6c6cf276d7b6910a36cb.source:
Options for the panel's neighbour graph, which otherwise draws with the main
graph's render options.

4807292ca29100eacf36cd40.source: Represents the configuration for the properties panel in the graph UI's sidebar

ace816c7a2e1cfc4d69b2eeb.source: Defines how to compute and display properties for nodes and edges.

c6ab440013c11c6996a1f341.source: A function that computes the list of edge properties to display.

b5dc66092ec88b225c39ef1b.source:
May be `async` — return a promise of the entries and the panel shows a
placeholder until it resolves.

81286764ad77463c8ad2de8b.source:
Whether the sidebar shows a properties panel at all. `false` removes it and its
separator, leaving the header, the neighbours panel and any extra panels.

7ab2e658fb358dca14df033e.source: A function that computes the list of node properties to display.

bc55493b1be4cb2a46e951c0.source: Custom renderer for the property panel. This content will override the default sidebar property panel.

93eb91008949f817b64d2865.source:
Return (or resolve to) `undefined` to hand the selection back to the default
panel: the [nodePropertiesMap](#nodepropertiesmap) / [edgePropertiesMap](#edgepropertiesmap) rows for one
element, the aggregated table for several. Return `null` to draw nothing.

2a24a9aa5fd266dbab176b15.source: Represents a single property entry to display in the properties panel.

5f17d84eee674c31c9f7c461.source: `name` is the label or key of the property.

3341395c16f4d20fed07eff4.source: `value` is the value associated to the key for the node or edge.

c1a3eda53964af57f4cdf9b5.source:
A `string` (for either field) renders as plain text; to render HTML, pass an
`HTMLElement` (or a function returning one). Since 1.4.0 string values are no
longer parsed as markup — wrap HTML in an element instead.

c9110dd10dc80d4f3612f3d8.source:
**Synchronous only.** Fetch the rows instead: an async
[PropertiesPanel.nodePropertiesMap](PropertiesPanel.md#nodepropertiesmap) resolves once and then hands back
plain entries, rather than putting a spinner in every cell.

6a60095ea183c6e58b5a7526.source:
A mode registered onto the mode rail — the door an integrator builds their own
Explore or Enrich mode through.

d13c998367d6fc3433eb7ef4.source:
Registered modes render **below a divider**, after the four built-in modes, ordered by
[order](#order). Register one at any point in the graph's life with
`graph.UIManager.addRailMode()`, or from a plugin's `install` via `ctx.addRailMode()`.
Either returns a disposer.

6d3b119de42143623558c943.source:
A `'pointer'` mode owns the contextual tool panel: it declares [tools](#tools), and may
add anything else through [render](#render). A `'flyout'` mode instead supplies a
[flyout](#flyout) factory whose panel opens while the mode is active.

37801e33d3a01ff1e5b3ae11.source: The tool this mode rests on when nothing is armed.

7cdeeddcd2a017963ac119d5.source:
An SVG string, injected with `innerHTML` and **not sanitised** — it must be
trusted. CSS sizes it to 20px on the rail.

d9e5aac84c21e57bd97b6779.source: Stable identity: what the store holds, and the `data-mode` on the rail button.

b028b124caa23ae69f27bde1.source:
Keep the panel open when one of this mode's tools is armed. Arming normally
collapses the panel so the canvas is clear — right for Select's Lasso, wrong for a
mode whose panel *is* the workspace and whose tools only say how to feed it.

2a945e413ffc3690f6be3a12.source:
`'pointer'` modes own the tool panel; `'flyout'` modes open a settings overlay and
have no tools.

6ec2d0e2af54013917388ae9.source: The rail button's label, used verbatim.

44537f873119e593b2bb73ea.source: Called when the mode becomes active.

260b97ad66db61fd46699152.source:
Called when the mode is left, and when it is unregistered while active. Disarm
whatever the mode armed here. Not called on UI teardown — use the disposers your
plugin already tracks for that.

f0e9eedfacd66683b9c5027a.source:
Display order among registered modes, ascending. Equal orders keep registration
order. Does not affect the built-in modes, which always come first.

d7e525efcd0b8de455e9d5dc.source:
Whether the tool panel is expanded the first time the mode is entered. Defaults to
open so the mode's tools are discoverable.

c403b40999f9c5c347e0d000.source: Let the analyst drag this mode's panel wider or narrower by its right edge.

1cd78784ffc587a9d099f4a0.source:
Off by default: a panel of icon rows has one right width, and a handle on it is a
control with nothing to do. A mode whose panel is the workspace — a form, a list,
a set of results — is where the choice is worth offering. The width is remembered
per mode for the session and is not persisted, so a reload starts from
[panelWidth](#panelwidth) again.

8b16e04b85726b1c894584d6.source:
How wide this mode's tool panel is, in pixels. The built-in width fits a row of
icon + label; a mode whose [render](#render) slot holds a form or a list needs more.

71101f216403f3b21c63daf0.source:
Extra panel content, appended **below** the tool rows — a slider, a search box,
anything the rows cannot express. Re-invoked whenever the panel is rebuilt.

ac766b45babfdfe6e07ea6d5.source:
A single key that activates the mode, or toggles its panel when it is already
active. Registered through the normal keybinding manager, so a key already bound is
shadowed (with a warning) until this mode is removed.

24a28ec6d0d5e1d997a141f7.source:
The mode's tools, as rows in its panel. Pass a function when the set depends on
the current selection or data; it is re-read on every render.

3bcc76094ae7360d69b1cb8b.source: One tool in a rail mode's contextual panel — a row in the panel the mode owns.

6555e3c394fa8be29e11b40d.source: When it returns false the row is disabled. Re-checked on every selection change.

75cd9acca499d36fea4600b3.source:
An SVG string. It is injected with `innerHTML` and **is not sanitised**, so it
must come from a source you trust. CSS sizes it to 18px in the panel.

3d80556f9c3cfa4c86060f93.source: Stable identity: what the store arms, and the `data-tool` on the row.

fa0fa2b210121bb14190aa7b.source: The row's label, used verbatim (so it can be translated).

09025b7f32abdacd1e96875d.source: Perform the tool's effect. A `'toggle'` receives the desired armed state.

2228f2d4949f554aa3954ef3.source: A [DockTab](DockTab.md) once registered: its `id` is resolved.

68d07ce4a8440cb573a91b48.source: An [ExtraPanel](ExtraPanel.md) once registered: its `id` is always resolved.

141f362cf283aedfa39a95a3.source: Determines whether the sidebar is collapsed by default.

c7118b5b7b7de6f23e586433.source: `'auto'` Keeps the sidebar open unless there isn't enough screen space, in which case it collapses automatically.

e0f7d50323675a54f9726654.source:
Whether the sidebar exists at all. `false` gives `full` mode a canvas with no
side column — the properties, neighbours and extra panels have nowhere to go,
and `addPanel()` keeps its registry without a host to draw it.

533a55cec44dfd5e02c93984.source: One column of the data dock.

15a36ac7bd197ec8fd3ea5a3.source:
Deliberately an extension of FilterFacet: a facet already says how to read a
value off an element and what kind of value it is, which is exactly what a column
needs. So declaring `UI.filter.facets` describes your data once and the filter panel
and the table agree about it.

e1a364dcd4fb4e9cf3959c9f.source:
How to read this column off an element. Defaults to `element.getData()[key]`, which
is what makes a FilterFacet usable as a column unchanged.

2a64d5943eea3b312a02dab8.source:
Give this column a filter control in its header, typed off its [type](#type) — a
Min/Max pair for a `numberRange`, a dropdown of the values present for a `select`,
a substring box otherwise.

abe047996140cb5346865a8c.source:
It narrows the **rows**; the canvas is left alone unless someone presses the dock's
**Apply to graph** button (see [TableOptions.filterGraph](TableOptions.md#filtergraph)), so reading and
filtering stay separate acts.

d63aa817f8def5309d7ecb6f.source:
false for a column you declare — but `true` throughout the **derived**
column set, which infers its filters off the types it already inferred. Declare
`columns` and you get exactly what you asked for.

6a71bdcfc00f942ea1f80fa6.source:
Render the cell. A string is inserted as text, an `HTMLElement` as markup.
Ignored by export, which always writes the raw value.

881ccead9ec02e568f0147ca.source: Start hidden (still listed in the column picker).

1cfaf196c95848b0b2c7142c.source: Filter identity, and the `GraphFilters` key `setFilter` / `getFilters` use.

9c2e2014456a31cea5e07b4d.source:
Human label for the form control, used verbatim (so it can be translated).
Defaults to a prettified `key`.

e0050cac43c09baf16aa2cde.source: Column width — a pixel count, or any CSS length.

3f53952a5b42f91437c55585.source:
The data dock's configuration. Everything here is read-only behaviour: the table
reflects and selects, and never changes the graph. Hiding, pinning and restoring stay
with the sidebar's bulk actions and the filter panel.

a73f26cd244797d64b4e45c6.source:
Folded away to just its header bar. `'auto'` follows the room available, until the
first explicit collapse or expand hands control to the user for good.

f50c2163d7b9d78d784f4506.source:
The node columns. Omit to have them resolved for you: from declared
FilterOptions.facets if there are any, otherwise by scanning node data.

0ba2148a089ff022c4fb5a1f.source: The edge columns, on the same terms as [TableOptions.columns](#columns).

2e6b0a725c6bd1ad74659cf3.source: Export buttons offered in the dock header. `false` hides them.

21637fe347bf909f8354e306.source:
Offer the **Apply to graph** button, which hides the elements the column filters
leave out — the one thing in the dock that changes what the canvas shows.

9698d2f16c6d1a217a4f6375.source:
Nothing happens until it is pressed: narrowing a column is still reading, and the
`Visibility` column goes on reporting the truth beside it. Pass `false` for a dock
that can never touch the canvas at all.

b3f9355d2412fb44db0550e6.source:
The dock's height: a pixel count, or a fraction of the canvas between 0 and 1.
Clamped so the canvas keeps a usable minimum whatever you ask for.

47daab3986f5eb5874e65f5e.source:
Whether a cluster's nested nodes get rows of their own, as peers of the graph's own
nodes, with a `Cluster` column carrying the path they came from. A **Nested nodes**
switch in the header takes them back out for a reader who only wants the top level.

ce38eee89503a484c15b3f6f.source:
They are listed flat rather than as a tree on purpose: the dock exists to answer
questions the canvas cannot — which are the hubs, which are over a threshold — and
that only keeps working if a sort or a filter reaches every row equally.

fb50d2c550ffca77f954fea1.source:
A nested node is not a node of this graph: the canvas draws it from a separate
subgraph, so it has no dot of its own here and its `Visibility` reads `nested` while
any cluster above it is shut. Pass `false` for a dock that never lists them, where
`Children` is all a cluster's row says about its contents.

9c56ba3262df0b29d5756a0b.source: true (the `Cluster` column appears only on a graph that has clusters)

6b670a3fe7dedb59ff95b21f.source:
Whether the dock starts expanded. Three states, because the collapsed bar is the
control that opens it:

dc53b9dabbee031516c26a0c.source: `true` — present and expanded, showing the grid.

5bbe9d7b27b353f4f6672a74.source:
`false` — not present at all, for a canvas with no dock. `Shift+T` still brings
it in.

bb0baa60a0fc292dcf5e8914.source:
**unset (default)** — present, folded to its header bar. The bar is the
affordance, which is why there is no toolbar button for the dock.

21debffd425611e8a832d815.source: Which tabs to offer, in order.

184f464313726af2515df746.source: Row count above which rows are windowed rather than all rendered.

334840262add29149ba613fd.source: May be `async` — the property list shows a placeholder until it resolves.

8ab1395a7f0eb442a92884ed.source:
`{ nodes, edges, groups }`: per kind. A missing key is `true`, so `{ edges: false }`
means everything but edges.

a6bdcfe5b4fe852703ebf985.source: `(element, kind) => boolean`: asked on every hover. One that throws counts as `false`.

3b88328a5655719bfd72b5c6.source: Custom renderer for the tooltip. This content will override the default tooltip

8a7230ba52b1083fb43f89c3.source:
A returned `string` renders as plain text; return an `HTMLElement` to render HTML.
May be `async`, on the same terms as [Tooltip.renderNodeExtra](#rendernodeextra).

d568d5b04ba30769617c0eff.source: Custom renderer for edge tooltips. This content is added after the default tooltip.

3eb04b7d57cc208198df266b.source: May be `async`, on the same terms as [Tooltip.renderNodeExtra](#rendernodeextra).

64e8d44646e1ba7d4c452d82.source:
Custom renderer for a group's tooltip, made by `UI.simplify`. Added after its
members and the nodes it links to. A group skips `render` and `renderNodeExtra`,
which are about one node's data.

6a75be4813e8dd4c35bc7aba.source: Custom renderer for node tooltips. This content is added after the default tooltip.

d7f3235bfbfaf5d5105cdabc.source:
May be `async` — the tooltip shows a placeholder, then swaps in the content and
repositions itself. Hovering another node first drops the stale result and aborts
`ctx.signal`.

7a7a44b97dfc77fd28f7751c.source: Which kinds show a tooltip. A missing key is `true`.

b51974736a27f27a57ee04b4.source: `UI.topBar`: the strip along the top of the canvas, and the host's own pills in it.

a7cd88f33b8a5fd8ae276a03.source:
Pills the host adds beside the built-in ones, in the same style. The function form
is called again on every refresh, so it may return a different set.

17d662a7e4b79f12a59ca70e.source:
One host pill in the top bar: an action on the whole canvas, such as saving it.
Every function field is re-read on UIManager.refreshTopBar, after a data
change, and once an `onclick` that returned a promise settles.

e5b4630d2277435d4dde035b.source: Stable id: the pill's `data-action`, and the key UIManager.removeTopBarAction takes.

6767e1416884318f4ff13ccb.source:
Rows behind a caret: the pill becomes a split button, the label running `onclick`
and the caret opening these. The same row type as the context menus, without
`submenu`. The function form gets the context, so a row can prompt too; it is called
on every refresh and every open, and no rows means no caret.

fdfe7afbc0e5975219272267.source:
Runs on a click, or Enter / Space on the focused pill. A returned promise disables
the pill until it settles, so a slow save cannot be started twice, then refreshes
every action.

189102804359912bd009a055.source:
`'start'` follows the built-in pills on the left; `'end'` sits just before the
undo-redo group on the right. Declaration order within each.

4e9a9225153fc4d14564d781.source: Shown as a badge on the pill. Visual only: the binding is the host's to register.

8eb2f2adf8070570abc3b55e.source: The label: "Save as graph", then "Update graph" once saved.

46728ba76a9c76a2d52ee640.source: Ask before doing something; resolves `true` only on the confirm button.

d6acc8a9094696bc86fd1f68.source:
Open the library's modal and resolve to the values, or `null` on cancel. The same
declarative form the editors and a pivot's save use; titled with the action's label
and submitted with *OK* unless the options say otherwise.

1b0115626fa5387f3c02daf1.source: Re-read every action's fields, as UIManager.refreshTopBar does.

f002f3a84bfe48c09e5a1139.source:
A panel's title or body: static content, or a function of the current
selection (and the panel's own [ExtraPanelHandle](../interfaces/ExtraPanelHandle.md)).

a0a1f11a68598c268ab7300d.source:
A `string` renders as plain **text**; return an `HTMLElement` to render your
own markup. May be `async`: the panel shows a placeholder until it resolves,
and a result arriving after the selection moved on is dropped.

98c3b5de6025b1c86803c989.source:
The current sidebar selection handed to an [ExtraPanel](../interfaces/ExtraPanel.md)'s `title` /
`render`: the selected `Node` or `Edge`, an array for a multi-selection, or
`null` when nothing is selected. Same shape as [PropertiesPanel.render](../interfaces/PropertiesPanel.md#render).

7309a744a0672434b079042a.source: `"viewer"`: Navigate the graph (pan, zoom, drag), no UI panels.

937b66e9dc51dd5c39969c15.source: `"static"`: Static graph, no UI, no interactions.

5eea7de96ef6bd3c0f9b0d30.source: Classe(s) to be added on the element, typically used in icon libraries such as fontawesome

a9885d3e8f8e145ab857598a.source: Raw unicode to be used in icon libraries such as fontawesome

ede88d7acad9a13eba318580.source: An URL path to access the image content

b61aec2edddcd0024eb06d5c.source:
A key combination: modifiers then the key, joined by `+` — `'Ctrl+C'`, `'Shift+K'`,
`'ArrowUp'`. Modifiers are written `Ctrl`, `Meta` (Cmd on macOS), `Shift`, `Alt`, in
that order, and **`Mod` matches either `Ctrl` or `Meta`**, which is what a shortcut
meant to work on both platforms should use.

d8235cec9d98c7ca75f3c7fe.source:
The key itself is `KeyboardEvent.key` verbatim, so it is case-sensitive and shift
changes it: the two halves of an undo pair are `'Mod+z'` and `'Mod+Shift+Z'`.

c3aa3d5962b5863cefa53b84.source: Which canvas corner the legend is docked in.

ac151f0c821e43e40d5a584f.source: Which collection a legend section keys on.

5a70246228f07d4b687da07c.source:
Options to define an action item in a menu.
Can be used in contextual menus or multi-select menus.

ff17862643c3bf178515300e.source: Draw a rule above this row, to group what follows apart from what came before.

47cf7df2d9b4fda1e1bef6ce.source: Optional: a row that only opens a [MenuActionItemOptions.submenu](#submenu) needs no action of its own.

29b8627c3a0a082e4c14eec9.source: The keybinding activates this function. This is just visual. The actual binding is defined in UIManager

99ef639bce990a972a35936e.source:
Rows that open in a panel beside this one, which then carries the click. The
function form is resolved every time the menu opens, so a submenu may depend on
the element it was opened over.

3f43d5b2d12b8f779a958cf8.source:
A row with a submenu keeps its own `onclick` if it has one; the click opens the
panel either way, and closes it again on a second click.

23df40b6a89afe534494a22d.source:
An element pinned to the row's right-hand end, after the label — a count, a
badge, anything the row's own text should not have to carry.

11e97d978b18804819b44648.source:
Held by the caller rather than described to the library, so it can still be
written to once the menu is drawn: a value that is still being fetched fills its
slot when it arrives. An element is in one place at a time, so a row built fresh
on every open needs a fresh one too.

ea765a4fdab5e7035b64e98e.source: Title to be shown when hovering over the option.

2a63839715f23778d14febe3.source: Should the quick action item be flushed to the right of the menu

59ea1cb7628374b12c3f6b3c.source: Raw SVG markup as a string

213be9da59fb0410a05dc3ea.source: Which set of rows the dock is showing.

a8bbb37cdc15e0b2d937ce70.source: What a tooltip is shown for: a group made by `UI.simplify`, any other node, or an edge.

bf64572ec3212546a55f3f85.source:
A bounded, session-scoped history of what the canvas holds and shows: what was
brought in, what was taken out, what was hidden.

45ea8496787483c9fa1e62ab.source:
Reached as `graph.history`. Read it and drive it — the entry kinds are closed, so
a consumer cannot record into it. Every entry names the specific elements it
touched, which is what lets a sealed entry be skipped mid-span without the ones
around it getting out of order.

44b012d6f0fcc201d7091401.source: Fires on every change to the history. Returns a disposer.

543c7cfa3fea134621accc6d.source: What that span would touch — what drives the hover highlight and the menu's own copy.

fe6ef8468a00a6c7f3956af6.source: Redo the span running back through `throughEntryId`; the nearest one by default.

10aa4969b4a198ee0a9722d9.source:
Undo the span running from the newest entry through `throughEntryId`; the
newest entry alone by default. Lands as one `dataBatchChanged`.

8151bbfaa33d49c1e15996fd.source:
the entries actually reversed, newest first — sealed ones are passed
over and are not in it.

9f1af9c50130fc7863449a69.source:
What committing a span would actually do, counted by replaying it rather than by
summing the entries — so a hide cancelled by a later unhide nets to zero and the
menu says so.

8743ec8bea6b6036c9896e24.source: One reversible thing that happened, as one row in the history.

4cc215f184135b334caaeebd.source: For a `visibility` or `group` entry, which act it records.

6a98055cf191c83e87bf4381.source:
Stable handle, and what [GraphHistoryLike.undo](GraphHistoryLike.md#undo) addresses. A pivot
entry's id **is** its `runId`, so a `PivotRunOutcome` already carries the id
of its own row.

5cd86898617571ba5504fbff.source: What the row says: `Correlations`, `Deleted 3 nodes`, `Hid 5 nodes`.

9a408b8cf749fce6cd559f15.source:
The elements this entry touched — the row's counts, and what a hover highlights.
For a `removal`, what left the canvas: an element another source still vouches
for stays, and is not named here.

579648b83b0e563da34cf072.source:
For a pivot entry, which run of that pivot this is, counting from 1. The
tie-break between two runs of the same pivot: counts and clocks both collide,
an ordinal cannot.

60e4a4d83d74bd791506dc7f.source:
The consumer reported this operation as written through to its backend. A
persisted *creation* still reverses: the canvas loses what the backend keeps,
which a re-fetch undoes. The row says so, and the footer counts it.

8082b3e3b0055f4ebbf46114.source:
For a pivot entry, which pivot produced it — two runs of one pivot share it. For
a `removal`, the source that was removed.

ec782871b2e50c674eec95ac.source:
Never reversed — a deletion the consumer wrote through to its backend. Undo is
a canvas operation and issues no compensating write, so restoring these would
put back nodes the record of truth no longer has. Listed, and stepped over
inside a span rather than walling it.

2a56934ba2f75b80b6720dd4.source: What a span would do, before it is committed.

dca98f3ef27c158c7b53735d.source:
Inside the span and reversed, but written through to a backend that keeps its
copy — so the reversal is canvas-only. What the footer warns about.

2e3129bf213a00aa1e175c10.source: The simulated net effect of committing it.

46a7b0e5b5522b8c3fc44335.source: The span, newest first — the rows the menu marks.

e6562e9b6cae834ee44995f5.source:
The same thing as something the canvas can wear: what would go, what would be
hidden, and where what is *not* on the canvas would come back. Hand it to
`graph.showForecast`.

f0bfb062a8285d4c244efe62.source:
The elements the span touches that are on the canvas *now*. An entry whose
elements are gone names none, honestly — see [forecast](#forecast) for those.

d86e78438c9beb52a1b94a65.source: Inside the span, left alone because they are sealed.

712bc54be4672d43f91e2807.source:
Which of a kind's opposite acts an entry records, for a `visibility` or `group` entry:
the label says the same thing in words, in the graph's language.

929a3aca8f61c2ea1c7a2e6b.source: Which sort of entry a row is — a closed set.

3add581addf8f409927fc8b1.source:
`pivot` an ingest, `delete` a removal, `visibility` a durable hide or unhide,
`create` a node or edge drawn by hand, `removal` a `graph.removeBySource` call,
`group` a group made, removed or renamed by hand (`graph.simplify.groupNodes`).
Every one of them is a change to what the canvas *holds and shows*, which is the
only thing the library has the authority to reverse: a node's data is the
backend's, not ours.

741b88e4ce7ccfb74a0aadcc.source:
The language the library's own text is written in. Text the host passes in (labels,
facets, pivots, menu rows) is drawn as given and never looked up.

846ac056cf09600cb62aadbf.source:
A string is looked up in this order: the feature's own option when it has one (such
as `UI.emptyState.render`), then `messages`, then `translate`, then the bundled
language catalogue, then English.

22cf7dffedda6bc41f5a5951.source:
A BCP 47 tag such as `'fr'` or `'de-CH'`. It picks the plural rules, how numbers
are written and how lists sort. When given, it is also set as the `lang` of the
graph's root element.
English, Simplified Chinese (`zh`), French (`fr`), German (`de`) and
Portuguese (`pt`) are bundled. Regional tags such as `de-CH` use their
language's catalogue and retain their own formatting and plural rules.

13f095f96f969e44d7c095e2.source:
Messages that override the bundled catalogue, by key. Missing keys use the
selected language, or English when no catalogue is bundled.

83f70fe0aaebf049593a1c12.source:
A bridge to the host's own translation library, asked for every key `messages`
does not have. It gets the raw params, so the host's plural rules apply, and the
English text. Returning `undefined` uses the bundled language, then English.

e5980ff408f5ecdaf6ced52d.source:
A message that depends on a count, one entry per CLDR plural category the language
uses. The form is picked by `Intl.PluralRules` from the `count` param; `other` is
required because every language has it.

dac242fc81b0c1ba5e71519d.source: The id of a message the library writes, such as `'emptyState.message'`.

fe28fd089075075ae9d85b54.source:
The values a message's `{placeholders}` are filled with. A number is formatted for
the locale before it is substituted; pass a string to keep it as written.

f004bb13fa7e3beedc0e4dfa.source:
Every message the library writes, by key. `messagesEn` is the English catalogue
and the starting point for a translation.

f524132d19325cdf35ee2b57.source:
One message: plain text with `{name}` placeholders, plural forms, or a function for
anything the other two cannot say. A function gets the raw params and the graph's
[I18n](../../../../interfaces/I18n.md), to format numbers itself. Messages are text, never HTML.

80100901d6d7e6bb553cbf20.source: Options for the confirmation modal handed to [DeleteContext.confirm](DeleteContext.md#confirm).

f54d874eece01547bcdd89c2.source: Body copy. A `string` renders as plain text; pass an element to render HTML.

c4830d571eb0ee1cf2499fe8.source:
Edges that will also be destroyed as a consequence of removing `nodes` —
`graph.removeNode` cascades into every incident edge. Resolved by the library,
not the consumer. They follow whichever nodes survive a narrowed decision, so
they can't be narrowed on their own.

241cc667110a087e9acddffc.source:
Open a confirmation modal, resolving `true` on confirm and `false` on any
cancel path (Cancel, ×, overlay, Esc) — so `if (!await confirm(…)) return false`
is the whole guard. Resolves `false` in UI modes with no modal slot.

162d20b858c1fe3783cec0ee.source: Edges the user asked to delete (never overlapping [cascadingEdges](#cascadingedges)).

6b68d15b4624d69e3573adfb.source: Nodes the user asked to delete.

16f9621a4cfb4a4ed9056568.source: Notes the user asked to delete.

a8087bc4a3dff3c921a98865.source: What a resolved delete actually removed — the return of `graph.editing.requestDelete`.

862b1824e10423fb63abf523.source: False when the hook vetoed (or there was nothing left to delete).

0e7a6a837ff09b1fb6efb5be.source: Edges removed, including the ones a node removal cascaded into.

87341083f6919ae89e656855.source: `'edge'` for a node→node edge, `'note-link'` for a note→node attachment.

9bb2f2632483f5d0806f52d6.source: Whether the gesture was click- or drag-to-connect.

6a7092325e4c6d9227ed94bb.source:
Prompt the user for a whole data payload via a modal — a declarative form
(EdgePromptDataOptions.fields) or custom HTML
(EdgePromptDataOptions.render + `getValues`). Resolves to the collected
object, or `null` if the user cancelled. Feed it straight into the decision —
e.g. `return { accept: true, data: values }`. Modal only (no inline variant).

cf722b34f4635b3e1f24d8ce.source:
Prompt the user for a label while the connect gesture is still pending, using
either a floating inline input or a modal (per [EdgeLabelPromptOptions.mode](EdgeLabelPromptOptions.md#mode)).
Resolves to the entered string, or `null` if the user cancelled (Esc / closed).
The shadow-edge preview stays up while it is open. Typically fed back into the
returned decision's `data` — e.g. `return { accept: true, data: { label } }`.

ebb9df8fd9113c1f81aff50b.source: The source of the connection — a [Node](../../../../classes/Node.md) for an edge, a [Note](../../../../classes/Note.md) for a note-link.

096ccbdef643a8c9da13e88b.source: Value the field is pre-filled with.

ba1f536a9c939dee38457cb1.source: `'inline'` = floating input at the edge midpoint, `'modal'` = a modal field.

405f6da3bd352b39a34dc97a.source:
What is about to land, after dedup and after the analyst's picks — so a
candidate already on canvas never appears here.

2ad277a625c29465b1978268.source:
Open a confirmation modal, resolving `true` on confirm and `false` on any
cancel path — the same primitive [DeleteContext.confirm](DeleteContext.md#confirm) uses.

4dc997a78ce0706615c2053a.source: The nodes the pivot was run on. Empty for an origin-less pivot.

6e14471e2a0e874bc83fad42.source: `'triage'` when the analyst picked, `'auto'` when the pivot auto-ingested.

3dc6bde3f115f38cb6c24724.source:
Live validity predicate evaluated *during* the connect gesture as the cursor
hovers candidate targets (à la React Flow's `isValidConnection`). Return
`false` to mark the hovered target invalid: the shadow edge renders in an
invalid style, and releasing / clicking on it creates nothing (in that case
[onBeforeEdgeCreate](#onbeforeedgecreate) is not consulted). Runs on every pointer move, so
it must be synchronous and cheap.

b3ced0713d3c3af5c1ec9dbb.source:
Called when any of a node's rim badges is clicked, after that badge's own
`onClick`. Use it for behaviour every badge shares; use [NodeBadge.onClick](../../RendererOptions/interfaces/NodeBadge.md#onclick)
for one badge's own action.

d36f4bc700aeee387d540549.source:
Declaring it makes every badge take the pointer cursor and consume its click, so
the node underneath is not also selected.

7a48908e10bf7ee55bd131c9.source:
Called when the user asks to delete graph elements, *before* anything is
removed. The library resolves the whole target set first — including the edges
that removing a node would take with it
([DeleteContext.cascadingEdges](DeleteContext.md#cascadingedges)) — so a consumer can persist the full
consequence of the gesture without re-deriving the cascade.

522b90c08178c21a104f22a3.source:
Return `false` / `{ accept: false }` to veto: nothing is removed, no
`nodeRemove`/`edgeRemove`/`noteRemove` fires, and the selection is left intact.

681166d2c72a4e2aed615295.source: Return `true` to delete exactly what was requested.

de24dcb420d3803c3221ef0f.source:
Return `{ accept: true, nodes?, edges?, notes? }` to **narrow** the delete to
a subset — e.g. keep only what the backend actually deleted. An omitted key
means "as requested", so `{ accept: true }` is equivalent to `true`; pass an
empty array to spare that kind entirely. Elements that weren't part of the
request are ignored.

ff95fa4f7f533eaceaf727e0.source:
May be async (persist the delete, then decide) — a second delete gesture is
ignored while a decision is pending. [DeleteContext.confirm](DeleteContext.md#confirm) opens a
confirmation modal so consumers don't rebuild one.

f51d155f941a5b849ba57708.source:
Only user-initiated deletes are gated: programmatic `graph.removeNode()` /
`graph.removeEdge()` / `noteManager.removeNote()` never invoke this hook, so
consumer code driving the model isn't blocked by the consumer's own gate.

e19261ecd84b6ec3956b371f.source:
Called during a connect gesture, after the target node is resolved but
*before* the edge (or note-link) is created. Acts as the edge equivalent of
[onBeforeNodeEditCommit](#onbeforenodeeditcommit): a validation / enrichment / veto hook.

11b6a0b24abf268b74c8146b.source:
Return `false` / `{ accept: false }` to veto: the preview is dropped,
nothing is added, and connect mode stays armed so the user can retry.

c8c449b9ab3fb148723421cc.source:
Return `{ accept: true, data?, style?, id?, directed? }` to accept and
supply the new edge's payload/style/id/direction.

4f99928354a4dec094c28df3.source:
May be async (e.g. persist to a backend before deciding); the shadow-edge
preview persists until the promise settles, and no new connect gesture is
accepted while it is pending. Fires for both click- and drag-to-connect.
Also fires for note→node links ([EdgeCreateContext.kind](EdgeCreateContext.md#kind) `'note-link'`),
where the edge-specific fields of the decision are ignored.

e2f2d627839f8da5eab9c50f.source: whether the connection should be created, optionally with its data.

ab87b9ebf060eccb2844238c.source:
Called when an edge edit session is about to be committed. Acts as a
validation / persistence / veto hook, mirroring [onBeforeNodeEditCommit](#onbeforenodeeditcommit):
return `false` (or a promise of it) to refuse, leaving the edge's data
untouched and the modal open. On success the edge's data is replaced and
`edgeChange` fires on the data bus.

b4abc8dc4b1a54ea8c1cf806.source:
Called once, with the whole candidate set, just before a pivot ingests it —
the one gate on the ingest pipeline.

c5cb0754f91cb4b98a643ef4.source:
Return `false` / `{ accept: false }` to veto: nothing lands, and the run
reports `'vetoed'`.

06ba604b3408b83a434f5e73.source: Return `true` to ingest exactly what was chosen.

390f1814afc341c05b998f63.source:
Return `{ accept: true, nodes?, edges? }` to **narrow** the ingest to a
subset — e.g. only what the backend confirmed. An omitted key means "as
requested", so `{ accept: true }` is equivalent to `true`; pass an empty
array to land none of that kind.

3b3411732cd8c67db233e0f2.source:
Called once per ingest with the entire batch, never per candidate: a pivot
that found 1,800 correlations must not turn into 1,800 hook calls, and the
per-gesture write-path hooks ([onBeforeEdgeCreate](#onbeforeedgecreate), [onBeforeDelete](#onbeforedelete))
are deliberately about user gestures rather than a programmatic merge. It gates
`autoIngest` pivots too, which is what keeps them governed.

c44928305d29cfe147ce1d48.source:
May be async (persist, then decide). [IngestContext.confirm](IngestContext.md#confirm) opens the
shared confirmation modal.

83807b321a9d069ede5abc48.source:
Called when the user creates a node interactively (Create ▸ Add node, or the
canvas context-menu's "Add Node Here"), once the graph-space position is known
and before the node is added. Mirrors [onBeforeEdgeCreate](#onbeforeedgecreate):

d98672db0a304cc1fe309d23.source: Return `false` / `{ accept: false }` to veto — nothing is added.

275cc9622112e21ec45df0ed.source: Return `true` to accept the library's default node.

06b60ce7e5daa9d33632c52b.source:
Return `{ accept: true, id?, data?, style? }` to accept and supply the new
node's id / payload / style.

d4a1bf80a01febaeab0ebc33.source:
May be async, and [NodeCreateContext.promptData](NodeCreateContext.md#promptdata) opens the same
declarative-form or custom-HTML modal the edge hook uses. Absent this hook the
tool still works — it just creates a default, unnamed node. Programmatic
`graph.addNode()` is never gated.

3b53c6eacecbb8998b53a3cf.source:
Called when a node edit session is about to be committed. Acts as a
validation / persistence / veto hook: return `false` (or a promise of it) to
refuse, leaving the node's data untouched and the modal open. On success the
node's data is replaced and `nodeChange` fires on the data bus.

90223b2bbbbb77112297f5f3.source: boolean indicating if the commit should proceed or not

a35832ce10adf62f6c3f3d3b.source: Called when the canvas is about to be zoomed.

e612705e5af76663f5c95f7b.source: Called when the canvas is clicked.

5d645cf023eda538bb80fb89.source: Called when the canvas is right clicked.

22399d656f8112d8a5174576.source: Called when the mouse move over the canvas.

06ca45af0f0a80ee2eee45ab.source: Called when a user pointer down the canvas.

7fc8b1537d99c2c9b0347b7d.source: Called when a user pointer up the canvas.

1eda44442de10e8181e5ae11.source: Called when the canvas is zoomed.

15ce93bd672f11be884431f2.source: Called when an edge is unselected by the user.

62100f77003207f300332aa7.source: Called when an edge is selected by the user.

53903e4ff00add2a9fd36456.source: Called when an edge is right clicked.

728af14a8fbef41caecffc6e.source:
Called when an edge edit session starts. Acts as a UI hook, mirroring
[onNodeEdit](#onnodeedit): return the body to inject into the edit modal. A custom
body owns the draft — mutate `session.draft` (or call `session.setDraft`) as
the user types, because the library has no form to read on submit.

fab094412a917ccd30dd423e.source: A HTML Div that will be injected in the modal's body

8828a01e77f961c5d1046237.source: Called when an edge edit session gets cancelled.

fa6b69b5be34313a8e9d61c5.source: Called when a user hovers over an edge.

b4105074b9e781a87da23eb3.source: Called when a node is unselected by the user.

2f77c72615f354e8887a95b6.source: Called when a node is clicked.

47205162386641e46b64eacc.source: Called when a node is right clicked.

84d5c1de253ac923a11b5df7.source: Called when a node is double clicked.

f0463da2c67d48afba7b64d9.source: Called when a node drag ends.

19f1083ab00d23f9ececb630.source: Called when a node is dragged.

d907570a1e4e235f1d57821e.source: Called when a node edit session starts. Act as a UI hook.

594268dae6012a9e60553d81.source: Called when an node edit session gets cancelled

dcfec50ca846ee874d462410.source: Called when a user hovers over a node.

7f65eead8b7013816b64f3f7.source: Called when a user hovers out of a node.

02148a5a7b8b3edaa239af44.source: Called when a user pointer down a node.

09ee33fc002cd7ecc1361352.source: Called when a user pointer up a node.

efdfc8ef75c8e8b9d7638617.source: Called when a node is selected by the user.

905df252d54ba316cd689e73.source: Called when nodes are selected by the user.

a8e3140150fcd3ef427382a2.source: Called when a note is clicked.

8f5f3b6a01c377bea50a186c.source: Called when a note is right clicked.

4bd7bffe28f75751bbb2f30a.source: Called when a note is double clicked.

93d5b26ed439590234c607db.source: Called when a user hovers over a note.

4c9744acd0f1e845941333a9.source: Called when a user hovers out of a note.

6bffde20e59ef2708451cfca.source: Called when the every tenth of simulation ticks.

ab57db2763a1c749bd40967b.source: Graph-space position the node will be placed at (correct under any zoom/pan).

447114f7a8ecba0b7fc00192.source:
Prompt the user for the new node's data payload via a modal — a declarative
form ([PromptDataOptions.fields](PromptDataOptions.md#fields)) or custom HTML (`render` + `getValues`).
Resolves to the collected object, or `null` if the user cancelled. Feed it
straight into the decision — e.g. `return { accept: true, data: values }`.

15171894ee9859c5ed5a2d59.source:
Options for a modal that collects a whole data payload (not just a label) —
[EdgeCreateContext.promptData](EdgeCreateContext.md#promptdata) and [NodeCreateContext.promptData](NodeCreateContext.md#promptdata).
Supply **either** `fields` (a declarative form, built with the same field system as
the node editor) **or** `render` + `getValues` (arbitrary HTML you populate and read
yourself). If both are given, `render` wins.

56303c14912b32e295947d01.source: Declarative form fields; the resolved object is keyed by each field's `key`.

4d2328e7f6f487d37e18d53c.source: Read the collected values out of your custom `render`ed body on submit.

8273e1e7ae50bbfb513c6f8c.source: Populate the modal body with your own HTML (ignored if fed no `getValues`).

992f276f2cac611c5d525eab.source:
`true` deletes the whole request, `false` vetoes it. The object form (with
`accept: true`) narrows the delete: each supplied array replaces that kind's
requested set, and an omitted key leaves it as requested — so `{ accept: true }`
matches `true`, and `{ accept: true, nodes: [] }` deletes no nodes.

46bf4087f6fcd6417c530476.source:
The consumer wrote this deletion through to its own backend — only the consumer
can know a write happened, so only the consumer can declare it. The history row
is listed and never reversed: undo issues no compensating write, so restoring
these would put back what the record of truth no longer has.

ca29e57deda9bbf542f11523.source: Which affordance asked for a delete.

6a256c0e8edd5324710ef978.source:
`true` accepts with defaults, `false` vetoes. The object form accepts (when
`accept` is true) and lets the consumer supply the new edge's data/style/id/
direction. The `data`/`style`/`id`/`directed` fields apply to edges only and
are ignored for note-links.

5560685e9e341fd93699c511.source:
The consumer wrote this creation through to its own backend — only the consumer
can know a write happened, so only the consumer can declare it. The history row
is marked saved and still reverses: undo takes the element off the canvas, the
backend keeps its copy, and the menu says so before the click.

d1e00b3e276b800cf312cb40.source: Whether a connection was drawn by click-to-connect or drag-to-connect.

0906bee6300f824eba399caf.source: Which UI the label prompt uses.

4f63288384d2fee3dae38f10.source:
`true` ingests the whole batch, `false` vetoes it. The object form narrows:
each supplied array replaces that kind's set, matched by id, and an omitted key
leaves it as requested.

6db416ef5e0a005745282470.source:
`true` accepts the library's default node, `false` vetoes. The object form accepts
(when `accept` is true) and lets the consumer supply the new node's id / data / style.

7cfb85e30628e4b11a5e465d.source: Whether an interactive node create came from the tool panel or the canvas menu.

bd8d4a2e207ee3ca9502030d.source: Should the nodes be placed horizontally rather than vertically

72596576fba0059491794723.source:
Multiplies the distance between consecutive levels — the depth axis of the tree, or
the gap between rings in `radial` mode. At `1` the tree is scaled to fill the canvas.

f852c4143d3e6a4337dceaa0.source: Should the nodes be placed radially instead of vertically

828bab9bc2ddb484b5a9acea.source: The grap between each layers used in the radial mode

747816b7c322e80086507ffe.source: The algorithm to use to find the root of the tree

112d597897c3fe7d7a5acdf3.source:
Multiplies the distance between nodes *within* a level — the breadth axis.
Ignored in `radial` mode, where a level always spans the full circle.

1e6786575bda2ea5285bafee.source:
Whether the two spacing multipliers tune themselves from the size of the nodes
and the shape of the tree, or stay exactly where they are put.

334c8b8edf63c9f21ca465de.source:
`'auto'` is the default — except for a tree that sets `levelSpacing` or
`siblingSpacing` explicitly, which is taken as having made up its mind. Turning
either multiplier by hand afterwards also leaves auto, permanently.

9990013d7da3ed918dca70b8.source: The strength of the force keeping the nodes placed to form a tree in place

c229bd616c49efe16577069a.source:
Lays a small graph out the way a person would draw it, and pins it there. Computed once
per change rather than simulated, so the same graph always gives the same picture.

9b70a45e93759bf8666f8e21.source:
Each connected component is laid out on its own, and the components are packed side by
side to fit the canvas at the largest zoom.

0e9c04aa6c032cc393d673bc.source:
Leaves of one type hanging off the same one or two nodes line up as a block, beside
the nodes they hang from.

2245d2a3ca7ca17379269765.source:
Everything else is placed so its distances follow the edges: a hub's neighbours come
out on a ring, a chain on a line.

edcefdc6da95c90d92097653.source: Nodes with no edge at all go in a tray beside the rest.

fa21796ad17dbfd0a4bb7c78.source: Meant for graphs of up to a few hundred nodes.

70c547937ada05b5cd99fc30.source:
How a block lines up. `'auto'` stands it across the line to the nodes it hangs from;
`'row'` and `'column'` force one way.

797b2e1742e1d5fda1ba57f6.source:
Clear space between two nodes, in graph units. An edge is drawn twice this long, and
components and the tray sit three times this apart.

8892cdb87f98d7e4fbcc9ad0.source:
The fewest leaves sharing a type and their neighbours that line up as a block; fewer
are placed one by one. A leaf has two neighbours at most.

1f849b9a46f495420125e2e2.source:
Move each floated label (see `textVerticalShift`) to the side of its node that its
edges leave free; a block's members all take the side away from the nodes they hang
from. The style still decides how far out the label sits.

1f6c4a39b833205771eb50db.source: Where the nodes with no edge go: under the rest, or to their right.

4b34cbdcafe7d914fcb8f64c.source:
Name of the `node.data` key holding the row the node should sit on, counting from
`0` at the shallowest root.

921b177014f060b3260f34f4.source:
Leave undefined — the default — and a node sits one row below its parent. Name a
key and each node that carries it is pushed down to the row it asks for, the gap
filled with empty rows. This is how the roots of a multi-tree graph are put on
different rows: give one of them a depth of `2` and its whole tree starts there.

5401cb779b858a813fd46a84.source:
A row can only ever push a node *further down*: a tidy tree cannot place a child
above its parent, so a depth that is not below the parent's is clamped to
