`parent + 1`. Empty rows take up real space, so a large depth on a shallow graph
squeezes every row — `levelSpacing` is the way back out.

4497dc728f9187e42d750c74.source: Name of the `node.data` key holding the id of the node's parent in the hierarchy.

f965b3341f419f3e647d265d.source:
Leave undefined — the default — and parenthood is derived from the edges, as it
always was. Name a key and each node that carries it is attached to the node it
names, whether or not an edge joins them; a branch declared without an edge is
drawn without a line. A key naming a node that is not being laid out, or one that
would close a cycle, is dropped for that node, which falls back to the edges.

80b9f2415d7c2addd1b39963.source:
Ignored while `rootId` is set: pinning a root re-derives every parent from the
edges, which is what makes the root picker able to re-hang a declared tree.

2b7907bda4c2f9f13f045636.source:
Specify the ID of the node to be used as the root of the tree.
Keep undefined to let `rooIdAlgorithmFinder` to select it.

15e86118347e280a7b1a8de8.source:
A fetched node awaiting triage. Not in the graph, not in the data table, not in
any facet count — until it is ingested.

78d401b828d19cc1415456ac.source: Already on canvas, so it cannot be ingested; the run still records its vouching.

83edbf7a5179acb1dc0e2bf6.source: The candidate's id, stringified — what dedup and rejection memory key on.

e3c19dd2ac9b333b49cef58e.source:
A candidate edge that is a triage row in its own right — both its endpoints are
already on canvas, so nothing else would stage it.

46c308a5984f9923e9dea2cd.source:
One `fetch`'s worth of candidates, held for triage. There is at most one set
per pivot id: a re-run replaces it.

837a46db06a3678efec543b5.source:
Edges that are not rows: they follow their endpoints and land iff both ends end
up on canvas. Not shown in triage — an edge to a node the analyst did not take
is not a decision of its own.

82258d452c75f5fd3100e383.source: How many of them are already on canvas.

0354816cc35f96d82911b68d.source: Edge-only results: both endpoints already on canvas, so they are rows of their own.

22317d6d08fc9d15212c97c5.source: Set when `fetch` rejected — the pane offers a retry.

1a9bed3399be709a42f5c530.source: How many nodes the provider returned, before dedup or suppression.

1b5d1fa4e02357b4f2459455.source: The narrowing this set was fetched with.

2344a9a670304a85d511d4d7.source:
A re-run of this pivot, waiting rather than replacing: it landed while rows
were marked, and throwing the analyst's triage away unasked is not a swap the
library gets to make. The surface announces it and offers both ways out —
[PivotManagerLike.showPending](PivotManagerLike.md#showpending) and
[PivotManagerLike.dismissPending](PivotManagerLike.md#dismisspending).

746302d6fb9ed21cf7957488.source: A re-run with nothing marked replaces outright, and never lands here.

c474b2f523bf874830b58983.source:
The run might still land without triage, so nothing here has been *offered* yet.
The set exists from the moment `fetch` starts — that is what makes the run
watchable and cancellable — but a surface must not put a provisional set in front
of the analyst: it is about to disappear onto the canvas, and taking the screen to
say so costs more than the result it is announcing.

80b9da878cb1590c938b0aa3.source:
Cleared the moment the run turns out to need triage, which is the surface's cue to
come forward. A run that was always going to stage is never provisional.

9a593c6ec33183819391bf53.source: Set when the provider blew through the absolute ceiling. Nothing was staged.

9fd2d88d3ebb5c4cf3ea5d7b.source: The id this set's first ingest will be recorded under.

e05dd179ccf0d9f1342db06b.source: How many were dropped because they were explicitly rejected earlier this session.

330cd31efba21c6016d95d6f.source:
Handed to both provider calls as the last argument. Extends
[RenderContext](../../AsyncContent/interfaces/RenderContext.md), so cancellation works the way it does everywhere else:
forward `signal` to `fetch`, or poll `isStale()` between steps.

2ecf508051086af48f38e173.source:
One runnable enrichment: what it is called, what it runs on, how to advertise
what is out there and how to fetch it.

a1839f69003ebd2ee7a1807d.source:
A pivot is two functions and some metadata. [PivotDefinition.summarize](#summarize)
is the cheap "what's out there" call whose facets become the narrowing
controls; [PivotDefinition.fetch](#fetch) is the real one. Results are
*candidates* — staged for triage, never on the canvas — unless the pivot
declares [PivotDefinition.autoIngest](#autoingest).

fecfd7bbe9da3587a7540cf1.source:
Whether this pivot applies to a given origin, and to how much of it. Re-read on
every origin change, so it must be synchronous and cheap. Omit it and the pivot
applies to everything. Not consulted when `origin` is `'none'`.

c89cbe48e31579164b6fee61.source:
Return a **boolean** for a rule about the origin as a whole — "only with two or
more picked", "never on a note". Return the **nodes it applies to** for a rule
that reads one node at a time, which is the normal case for enrichment: a
selection mixing a domain and an IP still offers the domain-only providers,
against the domain alone. An empty array means the same as `false`.

949cc7b9597c64afa0f007fc.source:
Whatever it keeps is the origin the provider is called with — `summarize` and
`fetch` never see a node this turned down.

2ad687bb693ef9a21aa1fad2.source:
Land results directly instead of staging them for triage. For small, trusted
results — expanding an event into its objects — not for anything an analyst
would want to pick through. The cap still applies.

88850fa97231c3e43b5eddae.source:
`true` and `false` are both answers, and both hold however the run was started.
Leaving it unset is *not* the same as `false`: it says the pivot has no view, so
a one-click run may decide on size alone — see
[PivotRunOptions.autoIngestUpTo](PivotRunOptions.md#autoingestupto). Runs made any other way still stage.

ec64f71498abfb3f944175a7.source:
Write each run the moment it lands, with no gesture. For a pivot whose results
are the source system's own data already — expanding an event into its
objects — where saving is an update rather than a decision.

258d39015e5fedcf92132774.source:
The save runs after the ingest resolves rather than inside it, so a slow
backend never holds up the canvas; its outcome is reported by the notifier.

c2f9b8fcb1a9b0fc77963621.source: The real fetch, narrowed by what the analyst chose.

801f123c509dc12dc09f61b5.source: SVG string, injected with innerHTML and not sanitised — it must be trusted.

1697790c2858549efe81df18.source: Stable identity: what the registry keys on, and the provenance tag written on ingest.

f8ce2726178fd7b4fc6d1579.source: Label, used verbatim (so it can be translated).

ac7e48b50012598764b11d0f.source:
Refuse to fetch while the advertised count exceeds this. A count the provider does
not know (`total: null`) is never refused. There is no library
default: a pivot that declares no cap is never gated by one (the absolute
ceiling of [PivotManagerLike.candidateCeiling](PivotManagerLike.md#candidateceiling) still applies to what
`fetch` returns).

aee199588df7aaf9e07cb827.source:
Choices for the context menu. With any, the pivot's row opens a submenu with one row
per choice, each running the pivot on the spot with that narrowing, and a last row
opening the pivot panel. Receives the nodes the pivot applies to. Synchronous and
cheap, like [appliesTo](#appliesto): it runs every time the menu opens.

31538eabe6866ff9b9bda60e.source: Return `[]`, or omit the hook, for a plain row that runs with no narrowing.

296eb9204099e6f95adaa651.source:
What this pivot runs on. `'selection'` pivots need an origin — the nodes the
analyst pointed at; `'none'` pivots need no nodes at all (search, import, a
staging tray) and receive `[]`.

444e3f87dd7d957ec9cd3641.source:
Write an ingested run's result back to the source system — the one half of the
contract that is not read-only.

83149fb1b547248d7a4aebd8.source:
Omit it and this pivot's results are *not savable*: they never enter the
ledger, are never counted unsaved, and no Save appears for them. A pivot over
derived data that could not be written anywhere should omit it rather than
declare one that fails.

e68fdfe60d2a6abd962f001a.source:
Never called by the library on its own — an explicit
[PivotManagerLike.save](PivotManagerLike.md#save), or [PivotDefinition.autoSave](#autosave). The
consumer performs the write; the library only asks for it and records the
answer.

2dc8db2bf903b485007e5259.source:
Cheap "what's out there". Called with `{}` before any narrowing exists, and
re-run as the origin or the narrowing changes; its facets become the narrowing
controls and its `total` is the number the cap is judged against.

46c7035e19e09911212f74d7.source:
Omit it and the pivot offers no advertised count and no narrowing — legal, but
then [PivotDefinition.fetch](#fetch) must be safe to call blind, since nothing
can gate it.

b29cbce78cc39bafd6826b38.source:
One narrowing control, declared by the provider and rendered by the library —
the same facet vocabulary the filter panel speaks.

c9621a36bd14a0b133d9595e.source:
What the provider does when this key is absent from the narrowing, drawn as the
facet's starting value and the value *Clear narrowing* returns to. A `multiselect`
takes the picked option values, a `select` one value, a `boolean` true or false.
The key is still left out of the narrowing while the facet holds its default, so
the provider must treat "absent" as this value. An emptied `multiselect` with a
default is sent as `[]`, meaning *none*.

654f82ed33ed6bfd4bfd8364.source: For `select` / `multiselect`. A `count` is shown beside the option when given.

4b530f9eaaa72158860a8e95.source:
The shape [Graph.pivots](../../../../classes/Pivotick.md#pivots) exposes. Declared as an interface so the
consumer-facing surface is documented in one place and the implementation can
stay internal.

cdba8be21ab1906d8451717b.source:
How many pivots apply to one node — what the `'summary'` rim badge counts. Held
between graph changes, so it is cheap to ask per node per render.

5bcb7aa11800f5d111bd304d.source: Abort in-flight calls — one pivot's or all, and optionally only one kind.

18e806691e237a4a450fe673.source:
The id the source system assigned this element when it was saved, when it
assigned one. The element keeps its own id — re-keying reaches into edges,
clusters, selection, the query engine and the history — so
`graph.getNode(canonicalId)` still misses and this is the read that does not.

53ed185bd749ca681235811e.source: Drop a waiting re-run and keep triaging what is on show.

b697f915d5b61357f04744c9.source: What applies to this origin. An empty origin yields the origin-less pivots.

ecc002d43ee894458b3f8312.source: Whether this element belongs to a run whose pivot can write it anywhere.

ee635ebe2c9c2b4358657a12.source: Written to the source system. `false` for the unsaved *and* the not-savable.

efc98f03e3b3d08d75241062.source:
How much of `nodes` one pivot applies to — the origin it would actually be run
with. Empty when it does not apply at all, and always empty for an origin-less
pivot. What a surface reads to say "3 of the 5 you picked".

963067c65572460f64813709.source:
Write ingested runs back to their source systems. Runs go one at a time, and a
run whose pivot declares no `save` is never among them.

df5578a5d171fa0214bb37e4.source: Each run is sent only what is still unsaved, so a retry is the same call.

b39c334a79c27475921678ac.source:
A run id for one run, a pivot id for every unsaved run of that
pivot, a [PivotSaveSelection](PivotSaveSelection.md) for just those elements, or nothing for
all of them.

5be8813c4de392ea1b0a6040.source:
`interactive: true` when an analyst asked for the save, so
[PivotSaveContext.promptData](PivotSaveContext.md#promptdata) can open its modal.

3574e721edb5a284a3279138.source: Promote a waiting re-run to the set on show.

ee5f92aa0084a76da92179d4.source:
What a Save would send, exact rather than advisory. Narrowed to one pivot's
runs when given an id — what a triage pane's own line counts.

80bc38d2daa38c36222c3a13.source: Absolute ceiling on what one `fetch` may stage. Refuses rather than truncates.

8aa4df7c2cc7e23613165bc8.source:
How many new candidates a one-click pivot lands without triage — what
the UI manager's `quickPivot` passes as [PivotRunOptions.autoIngestUpTo](PivotRunOptions.md#autoingestupto).
A run made any other way is unaffected.

52da4158865f8518b5181e70.source: One row of a pivot's context-menu submenu. See [PivotDefinition.menuChoices](PivotDefinition.md#menuchoices).

9cd0e890dd7229c37968f078.source: What the pivot is run with, and what the panel opens on if the run is capped.

ccfcaa8470c0eae6fd581acb.source:
Why a run was refused. A refusal always carries the number, the limit and
therefore the way forward — nothing is ever silently truncated or sampled.

a0dacf53dbac573f17a31d0e.source: `'cap'` — the advertised count exceeded the pivot's `maxCandidates`, so nothing was fetched. `'ceiling'` — `fetch` returned more than the absolute ceiling, so nothing was staged.

6ca2ecc58fb7f578274d1a35.source:
A rejection the session is holding, as a surface can show it. The row is kept
alongside the id it keys on: the memory outlives the run that carried it, and a
list of bare ids is not something a rejection can be reconsidered from.

974adf61baf2f6f0b217fb7a.source: The candidate id the rejection keys on — what suppresses it on the next run.

ba42b501b8508a27fab807a9.source: The row's `data.label`, or its id when it had none: the name the table gave it.

8bb14a350c4287d2f425f5dd.source: The row exactly as the provider returned it. An edge row can be rejected too.

aeb92bba7bf46c11a9c84cff.source:
One ingest's rows, kept so undoing it can put them back rather than asking the
provider for them a second time — which matters most when the alternative is
refetching two thousand correlations through a rate-limited API.

f035536f7dfddc2ad360be8c.source:
Costs little: the candidate wrappers point at the same raws the run already holds,
and the record dies with its entry when the history evicts it.

6edf8c93c8081eef7a2eb198.source: Enough of the set's identity to rebuild it, if the ingest emptied and closed it.

113c847f724baa4bcce61f1e.source: Each row with the index it sat at, so it goes back in place rather than at the end.

2a7735e7ac64435bd6127cea.source:
A flat graph fragment. No returned node names an existing on-canvas parent —
nesting travels in `RawNode.children`. An edges-only result is legal: edges
whose endpoints are all already on canvas become triage rows of their own.

73a37a18acbc20daf1dd5aed.source:
One ingest, undoable as a unit. Holds the raw payload as well as the ids, so
redo re-lands the recorded delta without refetching or re-gating.

3367b91b9d9cd4d2408d87c9.source:
Nodes this run added *inside* a container: a new container's own subtree, and
children merged into a container already on canvas. Undone before the
top-level nodes, so nothing is left orphaned in the graph.

6b4465a7a2f33c8cef3fe8f7.source:
The nodes the pivot was run on. Empty for an origin-less pivot, and what a
save payload carries as "which event does this attach to".

c7a672af45cabd7781957a2b.source:
What this ingest took out of the staged set. Only the newest ingest is ever
re-staged, so this is a record of what *could* be restored rather than a
promise that it will be.

74883513f71f190ed246f122.source:
How many of this run's elements have been written to the source system —
nodes, children and edges together. A surface reads it to warn *before* an
undo rather than after: undo takes things off the canvas and issues no
compensating write, so what was saved stays saved upstream.

30d5bd939eb9a795e15e5c96.source: Children merged into a node already on canvas, so redo can merge them again.

247e7ab6c5fd7d2427e48032.source: Elements already on canvas that this run vouched for without adding.

bb0e7b8808f4490c83e9c67c.source: What a caller can say about one run beyond its origin and its narrowing.

753fe7ae3e315c4a7cdaac68.source:
Land the results with no triage when this many candidates or fewer are new to
the canvas — the deal a one-click pivot makes: no counts to read and nothing to
narrow, so size decides. Deduped candidates do not count towards it; edge-only
rows do, because they are rows an analyst would otherwise have been asked about.

c18abc8df205399ac3183c3e.source:
Only consulted where the pivot left [PivotDefinition.autoIngest](PivotDefinition.md#autoingest) unset. A
pivot that declared it either way has already answered the question, and its
answer holds however the run was started.

64cba4dd83b4451aee796c29.source: Candidates dropped because they were already on canvas.

b02da423148d846b709482fd.source:
This run's identity in the provenance records — the handle for
`graph.history`, whose pivot entries are keyed by it. A staged run's later
ingest announces itself under this same id; a *second*, partial ingest out of
one staged set gets a fresh id of its own, so each batch is separately
undoable.

832177e5941029b5fb04531f.source: Candidates suppressed because they were explicitly rejected earlier this session.

04a665772933344622a6e42c.source:
Handed to [PivotDefinition.save](PivotDefinition.md#save) as the last argument. Mirrors
[PivotContext](PivotContext.md) minus the narrowing concerns.

8ccc7f6e231b94d448aceb0b.source:
`signal` is here so a write can be forwarded like any other request, but the
library never aborts it except when the graph is destroyed: cancelling a write
mid-flight leaves nobody knowing what happened, which is worse than waiting.

2b3a26094e07006fca873834.source:
Ask the analyst for something before writing, in the library's own modal: a
declarative form (`fields`) or custom HTML (`render` + `getValues`), titled
and submitted with *Save* unless told otherwise. Resolves to the values, or `null` on cancel.

ff7ae9cf1736d1bf01b2fcf3.source:
A save nobody clicked ([PivotDefinition.autoSave](PivotDefinition.md#autosave), or
[PivotManagerLike.save](PivotManagerLike.md#save) called without `interactive`) gets `null` at once,
with nothing drawn. Return `{ cancelled: true }` after a `null` to leave the run
pending with no toast.

19607a2cf3ff6a74fc167935.source:
Someone clicked for this save, so the save may ask them something. The
library's own Save buttons and the toast's Retry pass `true`.

4af82ab34f141af7039ba521.source:
What the consumer is asked to write. Live graph objects rather than raw
fragments, so the payload carries whatever the graph has made of them.

5f007ee3e3f5743819b7d0a9.source:
A retry carries only what is still unsaved, which is why this is built fresh per
attempt rather than kept with the run.

c9e4318155ef0ee7eb83f339.source: 1 on the first attempt, incremented by each retry.

874a693af460f63694937fc1.source:
Nodes this run added *inside* a container, flattened. Each one's container is
reachable through [Node.parentNode](../../../../classes/Node.md#parentnode), so a payload can be grouped by
parent without a second traversal.

8cb8a2cb07176d65e2716409.source: Top-level nodes this run created and that are still unsaved.

546a0288faf3c9448b17475f.source: The nodes the pivot was run on — "which event does this attach to".

54279a4895da9a803eed85f1.source:
Already on canvas before this run: vouched for, not created. Context only —
writing these is the job of the run that produced them.

67228e9415d73a8cec810f3e.source:
Every count here is **exact**, unlike the advisory ones a provider advertises:
this is a ledger of what the library asked for and was told, not an estimate.

d694296937f5babdf130068a.source: Runs whose save reported `{ cancelled: true }`: left as they were, not failed.

c480ff5d8e70cf4e8c9ab8e2.source: Still unsaved after this attempt — what a retry would send.

a0310bee75b6785aa010f22c.source: How many runs were attempted, not counting a cancelled one.

85df7f5082a713465fe9098f.source:
Part of what the runs landed, for [PivotManagerLike.save](PivotManagerLike.md#save): say, the nodes an
analyst selected.

af215773f2d3a9a18aee1335.source:
Each run that created a named element is asked once, with a payload narrowed to
what was named: the named nodes, the pending children under them, the named edges,
and each pending edge from a named node whose other end is named too or will not be
left unwritten (the origin, a node already saved). Anything else stays pending,
and named elements no savable run is still waiting on are ignored.

a8860c44da0c12f82ca1f91d.source:
Every count here is **advisory**. It legitimately differs from what ingest
lands — dedup is the common case — and a shrink is never an error.

b065b32e81fed40f81c42ad8.source: Optional breakdown; each entry becomes one narrowing control.

3ab71ae96b43626ee2856871.source: Advisory total. Render it as approximate.

c68316e90dab13b73ede73f4.source:
`null` or left out means the provider does not know, which is not the same claim as
`0`. No count is drawn for it, and [PivotDefinition.maxCandidates](PivotDefinition.md#maxcandidates) is not judged
on it: only [PivotManagerLike.candidateCeiling](PivotManagerLike.md#candidateceiling) bounds what the fetch returns.

3276901d55280eb8f33ec43d.source:
One run's vouching for one element. Kept internally so two runs of the same
pivot stay distinguishable — undoing one is built on it —
while the public surface stays `getSources(): string[]`.

11dce58edf3d2305e00d4f48.source:
The facet types narrowing may use: everything the query engine knows except
`regex`, which a backend cannot be asked to evaluate. The triage pane's own
client-side filters keep the full vocabulary.

a7bf9e8595fc85d45eacfe40.source:
The analyst's narrowing choices, keyed by facet key. Passed to both provider
calls verbatim; the library never interprets a value.

b6a10f6d7d7d818f6b2c9ca3.source:
What the library draws on a node's rim for its pivots. See
`GraphOptions.pivotRimBadge`.

aea17eebcaab45596cfc72be.source: When the pivot rim badges are drawn. See `GraphOptions.pivotRimBadgeVisible`.

dbf46be30197685db0793106.source:
`void` or `true` means everything in the payload was written; `false` means none
of it. An object reports a partial write — **anything not named is treated as
still unsaved**, so a save that names nothing saved nothing. Throwing is
equivalent to `false`, with the error surfaced in the retry toast.

611b8e2e662e70349bc6faad.source:
Ids naming an element this run did not create are ignored: a pivot never writes
what it did not produce, so it cannot report it written either.

fb5a29100cb1edbed71d3ccf.source:
The analyst backed out, typically of [PivotSaveContext.promptData](../interfaces/PivotSaveContext.md#promptdata).
Nothing is recorded, no toast is shown, the attempt does not count, and a
save over several runs stops here. Every other field is ignored.

436278883b3c80d23e0af0a7.source: Ids the source system assigned, keyed by the local id.

cc82d3d232b4594f40aefff5.source: Shown verbatim in the result toast — why the rest did not save.

0da90b6ee176300150e2b473.source:
Taken at face value, including for an edge whose endpoints did not save:
what the source system says it wrote is not the library's to second-guess.

2d9919306e10f8b9eb249f14.source:
What vouches for an element the analyst drew by hand. It is a source like any
other, so `graph.removeBySource('manual')` reaches hand-drawn work and undoing a
creation removes the element only when nothing else still vouches for it.

c0abb38fd294040908e6615b.source:
A hand-created node therefore reports `['manual']` from `getSources()`, not
`['seed']`.

77b2005c0bba4a7fb5400351.source: Every element with no pivot vouching for it is vouched for by the seed.

d53bd835deac31e23f9b1760.source:
The key a potential declared for no particular pivot is held under — what
`node.setPotential(count)` writes and the `'summary'` rim badge reads.

d90a626c78cf450ceed1e4f0.source:
Exported so a consumer clearing declarations by hand can name it; the one-argument
`setPotential` is the way to write it.

80a6fb50f32217213c6a5381.source:
Represents a node with a custom SVG path.
The `d` property corresponds directly to the `d` attribute of an SVG `<path>` element,
allowing fully custom shapes.

6fcee44cffa3e8bf77e7398c.source:
Whether the dash should be animated (e.g., animation moving along the path)
@default: true

749a3bbc7054bb261272136e.source: Which end marker should the edge use

c872c6558768503190a6d4a7.source: Which start marker should the edge use

b6bc3846f29a90c7485c0765.source: Keeps labels horizontally aligned to the viewport

14cc54dd2e7445b774312af5.source: Callback to dynamically override style properties based on the edge.

1adda9182d1a6e407142ce1b.source:
Where it sits depends on which style block declares it. On an **edge's own**
style it wins outright, and `edgeStyleMap` is skipped entirely. On
`render.defaultEdgeStyle` it is the computed form of the default slot: it fills
only what neither the edge nor `edgeStyleMap` set (and what a per-edge `styleCb`
left out), and its result still loses to both.

d6562b341361d413b71d9477.source: Runs once per edge per render, so keep it cheap.

ed6e8b4c3ef1938841183a4c.source: Callback executed during the init phase, before the first rendering

a54d48307764ecc54d524365.source: The default edge style to be applied on all nodes

00d3adc1302039d3c3510285.source: The default edge's label style to be applied on all nodes

a82667f5c93d6edc1bf07a7f.source: The default node style to be applied on all nodes

823e58c23e40c190b3380674.source:
How long, in milliseconds, a drawing takes to fade into or out of the graph as the zoom
changes what is worth drawing. `0` makes every such change in a single frame, which is
what a graph declaring no transition does.

6d6c717293ac120af5ef9fe5.source:
It covers a node swapping between its [NodeStyle.tiers](NodeStyle.md#tiers), its
[NodeStyle.focusTier](NodeStyle.md#focustier) drawing arriving and leaving, and a label crossing
[GraphRendererOptions.minLabelFontSize](#minlabelfontsize). An outgoing drawing is kept alive on a
layer of its own and the two fade past each other, so a node is never absent mid-swap —
only briefly softer where they overlap.

0ef1f7d5fc38fe2bcab12f3f.source:
Every node on screen crosses a threshold at the same moment, so this starts as many
fades as there are nodes changing. `prefers-reduced-motion` turns it off.

c0f7a2e866879643ef750a90.source:
Measured on 210 nodes each holding a 140x44 card: the fade itself costs nothing — the
canvas holds 60fps for its whole length — but keeping that many outgoing cards alive
for an instant adds about 26ms to the one frame the crossing already spends. Set it to
`0` on a graph where that frame matters more than the transition.

a46f5f4c1dee347063c83a70.source: Maps edge kinds to their styles.

7d789a0f5284803c88271a0d.source:
Each key is an edge kind (as returned by `edgeTypeAccessor`) and maps to a
partial `EdgeStyle`. An edge's own `styleCb` still wins over the map, exactly
as it does over [nodeStyleMap](#nodestylemap).

e07f91c39e792dacdee37b5c.source:
Function to access the kind of an edge — the dimension [edgeStyleMap](#edgestylemap)
keys on, and the one an `edge` legend section and edge filter facets derive
from when they aren't given a data key of their own.

0985d9e6526dd0dedb1266fa.source: Controls whether non-connected nodes and edges are grayed out when a node is selected

812352b18dda817ed10612a6.source:
Controls whether nodes can be expanded or collapsed to show their children.
`false` also drops the chevron, the `Enter` shortcut and the dashed collapsed outline.

848e881e2c6af774527592cc.source:
The node a fit held at [minFitScale](#minfitscale) centres on, by id; a folded node's group
stands in for it. The view stops at the content's edges, so an anchor near one sits
near that side of the canvas. Unset, or not drawn, the fit centres on the content.

8cb77da249fd1ba0159c9768.source:
When a node's [NodeStyle.focusTier](NodeStyle.md#focustier) drawing fires. The style says what the focus
drawing is; this says when.

69a984ae5a3df2b2ae86a41b.source:
Selection only promotes a node that is selected on its own — a box-select of fifty
would be a wall of overlapping cards. `'off'` suppresses the behaviour without editing
the style, which is what an integrator embedding someone else's preset needs.

683434a9ffe4737927464dfa.source:
What the chip over an open group shows, in place of its label. A string is shown as
text. The chip keeps its close mark and still folds the group back when clicked.
Return nothing to keep the label.

b81e1093b951b7c42de88720.source:
The look of a group made by `UI.simplify`, layered over the default: a disc in the
type's colour inside a ring, the count on the disc once there is room, the label
below. A group is drawn as a node, so `tiers`, `focusTier`, `html`, `shape` and
`badges` work as they do on one. Return nothing to keep the default.

72051a1aced467f8396d632b.source:
`base` is the style the library would draw. What you return replaces its keys, so
to keep the count on the disc while adding a tier, spread `base.tiers`.

4f726d7e82e52c3f31b47065.source: Defines custom styles for marker shapes used in the graph.

854c39947b59496b3d54dc87.source: Each key is a marker type (e.g., `'diamond'`, `'arrow'`) and maps to a `MarkerStyle` object.

c85ccf2a3fa247f9ce548308.source:
The lowest scale a fit zooms out to. Content that would need less is shown at this
scale, centred on [fitAnchor](#fitanchor), and runs past the canvas edges. Unset, a fit
always shows everything. An explicit scale passed to `fitAndCenter` ignores it.

8f2b1968166d0f083c6e2764.source: The rendered font size, in CSS pixels, below which a label is not drawn.

36817b26f76dcd8e1106f534.source:
A label rides the graph and scales with it, so past a certain zoom it is text nobody
can read — and on a graph large enough to open zoomed out, every label at once. Below
this size the library draws none of them, which also takes them out of the pass that
repositions a label on every simulation tick.

7502c97121315d4bf627c8fc.source:
One number for the whole canvas: an edge's label and a node's alike. The difference
between them falls out of the font size already, since a node's label is derived from
its size — a big node keeps its label longer than a small one.

f32adccbe22b66a2795bf679.source: `0` draws every label at every zoom.

6feefd1253016f1ff160ba91.source: Maps node types to their styles.

797a87c5afaef05dd80c0e9e.source: Each key is a node type (as returned by `nodeTypeAccessor`) and maps to a `NodeStyle` object.

7bc359e8ae5eda867480bf68.source: Function to access the type of a node. Used in

d0809e0f5ca2fdecdc0e7961.source: Used to style nodes based on their type.

5dd74ddb58edd37fc82f68b9.source:
Allows full control over how a cluster is displayed
The function can return either:

50f7fd2df31cffdf2d217b51.source: An `HTMLElement` to be used as the cluster, or

ed036f7e10c28d4397fae4eb.source: A string to render inside the cluster

80de4f0bca0f397db1408372.source:
Allows full control over how edge labels are displayed.
The function can return either:

191300a0579e25a736e5c40c.source: An `HTMLElement` to be used as the edge's label, or

b7f41b33baf6b13f430913c6.source: A string to render inside the label

5c772043dafad1e4bbd7a256.source:
Allows full control over how a node is displayed
The function can return either:

63bc4d0c4715f1e420c3308a.source: An `HTMLElement` to be used as the node,

f8e40eebf5eb7043cea50aba.source: A string to render inside the node, or

a86737109a7600cf42c9da19.source: nothing, to leave that node to the normal styling pipeline

a3496001af551ff97faed165.source:
A card returned here **is** the node: no shape, icon, picture or label is drawn
behind it, and its measured size drives the collision radius and edge anchors.
Returning nothing for a node instead gives it its `nodeStyleMap` entry, shape and
label as usual — so this can card a few nodes rather than all of them.

eec3fda2c203bd9ad1646c52.source:
For a card that composes with the rest of the styling chain, declare
[NodeStyle.html](NodeStyle.md#html) with `shape: 'none'` instead; it resolves per type or per
node, where this one is global.

5a94d351125921ba0a6ab8fb.source: Defines the rendering method used by the graph.

bdc4a3756c01766d2b270cac.source:
Callback to dynamically override label style properties based on the edge. On an
edge's own label style it wins outright; on `render.defaultLabelStyle` it fills
only what the edge's own label style left unset.

89950a9a10df0ccd0ede96e2.source: Define the styling of an Edge marker.

32d2f8ed0d1fecad421a1e53.source: A small indicator pinned to a node's rim — what KeyLines and ReGraph call a *glyph*.

8ee034025737f5c4dcb965cd.source:
Badges are a decoration channel of their own, so a node can carry a fact that `color`,
`shape`, `size`, `iconClass` and `imagePath` are already spent on. They describe **only the
node they sit on**: a collapsed cluster does not aggregate its children's badges — walk
`node.children` yourself if you want that.

8b3a19a69697efa9100982c8.source: Called when the badge is clicked, before InterractionCallbacks.onBadgeClick.

7c6040a1922c5da180fc4def.source:
Declaring it makes the badge take the pointer cursor and **consume** the click, so the
node is not also selected. A badge without one stays transparent to the node underneath.
Pressing a badge still drags the node either way.

100894b6775fbca187e257f5.source:
Which corner to sit on. Omit it and the badge is auto-placed in the first free corner,
clockwise from `'ne'`. An explicit position is honoured **verbatim**, even where that
overlaps another badge or the expand affordance.

53f20c348b98b393b5dc6709.source: Inline SVG markup, sanitized before it reaches the DOM.

13c609bfcac0d937580d2039.source:
A count, or one or two characters. Longer text grows the badge into a pill; past three
characters it renders as `99+`. Takes precedence over any icon on the same badge.

930ef8314df275db743d9866.source: Native tooltip, rendered as a real `<title>`. Does not suppress the graph's own tooltip.

6a923e97fcaa6e72bebd69a0.source:
Small indicators pinned to the node's rim, independent of every other channel —
see [NodeBadge](NodeBadge.md).

ee7716aed3d77805dba32122.source:
Resolved like any other channel: the narrowest declaration wins outright rather than
merging, so a node's own `badges` **replaces** whatever `nodeStyleMap` or
`defaultNodeStyle` gave it. An empty array is the way to say "this one wears none";
`undefined` renders no badge group at all.

6d79e7f3d4d6dacf1971d7b1.source:
Four fit on a plain node, two on one with children (the expand affordance reserves the
East corners). Anything beyond that collapses into a `+n` badge naming the rest.

ae0f05c61f46bb01d9353917.source: The main color of the node

025a65af431cefb05f90e926.source:
The drawing used while this node is hovered, or selected on its own — whatever the
zoom. This is where a node says everything about itself.

3a3469c86bf0d9f76bdd6185.source:
It merges over the resolved *base* style rather than over the active tier, so a chip
tier's `shape` or `html` cannot leak into it, and it holds a constant size on screen
however far the graph is zoomed out. It never changes the node's geometry: edges keep
landing on the tier underneath and nothing moves.

5512512db68fec90872e6f56.source: When it fires is [GraphRendererOptions.focusTierTrigger](GraphRendererOptions.md#focustiertrigger)'s to say.

6f95413fad6bb7fbb508bba5.source:
The index into [tiers](#tiers) from which [focusTier](#focustier) stops firing. While the node
is drawn at that tier or a richer one, hover and a lone selection leave it as it is,
for a focus drawing that the zoom tier already shows. Unset, the focus drawing fires
at every tier. Ignored on a node with no `tiers`.

753a924303db473f1a774f87.source: The html to be used inside the node as an `SVGForeignObject` element.

8a59daf92c56ae5344129791.source:
Resolved like every other channel, so a card can be declared at any level —
`nodeStyleMap[type].html` gives one kind of node a card while the rest keep their
shapes, and a single node's own style overrides that. Returning nothing draws no
card, so one callback can card some nodes and leave the others alone.

c9c42e3ad2575da10b388bf3.source:
Pair it with `shape: 'none'` for a card that **is** the node. Otherwise the shape is
still drawn behind it, and `size` is the smallest the node can be.

3493a58b0086e5e12af0a278.source:
The card is measured and the node grows to it, so it is never clipped and edges land
on its border. You do not have to make the returned element self-sizing — it is
measured inside a shrink-to-fit box, so `width: 100%` resolves against its own
content rather than against the placeholder.

1d2e5ea09ff944d313e88a9e.source:
**Trusted HTML only.** Whatever this returns is inserted as-is, so build it with
`textContent` (or escape it) rather than interpolating node data into a markup string.

77e4326fe9714af97753988f.source:
How an `imagePath` picture sits on the node's shape. Resolvable per node so
different nodes can mix modes (e.g. screenshots `'cover'`, other attachments `'icon'`).

afc9d263f667e8baafe32f34.source:
URL of a picture to draw on the node. Restricted to the `http:`, `https:`, `data:` and
`blob:` schemes; anything else is ignored. Rendering it fetches the URL.

57baa019f42a613b906bf3e3.source:
The half-width of the box this node reserves for itself in the layout, in graph units.
This is the only size the simulation ever sees: set it and the drawing no longer drives
the collision radius, so a node can change how it is drawn without moving anything.

9f30dfec186594e507243931.source:
Leave it unset and the drawing owns the spacing, as it always has — a shape spaces by
its `size`, an HTML card by what it measures.

4e98c17e586e0e1f985ffcb1.source: half the widest declared tier `width`, or unset when there are no tiers

a95ac3259319b36b842d271c.source: The shape of the node, either a standard shape or a custom SVG path

60bf304c1fc7c6f6fd5aa008.source: Callback to dynamically override style properties based on the node.

ce1727b2cad9c1ab2180a88f.source:
Where it sits depends on which style block declares it. On a **node's own**
style it wins outright, and `nodeStyleMap` is skipped entirely. On
`render.defaultNodeStyle` it is the computed form of the default slot: it fills
only what neither the node nor `nodeStyleMap` set (and what a per-node `styleCb`
left out), and its result still loses to both.

2f9d0a3cec124f4ce1d6dbe0.source: Runs once per node per render, so keep it cheap.

437d8e3123eef6ff38e193ec.source:
Inline SVG markup drawn inside the node. Sanitized before it reaches the DOM (scripting
and event handlers are stripped), but a remote `<image href>` inside it is still fetched
when the node renders — see the security guide.

68d5484cc5a4078df6bc7f50.source: The text to be used inside the node as an `SVGText` element

1055f1965be585dbad387664.source:
Font size of the node's label, in graph units (CSS pixels at zoom 1). The label's
offset, its built-in character budget and the zoom gate all follow it.

ebbdbc71031e8834a6f1e15b.source:
The horizontal shift applied to the node's label position.
A value of 0 means it is centered to the node, a value of 1 is east of the node, -1 is west of the node.
Other values are also accepted, e.g., 0.5 would be halfway between the center and the east of the node.

6a6f7ba5a3b0ead7d058e4b5.source:
Widest a node label may be drawn, in graph units (CSS pixels at zoom 1). A longer label
is shortened with a middle ellipsis to fit. Replaces the built-in budget, which is sized
to the node. Ignored when `textTruncate` is `false`.

9813bc4f4b12e327bce79ef6.source:
Rotation degree applied to the node's label.
Positive values rotate clockwise, negative values rotate counter-clockwise.

d48d116452449c475a7fd2a1.source:
Shorten an over-wide label with a middle ellipsis (`head…tail`); `false` draws it
in full, on a themed pill where it spills past the node.

62b413fcdb34f20d1f663c15.source:
The vertical shift applied to the node's label position.
A value of 0 means it is centered to the node, a value of 1 is north of the node, -1 is south of the node.
Other values are also accepted, e.g., 0.5 would be halfway between the center and the north of the node.

cbaa544b72d86fa72e8f2c77.source:
Alternative drawings of this node, chosen by how large it currently renders — a glyph
on an overview, a labelled chip once there is room for one, a card once there is room
for that. Ordered smallest first; the richest one that fits wins, and the base style is
the floor when none do.

71c69e3ec6f24ddb59feee95.source:
The node's footprint never changes with the drawing (see [layoutSize](#layoutsize)), so
swapping tiers moves nothing.

f54e012fc5c9902da20cf134.source: One drawing of a node, and the size at which it takes over. See [NodeStyle.tiers](NodeStyle.md#tiers).

dbbb63a552a28ab1027940fa.source: Rendered footprint in CSS pixels at which this tier takes over, i.e. `footprint x zoom`.

cd49d59a5c4616d9d503a399.source:
Defaults to [width](#width), which reads as "engage once there is room for this drawing".
That is exact for the widest tier, which then appears at its design size at zoom 1; a
narrower tier engages earlier and is drawn proportionally smaller, so set this by hand
if an intermediate tier should appear at the size it was drawn at.

ea333e71eb7d15a84c9bd7b8.source: Merged over the resolved base style while this tier is active.

c6acda0bb0412962d2f2017c.source:
The box this drawing is designed to fill, in graph units. Declared rather than
measured: it sets the node's footprint and this tier's default threshold before
anything is drawn, so the layout never has to wait for a measurement.

52612e90f0e0fe0a11b8089e.source:
Region selection — dragging a shape across the canvas to select what it covers:
the marquee on the canvas, and the Select ▸ Lasso tool that draws a freehand one.
`enabled: false` takes both away, leaving click and shift-click selection.

5fe756bcd456f6a1c9de5196.source: 'straight': The edge will go in a straight line from A to B

028e0e7d56e1d829f819b5b7.source: 'curved': The edge will always be curved from A to B

a0d87efb841eb36d6b60ff2c.source: 'bidirectional': The edge will be curved only if there is a birectional relation between A and B. So, from A to B and B to A

951e990fce8218e7460e8012.source: How an `imagePath` picture sits on the node's shape.

bb86ba67a644520a7511de80.source: `'icon'` — small picture centred on the shape (~1.2× size); the legacy default look.

da3ff89a53231e73ee656613.source: `'cover'` — picture fills the shape's box (2× size), cropped to preserve aspect ratio.

003318c7d56096dc2a06c536.source: `'contain'` — whole picture fits inside the shape's box (2× size), letterboxed with the shape `color`.

c04580e6a67990e44b2b6b9a.source:
`'frame'` — the node becomes a rectangle sized to the picture's own aspect ratio
(longest side = 2× size), so the stroke hugs it: whole picture, no crop, no letterbox
bars. The requested `shape` is ignored (always a rectangle) since the picture is the node.

94233d15596f969834f48e55.source: A map of all available edge marker styles.

db72fc22502484dffbf02f32.source:
Custom markers can be added here and referenced by `markerStart` or `markerEnd`
in [EdgeStyle](../interfaces/EdgeStyle.md).

73627e96bd9d146002fea793.source: Which corner of the node's rim a badge sits on.

99feb54e3b138d376fefa507.source:
The expand/collapse affordance owns `'ne'` when a node is collapsed and `'se'` when it is
expanded, so on a node with children **both** are reserved and auto-placement skips them —
otherwise badges would swap corners every time the cluster opened.

a1c1c55bb8116664226d5dd4.source:
What a tier is allowed to change: the drawing, never the chain or the geometry. Omitting
`styleCb` and `tiers` keeps the type from recursing; omitting `layoutSize` is what makes
a tier swap free of any effect on the layout.

ec978015c1927d4b7a8786f1.source:
The drawing is one slot: naming any of `iconUnicode`, `iconClass`, `svgIcon`, `imagePath`
or `html` replaces the base's drawing (and its `imageFit`) outright. Every other channel is
inherited unless named.

8312218982badad73acdb946.source:
A channel set to `null` is **taken away** rather than left to the style underneath, which
`undefined` cannot express, since omitting a channel only means "I am not naming it". This
is the one layer with that power: everywhere else in the chain `null` still falls through,
because a `styleCb` handing back a null straight out of node data is an ordinary shape and
has always meant "use the default".

331f5996237c1e29e3f0d2f6.source:
Clearing `shape` is not how a node is made shapeless — use `shape: 'none'`, which says the
content is the node.

a9b794273d282322d4973bdc.source: `'canvas'` - Reserved; not implemented (the renderer factory throws for it)

60bdb95317d708ca2afe4b95.source:
Represents one of the predefined, common node shapes.
These can be rendered using basic SVG elements like `<circle>`, `<rect>`, or `<polygon>`.

5b8611d359d52ea9f864f78a.source:
`'none'` draws no shape at all: whatever [NodeStyle.html](../interfaces/NodeStyle.md#html) (or an icon, a picture or
a label) puts on the node *is* the node, and the node's collision radius and edge anchors
come from that content rather than from `size`. The node stays selectable and draggable
over its whole extent.

4e377bd6d72078b53e190cb7.source:
Fold chains that hang off a node alone: a node whose only link is from its parent, and
so on down. Nodes leading chains of the same shape fold together, and so does each level
of their chains. An event with thirty files, each holding its own hash, becomes one group
of files linked to one group of hashes. Links count downstream only.

25a2ed5de348a10098dbc855.source: Fewer matching nodes than this stay plain nodes. Between 2 and 50.

a69dd8099d91a7c591ce46ac.source:
Fold whole neighbourhoods into a few groups: communities of densely linked nodes, found
with the Leiden algorithm, at a level from fine (1) to coarse (7). Only offered when
declared. Computed off the page in the compute worker when one can start; meanwhile the
previous grouping stays. A group may mix types.

fa8211d0c1f24334d008a32b.source: From 1, many small communities, to 7, a handful of large ones.

4b6bd87d08ac772f9acda087.source: `false` finds the communities on the page instead of in a worker.

a5f712afad55a0f9840d748d.source: A rule of the app's own.

a0a4ee172d09ed1a36c12095.source: One line on its card saying what it folds.

05edbb942288163aff7cf608.source: The name on its card in the Simplify flyout.

3c1d3005ccd7566b40991558.source: Fewer nodes sharing a key than this stay plain nodes.

6e155a6ae7c38d693529bca5.source:
Give each node to group a key; nodes sharing a key become one group. A node left out
stays itself, and ids that are not in `view.nodes` are ignored. A rule that throws is
switched off and the others still run.

73e6d95a08f0e3a6863a760b.source:
Fold nodes with few links into the nodes they hang from: a hub's leaves become one
"N more" on the hub. A group may mix types and may hold a single node.

bd79bda03a92d8c31188099a.source: Nodes with fewer drawn links than this fold. Between 1 and 10.

00b9c90c6b9f6ca9c5e44247.source:
The drawn graph as one rule sees it: what the node filters let through, with the groups
made by the rules before it standing in for their members. Read-only.

887cecfe98d969b216466657.source: The group behind this node, when it is one made by an earlier rule.

ff46f7f4fdc331eedc3924b6.source: The drawn nodes with a line to this one.

398f2fb32b894d6a73280501.source: The drawn nodes this one has a line to.

6872b17254fce07bf5a1a861.source: The type the rule groups by: its own `typeOf`, else `UI.simplify.typeOf`, else `render.nodeTypeAccessor`.

9178bacfff58658fa5e9a54a.source:
The nodes this rule may group. Annotated nodes, nodes pulled out of a group and
expanded clusters are left out; groups from earlier rules are in.

cb41105878adbb78a88536a1.source:
A group drawn by [simplification](SimplifyOptions.md): nodes folded into one dot on
the canvas. View state only — `graph.getNodes()`, the table, export and history see
the members, never the group.

19128aa7fa5258b448274838.source: The drawn neighbours that define it.

597b469e923c468e01e7a17d.source: Stable while the group keeps its key or most of its members.

195fe70266ea40b4981f4b05.source: A `landings` group's run: its id and the pivot that ran it.

1df98d227b99e0ff907d1bd6.source: The Communities level it was found at.

a83130d75fd1273c30a54a9a.source: The real nodes it stands for.

b1e153538f8ed33239c9a90f.source: Whether its members are back on the canvas.

7799a3ba518648703ceb17fb.source: The id of the rule that made it: `'neighbours'`, `'chains'`, `'degree'`, `'kcore'`, `'communities'`, `'landings'`, `'manual'`, or a custom rule's own id.

580d8da0c50eb75a725e4d0a.source: A hand-made group's title, shown in place of its type breakdown.

934469e5a564cfb696567975.source: How many members of each type; the key is `''` for nodes with no type.

3fdb38e0a674f4e1357a4bcc.source:
Fold everything outside the k-core into it: nodes with fewer than `k` links are peeled
off again and again, so whole trees hanging off the core fold, not only their leaves.
A group may mix types and may hold a single node.

2a8557e474bd57a260ab53ca.source: The links a node needs, among the nodes still standing, to stay. Between 1 and 10.

e8e23550a4346f45d1b220ec.source:
Fold what a pivot brought in: the nodes an ingest added, one group per type, when that
ingest was asked to land in a group (`graph.simplify.groupLanding`). A member stays
whatever links it gains. Added at the top of the rules, on, the first time a landing is
grouped; declare it to place it elsewhere or preset its smallest group.

9533ed1365821092127dc4be.source: Fewer nodes of one type than this land as plain nodes. Between 2 and 50.

b31fc6f0ab2b3319dd864693.source: A group made by hand: what `getManualGroups` returns and `setManualGroups` takes.

268d2a49f5e19c5ba2d1aa09.source: Also the id of the group drawn for it.

26b7cc6839f70992cd63007c.source: Every member, including ones deleted or filtered out since; only those present are drawn.

1a5e76088dcb5f8ae27f516f.source: Shown in place of the type breakdown. Unset, the group is labelled by its types.

50810e8a5dd7f9bcbabbdb6a.source:
The groups made by hand from a selection (`graph.simplify.groupNodes`). Runs before every
other rule, so a node picked into one leaves any other group. Added at the top of the
rules, on, the first time a group is made; declare it to switch it off by default.

7779f743c323ef10ae222d1d.source:
Fold nodes of one type that link to exactly the same nodes, the same way round.
The leaves of a hub are the simplest case: they all have the hub as their only neighbour.

07b76ad59e34d3164f602827.source: `UI.simplify`: which rules fold the graph, and how groups are named.

93dff09600afade0aef7165c.source:
The colour a node stands for in a group: the disc and ring, the open wash, the
tooltip's chips, a mixed ring's share. For hosts whose nodes carry no `color`.
Returning `undefined` falls back to the node's resolved style colour.

586ca9db4fedf06aa997acf5.source: `false` removes the feature: no rules run and the Simplify rail mode is gone.

026c5e2d76161885d947453d.source: Opening a group with more members than this asks first.

c347c241b9b4ce1583342e92.source:
The rules, in the order they run; each one sees the groups the ones above it made.
Left out, `full` mode offers the built-in rules switched off, and the other modes
run none.

b933aedcaf29f347515aa09b.source:
The name of a group's part, e.g. ``(type, count) => `${count} IPs` ``. `type` is
`undefined` for nodes with no type.

c61991de0e95f7a9bbd8ad4c.source:
The type every rule groups by and every group counts its parts by. A rule's own
`typeOf` still wins for that rule.

84311efef7551492827740ea.source: A rule's one whole-number setting: smallest group, fewest links, core strength or level.

109ac9bf3d16d844f8370bb0.source: A stepper, or a slider applied on release.

bb5bed62c3600c90ad368123.source: Which setting it is, whatever its label says: the smallest group, a threshold, or the Communities level.

3b626e9c4379c04eb73267a6.source: Its name on the rule's card.

1f99052762617e26d798ced9.source: Where a rule stands, for the Simplify flyout.

6e5cfe73371257a18b350b92.source: Still finding its groups; the previous ones stay on the canvas meanwhile.

fe847b64c668707351375b55.source: Declared by the app rather than shipped with the library.

39f618986573c8eeb54e0b1c.source: The rule threw on its last run and was switched off.

c0a70135f571cb3212b1ee6c.source: Groups this rule made in the last run.

954e082d12fe2ea765f2c16f.source: Set for a rule with a smallest-group setting.

093911cf3d254745e42bbe61.source: The rule's whole-number setting, what its stepper shows.

b5ecddf3221fea07ae5eb4ae.source: These may be scalled based on the amount of node and canvas size

d8741377a683d1b7c960eb41.source:
How long a simulation run is given before it is stopped, in milliseconds. Spent as
ticks so it holds below 60fps; the `settleTime` knob sets this and `d3AlphaDecay`
together.

f3d86a8c2f186a60aaf2346b.source:
Fallback collision radius, in px, used only for nodes that report no circle
radius. Nodes with a radius use [d3CollideRadiusMultiplier](#d3collideradiusmultiplier) × their radius.

239dfb3cbac9b6dd3f10138a.source:
Multiplier applied to each node's circle radius to derive its collision radius
(the spacing the sim keeps between nodes). Higher spreads nodes further apart.
This is what the "collision radius" physics knob scales via
[Simulation.setCollisionRadius](../../../../interfaces/Simulation.md#setcollisionradius).

a9cb052cfe93edd990012d2e.source:
Centring pull toward the canvas centre, applied only to isolated (degree-0)
nodes so they don't fly off; connected nodes use [d3GravityStrengthConnected](#d3gravitystrengthconnected).

81000028686ccf05bb5b2ac6.source:
Centring pull for connected nodes. Kept low by default so link + charge forces
find their own equilibrium; raise it to stop a sparsely-linked graph from
drifting apart.

3ea6efbcf2dfc9ef456634fb.source:
Automatically fit the graph to the viewport after a cluster is expanded or collapsed,
or a group from `graph.simplify` is opened or closed.

08421afa8753ab4a95b2d707.source:
`'auto'` — the layout re-tunes itself from what is on screen (node count,
node sizes, canvas size) and keeps doing so as the graph changes.

dae6213ad85d855e21de5eae.source: `'manual'` — the knobs stay exactly where they were configured.

5d2a659698133c41115b8b67.source:
Left unset, `'auto'` is used *unless* the graph configures a physics option
auto drives ([d3LinkDistance](#d3linkdistance), [d3ManyBodyStrength](#d3manybodystrength),
[d3CollideRadiusMultiplier](#d3collideradiusmultiplier), [d3VelocityDecay](#d3velocitydecay),
[d3GravityStrength](#d3gravitystrength), [d3GravityStrengthConnected](#d3gravitystrengthconnected),
[d3AlphaDecay](#d3alphadecay), [cooldownTime](#cooldowntime)) — so tuning any of them is enough
to keep it, and no existing configuration is taken over. Setting
`physics: 'auto'` *and* d3 options is legal: the explicit values seed the
opening frame and auto takes over from there.

79e3fd6e6f90b620e3c7bef8.source:
Turning any knob by hand (a flyout slider, a `set*` call, a preset) also
leaves auto.

310c74941a08deeab841082d.source: 'auto' when no physics option is configured, `'manual'` otherwise

25b364ae1c85bc712b62e4e5.source:
Ticks the opening layout runs before the first frame. `0` runs none, so nodes that
carry their own `x`/`y` open where they were given.

086e07a8827ad0698a32bb70.source: Pivotick is a hackable TypeScript graph visualization library built on top of [D3 force simulations](https://d3js.org/d3-force/simulation). It renders directed or undirected graphs with interactive controls, force simulation, tree layout support, and optional UI elements such as a sidebar, a data table, context menus and tooltips.

eb694cf3d8adaad349bc6bf6.source: It also does the thing it is named for: a **pivot** fetches more graph from wherever your data lives, stages the results as candidates you triage rather than dropping them on the canvas, and can write back what you keep — with an undo history over everything the canvas holds.

5957aee7fba9a2df786ebff5.source: Pivots — run an enrichment against what is on the canvas, triage the results in a dock pane, and ingest only what you keep

56b0486bb1e74b68d6c507ae.source: Saving a pivot's results back to the system they came from, with a ledger of what has crossed and what has not

eeaa9b69a869ec6b42418b3e.source: Undo and redo over what the canvas holds — ingests, deletions, hides and hand-drawn elements — as one timeline

2c271c2f484e8c530f02e658.source: Provenance: every node and edge knows which sources vouch for it, and one source's contribution can be dropped

63a15a03e8162cd3f98f413a.source: Force-based simulation with optional worker support

27891eb93599107096ec0327.source: Tree/hierarchy layout support, with the hierarchy inferred or declared by the data

c1dcd73a3298b9a680ce6a68.source: Self-tuning force layout, or hand-tuned from the Physics flyout

025a32af7b3256030feedb77.source: A data table docked under the canvas, sharing one selection with the canvas and the sidebar

923678cea8f427bedae011af.source: Minimap, a multi-key filtering legend and a declarative filter panel

e32c119ef8fe0b8406e9768a.source: Edge layers — edges keyed by kind, styled per kind and switched on and off without moving the graph

67e278778bd4c43db40073c9.source: Configurable node/edge styles, labels, rim badges, and callbacks

2efe5d10ac33905f41e92df1.source: Interactive editing — node editing and edge creation (drag or click) with validation and enrichment hooks

a394f2b350287f1d73578027.source: Extensible plugin API for adding custom UI, including your own mode on the left rail

8a48155b048d43b755848489.source: Run `npm run build` and `npm run lint`

dba20b31d1e8ec2092b57a52.source: Open a pull request with a concise summary of behavior and API changes

fd522bbcf8cddb117ff48a90.source:
Built-in rail modes that open a settings flyout instead of deciding what a drag does:
`'view'` (grid + canvas behaviour), `'physics'` (layout + simulation) and `'simplify'`
(the rules that fold nodes into groups).

5ee29957d1ce82d46087e8fb.source: Which canvas corner the minimap docks in.

198e03ba8963ebc60db1cff8.source: Note surface finish: a deep full-colour card, or a neutral terminal panel.

7d32aed6ee8a1d6411517170.source: Named physics presets — a fixed character to pick, as opposed to letting `Auto` decide.

7bba7dd4e49db3e27986d2af.source:
The two built-in pointer-modes of the control layout. Basic click-select, pan and
zoom work in *every* mode; a pointer-mode only decides what a plain drag / the
contextual tool panel does (rubber-band select vs. the armed create tool).

d04d2beaab03790eab35c554.source:
Every mode the rail can be in: the four built-ins — `'select'`, `'create'`, `'view'`
and `'physics'` — plus the id of any mode registered through `addRailMode`. Modes are
**mutually exclusive**: opening a flyout deactivates the active pointer-mode (and
vice-versa), and only one flyout is open at a time.

0f2dc0903b2104fdac50d307.source:
A plain `string`, since a registered id is arbitrary. Adding `| (string & {})` would
keep editor autocomplete for the four names above, but TypeDoc renders it as
`string & object`.

56d99859004149fa841f4bc6.source: Whether a mode owns the tool panel or a settings flyout.

631b9cc7558e4bec5232ff1f.source: What the `Visibility` column reports, and why.

623d36a533b7e9be288a0f53.source:
`filtered` and `excluded` are a node's two reasons; an edge reads `filtered` when its
own layer is switched off, and `endpoint` when an end of it is not on the canvas —
filtered out, or inside a collapsed cluster. An edge cannot be `excluded`: there is no
hide-this-edge action.

3d2626e1202a213493133551.source:
`nested` is the fourth answer for a node, and only reachable with
[GraphUI.TableOptions.nested](../pivotick/namespaces/GraphUI/interfaces/TableOptions.md#nested) on: it is inside a cluster the canvas has shut, so nothing
filtered it and nothing on screen is it. Distinct from `filtered` because the action
that brings it back is opening a cluster, not clearing a filter.

c38133807e7c61de7bc9c425.source:
`grouped` is a node folded into a group by `graph.simplify`: it passes the filters and is
on the canvas as part of its group. An edge reads `grouped` when its line is drawn to one.

b28a14c829c56235bf990be6.source:
The lifecycle phases every UI element participates in, in order. `mount`
is handled separately (it needs a container / slot); these three are the
argument-less phases the `UIManager` broadcasts.

867e64be0a22793a76593ec4.source: Complete catalogues shipped with Pivotick. Chinese uses Simplified characters.

d63b65ada8cb209357007158.source:
The library's English text, by key. A translation is a copy of this object with the
values replaced, passed as `i18n.messages`.

5c85ddafad86241026d7ce69.source: Inclusive `[min, max]` slider range for each [PhysicsKnobs](../interfaces/PhysicsKnobs.md) value.

bb09f09c458c057eed978027.source:
Knob bundles applied by [Simulation.applyPhysicsPreset](../interfaces/Simulation.md#applyphysicspreset). `tight`'s friction is
lighter than its name suggests on purpose: contracting a graph has to push past
`forceCollide`, which never scales with alpha, so heavier damping just stalls the run
short of the preset's own equilibrium.

8f2d3bb2921d99f9fbcebd41.source:
The library's graph-aware columns — the ones no generic grid could compute, because
they are about an element's place in the graph rather than its data.

f008770feab6cab165f8183c.source: Compose them into `UI.table.columns`, cloning to adjust:

d6d78ac6343db7bc28a6152b.source:
`label` and the edge `source` / `target` columns are resolved against the graph when the
dock builds them, so they read the same names the rest of the UI shows. Give a column
your own `accessor` to take that over. Their headings are written in the graph's
language (`GraphOptions.i18n`) unless you give one a `label` of your own.

dcb788cc18b1070ae39e7064.source: How many nodes a cluster holds directly — `0` for a leaf.

d9bfd4ff8eae3a6d146d0445.source:
Nothing else in the UI says how big a cluster is: not the label, not the tooltip,
not the sidebar. Without this the only way to find out is to expand it, which is
the exact "read the value instead of hunting for it" the dock exists for.

3808f564a5bb0e3e23a2ad47.source:
Direct children, not the whole subtree, so it matches the structure a nested
cluster's own row then reports one level down.

f7541b594cdc836eb7b765fa.source:
The clusters a nested node sits inside, outermost first — empty for a node of the
root graph. The `flat` nested mode's answer to "where is this row from", since flat
rows carry no structure of their own.

5b5d1e45c42e205337ca5908.source: The group `graph.simplify` put a node in, by its label; empty for a node in none.

3b6576393c8428815bfe6815.source: The element's display name, as the rest of the UI resolves it.

f11f7c1a60fe667b90957ab7.source: Whether the node is pinned in place.

6ec9171f2c05ce92bae6640b.source: An edge's origin, by display name.

c87c9c38d0eb66d35400e8fe.source: An edge's destination, by display name.

44063e9daa68070a2f85e923.source:
Whether the element is on the canvas, and if not, why — for a node, `filtered` by
the filter panel or `excluded` by hand; for an edge, `filtered` when its layer is
off or `endpoint` when an end of it has left. The dock lists hidden elements rather
than hiding them, so this is how you tell them apart.

71ce8f702e9165a962a60785.source:
Narrow and fixed-width: it leads the derived column set as a status gutter, so it
should not eat the room the name needs.

c4da2ff638076e4624b474d4.source: Inclusive `[min, max]` slider range for both [TreeSpacing](../interfaces/TreeSpacing.md) multipliers.

57a6e1ae540ad26f8a370e17.source:
The ceiling stops at 10 rather than following what the largest trees ask for, because
past it the extra room buys nothing readable: the view is fitted, so a tree 20× wider
than the canvas draws its nodes at a twentieth of their size. Beyond this a graph is
explored by panning, and the slider sitting at its maximum says so.

317cac638adc9015bae1d2ce.source: Pivotick allows you to customize how nodes, edges, and labels are rendered through the `render` option.

d8926794fea14bae7a0c6770.source: All styles defined here apply only when `render.type` is set to `svg`.

0c0c256adeb2ea4ae22c1a2c.source: **`defaultNodeStyle.html`** (per node or per type) is the same escape hatch inside the styling chain — see [HTML nodes](#html-nodes).

47f525ac1f3b65a195b0868c.source:
**`edgeTypeAccessor`** + **`edgeStyleMap`** are the edge counterparts, and they double as
the key a relation layer is switched off by — see [Edge layers](/edge-layers).

198bc3fe0c587bbb006fceab.source:
Pivotick measures what you return to size its `<foreignObject>` and to feed the force
layout's collision radius. The card is measured inside a shrink-to-fit box of the
library's own, so you do **not** have to make your root self-sizing: `width: 100%` on it
resolves against its own content rather than against the placeholder.

8719f52753ad421e59bf6db3.source:
When no combination of `shape`, `color`, `icon` and `text` will do, hand the renderer some
markup. There are two ways in, and the difference is only *where they are declared*:

cac15ae88c89c126f9262fc8.source:
`html` is the one to reach for first: it is an ordinary style channel, so it resolves
through the same precedence chain as `color` or `shape`, and a card can be given to one
kind of node while the rest keep their shapes.

15f8b9c4a1c5543f57e61cb5.source:
Without it, the shape is **still drawn behind your card**, and `size` is the smallest the
node is allowed to be — which is what you want for a card sitting on a coloured disc, and
not what you want for a card that is the node. `shape: 'none'` draws no shape, and hands
the node's collision radius and edge anchors to the card instead.

0895affc4121d53405765a51.source:
It is a shape value like any other, so it composes: a label-only node is
`shape: 'none'` with a `text` and no card, and an icon-only node is `shape: 'none'` with
an `iconClass`. A shapeless node with no content at all is invisible — but still there,
still draggable, and still selectable over `2 × size`.

e308a987cb5a1e1c06499e1a.source:
`text` is a separate channel, so a card and a node label are drawn together. If your card
carries its own title, set `text: ''` — an inherited value cannot be cleared with
`undefined`, which falls through to whatever the style map said.

c35d3ce0290efa82dfdb669f.source:
Your card is measured and the node grows to it, so it is never clipped, the collision
force spaces the real cards, and edges land on the card's border rather than on a circle
around it. You do not have to do anything to make that work — returning a `width: 100%`
root is fine, because the measurement happens inside a shrink-to-fit box.

932a855b1a260c38729cc3e5.source:
The measurement is **asynchronous** (a card cannot be measured before it is on screen),
so a node's radius is its styled `size` for the first frame or two and then becomes the
card's. The layout is nudged once when that lands.

bc99ca9d58f72e740e8067d5.source:
A card is measured **once, at render**. If its content later changes size on its own,
re-render the node to re-measure it.

bcad00d3759d6847fc0ff7ea.source:
Both callbacks may return **nothing** for a node, which hands that node back to the
styling chain — shape, style-map entry, icons and label as usual. So a single global
`renderNode` can card the nodes that deserve one:

1fca1ff1e02103bcc2b7716c.source:
Whatever you return is inserted as-is. Build it with `textContent`, or escape it — do not
interpolate node data into a markup string. See the [security guide](/security).

1e689b39b975552ae1998fd5.source:
A node label longer than the room it has is shortened with a middle ellipsis
(`Supe…abel`). Set `textTruncate: false` to draw it in full instead — as a default,
per node type, or per node:

b1739a7ebf22158c9a72fb78.source:
Between the two, `textMaxWidth` caps the label at a width you choose, in graph units
(CSS pixels at zoom 1), instead of the room the node gives it. A label that fits is drawn
in full, and a longer one is shortened with a middle ellipsis to that width:

6214a159658c02035fb1d8db.source:
A node label is drawn at `max(12, size × 0.45)` by default, so it grows with the node.
When a node is big for what it draws rather than for how much it matters, such as an image
thumbnail, set `textFontSize` (graph units) to keep its label in line with its neighbours:

478f0a46c69847a22f929fa2.source:
The label still sits just clear of the node, the built-in budget still takes its width from
the node (so a smaller font fits more characters), and the
[zoom gate](#label-zoom) judges it by the size you set.

d7f48a2285aaa7ba4128025e.source:
The cap scales with the zoom like the rest of the node, and it can be a function of the
node. It is ignored when `textTruncate` is `false`.

1bd47277d178f4f07fca711c.source:
A full or capped label usually spills past the node's shape, so it is drawn on the same
themed pill as a floated label to stay readable over the canvas. Pair it with
`textVerticalShift: 1` (or `textHorizontalShift`) to move the whole label clear
of the node. Edge labels are never truncated.

d17ad4b2cc34760c90bd8385.source:
`text` is a label on a node, not a substitute for one. A node that *is* its text should be
drawn as the node, through [`html`](#html-nodes), `renderNode` or a
[tier](#node-tiers) — those are the node's drawing, and the zoom keeps them whatever
[`minLabelFontSize`](#label-zoom) does to labels.

5fac618ee979510a9282ebce.source:
By the time a graph is useful, `color`, `shape`, `size` and `iconClass` are usually
all carrying something. `badges` is a channel of its own — small indicators pinned
to the node's rim, spending none of the others:

a843448228ab04b3fa986078.source:
Give a badge `text` (a count, or a character or two), an `iconClass`,
`iconUnicode` or `svgIcon`, and a `title` for its native tooltip. `text` wins if
you supply both. Longer text grows the badge into a pill, and past three
characters it renders `99+`.

e96c744dae650aba46201f18.source:
Omit `position` and badges fill the free corners clockwise from `'ne'`. Name one
(`'ne' | 'nw' | 'se' | 'sw'`) and it is honoured verbatim, overlaps included.

db8ec1c9eb79e48e9efa3334.source:
**Four fit on a plain node, two on one with children.** The expand/collapse
control sits north-east when a node is collapsed and south-east when it is
expanded, so on any expandable node *both* East corners are reserved — otherwise
every badge would change corner the moment a cluster opened. Badges beyond what
fits fold into a `+n` whose tooltip names them.

5634c304b515f29b8c5b7e99.source:
Badges scale with the node between a floor and a ceiling, so they stay legible on
a tiny node without swelling on a large one, and they sit on the shape's real
rim — the corner of a square or a framed picture, the 45° point of a circle.

c9bf6397a86f43b08ed23505.source:
A badge is hit-testable but transparent by default: with no handler its click
falls through and selects the node underneath, so a badge is never a dead spot.

e205fd3e400486afa4ff45f8.source:
Give a badge an `onClick` — or declare `callbacks.onBadgeClick` for behaviour they
all share — and it takes the pointer cursor and consumes its click, leaving the
node unselected. Both fire, the badge's own first. Pressing a badge still drags
the node either way, and a `badgeClick` listener on the interaction bus can
`cancel()` both.

282a9098ca1ff8a13730e6fd.source:
Badges describe **only the node they sit on**. A collapsed cluster does not
aggregate its children's — walk `node.children` in your own `badges` function if
that is what you want, since only you know whether a fact sums, wins, or neither.

c3516ab94e563e9118e6802f.source:
A drawing that reads well close up is unreadable on an overview, and a dot that fits an
overview cannot say what it is. `tiers` lets one node carry several drawings and picks
between them from how large the node currently renders.

8cfb0352cc4be589c3a86983.source:
Tiers are ordered smallest first and the richest one that fits wins. When none does, the
node draws at its base style, so the style you already have is the floor: a graph that
declares no `tiers` is unaffected in every respect.

faab1985cbbbb4433f6e47ca.source:
A tier merges over the base style, so a channel it does not name is inherited. The drawing
is the exception: `iconUnicode`, `iconClass`, `svgIcon`, `imagePath` and `html` are one slot,
so a tier that names any of them replaces the base's drawing (and its `imageFit`) outright.
A glyph at rest with a card tier needs nothing more than the card:

b40a296bebed29eba9924bc6.source: A tier that names no drawing, only `size`, `color` or `text` say, keeps the base's glyph.

1507d79d086e95698b46477f.source:
To take away a channel the tier does not otherwise replace, set it to `null`, which means
the tier draws that one **not at all**. `strokeColor: null` drops the base's outline, for
instance. `undefined` cannot stand in: it means "I am not naming this channel", which is
exactly how the base's value survives.

b44432214b374f1290bf1a2b.source:
This is the only layer where `null` works that way. Everywhere else in the style chain `null`
still falls through to the layer below, because a `styleCb` handing back a null straight out
of node data is an ordinary shape and has always meant "use the default".

2169955f01bd76266c7451eb.source: To make a node shapeless, use `shape: 'none'` rather than clearing `shape`.

0d4650479030c7bec3d15f2f.source:
The **rendered size**: the node's footprint in CSS pixels, which is `footprint × zoom`. A
tier engages once that reaches its `minRenderedSize`, which defaults to the tier's own
`width`, so `{ width: 140 }` reads as "engage once there is room to draw 140 pixels of
node".

fae4ddaad937ac08270a61bc.source:
The zoom scale on its own would not do. It multiplies coordinates the layout invented, so
the same scale means a different apparent size on a different graph, and a threshold tuned
on one dataset would be wrong on the next.

6c3283ac0d06fd16e96a9fe7.source:
A tier that has engaged holds until the rendered size falls to 85% of its threshold. Every
node shares a threshold, so without that band a canvas parked on one would flicker as a
whole.

f274d340e20b4353a97c30fe.source:
The box a node reserves in the layout does not change when its drawing does. It is
`layoutSize`, and it defaults to half the widest declared tier, so declaring tiers gives
the graph the right spacing without a second number. Nothing moves when a tier swaps: the
drawing changes inside a box that was already the right size, and the forces never see the
difference.

34e2f0572aca9968c3ad432d.source:
`width` and `height` are declared rather than measured, for the same reason. The layout has
to know the footprint before the first tick, and a measured card only reports its size once
it has been drawn.

4957ba2134af352bb222f027.source:
Set `layoutSize` yourself to space the graph tighter or wider than the widest tier. Note
that a tier is drawn at its design size only when its width equals the footprint; a
narrower one engages proportionally earlier and is drawn proportionally smaller. Give it an
explicit `minRenderedSize` if that matters.

7b094473c0c7b8182219d4b2.source:
`focusTier` is the drawing a node uses while it is hovered, or selected on its own,
whatever the zoom. This is where a node says everything about itself, so reading one never
means zooming to it.

9db3f396a09937af8189aac8.source:
It merges over the node's **base** style rather than over the active tier, so a chip tier's
`shape` or `html` cannot leak into it. It holds a constant size on screen: the drawing is
counter-scaled against the zoom, so a 280×150 card is 280×150 CSS pixels however far out
the graph is. And it never touches the node's geometry, so edges keep landing on the tier
underneath and hovering moves nothing.

b3a7858e7ecedf4d402545e6.source:
The focus drawing wears the node's [badges](#node-badges) on its own rim, at the same
on-screen size as the card. The node's own badges are hidden while it shows, so none is drawn
twice. Give `focusTier` a `badges` of its own to show a different set on the card.

3909cbc0146d137c284a7863.source:
Only a node selected **on its own** is promoted. A fifty-node box selection would be a wall
of overlapping cards.

26c4077d780bd6062aa73f38.source:
`render.focusTierTrigger` says when it fires: `'both'` (the default), `'hover'`,
`'selection'`, or `'off'`. Reach for `'off'` when you are embedding a style preset someone
else ships and want its focus drawing suppressed without editing it.

11967e3d044763a4e462e899.source: When a tier already shows it

3ba52f151e0d231e5386afcd.source:
Sometimes the focus drawing is the same as one of the zoom tiers: a glyph at rest that
hovers into a chip, with the chip also drawn once the graph is zoomed in far enough. There,
hovering would paint a second, smaller chip over the one already on screen.
`focusTierYieldsAt` names the index into `tiers` from which the focus drawing stops firing:

55831ecf6d3fefe1c10ecbe9.source:
While the node is drawn at that tier or a richer one, hover and a lone selection leave it as
it is. It follows the active tier, not the zoom level, so it uses the same thresholds as the
swap. Zooming in with the card open fades it out as the tier fades in, and zooming back out
brings it back without moving the pointer. Leave it unset on a node whose focus drawing says
more than any tier, and a node with no `tiers` ignores it.

4a7d54775f2df08d560021c9.source:
A focus card does not replace the tooltip. The two are independent, and a tooltip may
carry something the card does not.

e66b4a8f8469f6b52090a9e8.source:
A node cross-fades from one drawing to the next rather than cutting to it. The outgoing
drawing is held on a layer of its own and the two fade past each other, so a node is never
absent mid-swap, only briefly softer where they overlap.

12c357bb8fb159fc443b2d07.source:
`render.detailTransition` is how long that takes, in milliseconds. It defaults to `160` and
covers every drawing the zoom decides: a tier crossing, the focus drawing, and a label
crossing [`minLabelFontSize`](#label-zoom). Set it to `0` to replace the drawing in a single
frame:

b10db7f48d293aa5159c2547.source:
Every node on screen crosses at the same moment, so a crossing starts as many fades as
there are nodes changing. Measured on 210 nodes each holding a 140×44 card, the fade runs
at 60fps for its whole length; what it costs is about 26ms on the single frame the crossing
already spends, and that figure does not grow with the duration. Turn it off on a graph
where that frame matters more than the transition.

15c17623a8c257c0a1d921c4.source: `prefers-reduced-motion` turns it off on its own, whatever the option says.

e4670f827510570de4d1dc1c.source:
A label rides the graph and scales with it, so the further out the view is the smaller it is
